    "171fb2185a25edcf71d8281f0eb4d3c2626eccc7": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-09T13:56:58Z",
      "body": "Work package 4 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi. An\nopencode-go/<model> id names the endpoint; it now starts the pinned Pi in the\nTerminal window, with discovery off and one policy extension loaded from a copy\nin the session's private directory, the declared model, and the prompt after\n`--`. The runner checks the pin with require_pi, confirms by `pi --help` in a\nscratch home that the extension's flag is listed, and refuses otherwise,\nremoving what it made. It hands over no key and sets no agent directory: Pi\nsigns in from the maintainer's own ~/.pi/agent (Q-6). A prompt that starts with\n@ is refused, because Pi would read it as a file name.\n\nThe seven OpenCode-only functions, AGENT and GUARDED are gone. The tests get a\npi stand-in beside codex and osascript, and an opencode stand-in that must\nnever be called; the 25 canned effective-policy answers are replaced by tests of\nthe version pin, the read-back, the @ prompt, the scratch home and the absence\nof a key. 19 planted faults in the runner all turn a test red.\n\nDocuments that describe the verb to a reader still say OpenCode until package 5.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",

    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",
      "subject": "feat(adr): the gate adr-answers and the command decide adr",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "decisions/gates.yaml",
        "provenance.yaml"
      ]
    },

      "author_utc": "2026-10-13T07:19:18Z",
      "body": "A change claims its ADR files under adr_files in its spec header; the\ninterview-minimums gate checks the claim in both directions and reads the\nrepository's adoption day from decisions/adoption.yaml through\nscripts/adoption.py.     "d225f50d1ef4364395547863788297ef0959eaf3": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-09T13:12:52Z",
      "body": "Work package 3 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi. Pi asks\nfor no approval and has no sandbox, so the runner has to supply the policy: a\nplain ESM extension, scripts/stage2_session_policy.mjs, that the runner will\ncopy into the session's private directory and load explicitly.\n\nIt keeps read, grep, find, ls, edit and write inside the worktree as Pi\nresolves a path (a leading @, ~, file://, symlinks), keeps edit and write off\nits own file, .stage2-sessions/ and .pi/, asks before a dangerous bash command\nand blocks it when no UI can ask, blocks when its own handler fails, and\nregisters a flag that `pi --help` lists, which is how the runner will confirm\nthe load. 200 cases run it through a node driver without Pi and without a\nmodel; 25 planted faults, one rule removed each, all turn a test red. The\nfirst run caught `git -C . push` running unasked; the patterns now allow\nglobal git options before the verb.\n\nThe runner does not use the extension yet (package 4); nothing in\nscripts/stage2_session.py changes.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "d225f50d1ef4364395547863788297ef0959eaf3",
      "subject": "feat(stage2-session): add the policy extension of a Pi session and its tests",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/stage2_session_policy.mjs",
        "tests/test_stage2_session_policy.py"
      ]
    },

      "body": "In an interview on 2026-10-09 the maintainer decided what the first draft of\nthe policy extension had added beyond Pi's example: network programs do not\nask (Q-7), and of the git commands only `git reset --hard` and `git clean`\nask, `git push` does not (Q-8). Both differ from the recommendation.\n\nThe extension drops the network-client and git-push patterns. The tests move\nthose commands to the list that runs unasked, so the decision is pinned, and\nkeep `git -C . reset --hard` and the like on the asking list. 26 planted\nfaults, one rule removed each (including the two dropped patterns put back),\nall turn a test red. The plan's package 3 section is rewritten to match.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2).       ],
      "statement": "There is exactly one dispatch point for a writable work call. `run_attempts` sends every route whose endpoint tuple equals `CODEX` to `run_codex(... writable=True)` and every other tuple to `run_work_model(ctx, prompt, endpoint, writable=True, key=credential)`. The route lists that `implement` and `repair` hand to it contain only `claude-code-plan`/`glm-coding-plan` tuples (plus `CODEX` for repair), so an added `(\"opencode-go\", <model>, ...)` tuple would reach `run_work_model`, which builds a `claude -p` argv with `--model <endpoint[1]>` and `--tools Read,Grep,Glob,Edit,Write`. `run_work_model` reads `WORK_WRITE_TOOLS` and `glm_env` only; it knows nothing of Pi, the Go address record or terms."
    },

          "excerpt": "def run_reviewer(\n    ctx: Context,\n    model: str,\n    prompt: str,\n    key: str,\n    *,\n    free: bool = False,\n    timeout_seconds: int | None = None,\n    task: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One reviewer call through Pi with this run's refreshed OpenCode Go definitions.\n\n    The launch is the measured set (spec, criterion 8), started through the\n    repository wrapper (ADR 0019): the rung's id under the `opencode-go`\n    provider, thinking `max` (Pi clamps it per model), the read-only tools,\n    every discovery switched off, no session, retries off. Each call gets its\n    own scratch directory: a `HOME`, an agent directory whose settings set retries and turn compaction off\n    and the run's refreshed provider definitions, and the prompt file. The key reaches Pi as\n    `OPENCODE_API_KEY` only. Returns the scrubbed answer. A call that has not\n    ended after `REVIEWER_MINUTES` is stopped (criterion 15).\n\n    A free call (`free=True`, ADR 0021 decision 3) gets `--no-tools` instead of\n    the read tools and starts in its scratch directory, not the worktree: its\n    only input is the prompt it is given.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        scratch = Path(tmp)\n        agent = scratch / \"agent\"\n        agent.mkdir()\n        (agent / \"settings.json\").write_text(json.dumps(PI_AGENT_SETTINGS), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        # The launch resolves and assesses its model offline, against the one\n        # address record read fresh from the held declaration. Without the\n        # run's refreshed definitions there is no checked destination, and no\n        # unchecked launch stands in for one (criterion 2).\n        try:\n            policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(ctx.root)\n        except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n        store = getattr(ctx, \"models_store\", None)\n        if store is None:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"no refreshed provider definitions accompany the reviewer call for {model}; \"\n                \"its destination cannot be assessed and the call does not start.\"\n            )\n        (agent / \"models-store.json\").write_text(json.dumps(store), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        _dropped, notices = activate_overlay(agent, store, policy)\n        retain_address_notices(notices)\n        for notice in notices:\n            print(f\"Address notice: {notice}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        home = scratch / \"home\"\n        home.mkdir()\n        check_overlay(agent, home, model, policy=policy)\n        row = stage2_go.definition_of(store, stage2_go.PROVIDER, model)\n        if row is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"the refreshed definitions of {model} are missing or duplicated; no reviewer starts.\")\n        assessment = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, row)\n        if not assessment.admitted:\n            raise Refused(assessment.problem)\n        prompt_file = scratch / \"review-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            str(PI_WRAPPER),\n            \"--print\",\n            \"--no-session\",\n            \"--no-approve\",\n            \"--no-extensions\",\n            \"--no-mcp\",\n            \"--no-skills\",\n            \"--no-context-files\",\n            \"--no-prompt-templates\",\n            \"--no-themes\",\n            \"--offline\",\n            *([\"--no-tools\"] if free else [\"--tools\", PI_TOOLS]),\n            \"--thinking\",\n            \"max\",\n            \"--model\",\n            f\"{OPENCODE}/{model}\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            task or f\"Review the change {ctx.change} as the appended instructions say.\",\n        ]\n        env = foreign_env({\"HOME\": str(home), \"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": str(agent), \"OPENCODE_API_KEY\": key})\n        # Every key of the secrets file is scrubbed, not the OpenCode key alone: a member with read\n        # tools can quote the GLM key from the same file (DL-B-4 o",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::declaration_problem",
          "end_line": 1859,
          "excerpt": "def declaration_problem(root: Path, endpoint: str, model: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why the declaration does not clear this endpoint and model for framework content, or None.\n\n    For the `opencode-go` endpoint a model is also refused while its data terms\n    are unread or its declaration records a dated skip (ADR 0021, decision 5):\n    no paid or interactive call runs on unread terms. For a subscription\n    endpoint (`SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS`, the Z.ai plan) a model is refused\n    without a dated, sourced record or after its `valid_until` day (bead\n    coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        data = yaml.safe_load((root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) or {}\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError):\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    found = next((e for e in data.get(\"endpunkte\") or [] if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get(\"name\") == endpoint), None)\n    if found is None:\n        return f\"model-endpoints.yaml declares no endpoint {endpoint}\"\n    excluded = excluded_problem(root, model)\n    if excluded:\n        return excluded\n    if model not in (found.get(\"modelle\") or []):\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} does not list the model {model}\"\n    if endpoint == OPENCODE:\n        problem = terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    elif endpoint in SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS:\n        problem = subscription_terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    allowed = found.get(\"darf_sehen\")\n    # A list, not a string: `\"framework\" in \"not-framework\"` would be true (phase 6 of stage2-session, F-4).\n    if not isinstance(allowed, list) or \"framework\" not in allowed:\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} may not see framework content\"\n    residency = found.get(\"residenz\")\n    if not isinstance(residency, str) or not residency.strip() or residency == \"nicht-erklaert\":\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} states no data residency\"\n    return None\n",

          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "declaration_problem",
          "start_line": 1822,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::checked_prompt",
          "end_line": 2023,
          "excerpt": "def checked_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n):\n    \"\"\"Check the admission and exact prompt immediately before one call.\n\n    `admission_problem`, when given, replaces the individual declaration (the\n    free class, ADR 0021 decision 3); the leak check is mandatory either way.\n    A subscription endpoint's expiry notice prints first (bead coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    subscription_terms_warnings(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise AdmissionRefused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(ctx.change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), ctx.root, [(\"prompt\", prompt)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the call does not start.\")\n    # A scan can cross UTC midnight: an earlier admission cannot authorize\n    # dispatch after expiry, including retry and replacement calls.\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return result\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "checked_prompt",
          "start_line": 1990,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {

          "excerpt": "def begin_work_call(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    attempt: int,\n    route: str,\n    destination: Path,\n    reason: str | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Check and record one explore/implement attempt in its phase artefact.\"\"\"\n    result = checked_prompt(ctx, endpoint, prompt)\n    if destination == ctx.findings and not destination.exists():\n        destination.write_text(findings_header(ctx, producer_for(endpoint)), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    why = f\" · reason {reason}\"",

      "statement": "The Go-specific gates a Pi work route would need already exist as separate functions and are endpoint-parametrised, not verb-parametrised: `declaration_problem` applies `terms_problem` for `opencode-go`; `preflight` and `checked_prompt` call it for the first route and every attempt; `begin_work_call` records the audit line and `producer_for` already returns `pi` for an endpoint it does not name. `repair_prompt` branches on `endpoint == CODEX` and otherwise selects `REPAIR_FORMAT_FILE_TOOLS` (\"you cannot run commands\"), so a Pi repair attempt automatically receives the file-tools contract. What has no counterpart in the Claude Code path is `dispatch_go`, which refuses a launch without a caller-supplied checked `destination` and a `configuration` file whose `api`/`baseUrl` match that destination, and which re-reads the address policy and terms immediately before the send."

audit lines, appended once at the end\n        self.records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n        self.entries: dict[str, dict] = {}\n        self.stage_order: list[str] = []\n        self.scratch: dict[str, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory] = {}\n        self.started_at: dict[str, str] = {}\n        self.launch_mono: dict[str, float] = {}  # monotonic launch time, for spent-allowance tracking\n        self.ended_mono: dict[str, float] = {}  # monotonic end time: a call's own execution, not later waiting\n        self.key: str | None = None\n        self.state = None\n        self.store: Store | None = None\n        self.locked = False\n        self.store_failure: str | None = None\n        self.unstored: set[str] = set()\n        self.run_id: str | None = None\n        self.source = None\n        self.not_reused: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n        self.map: dict | None = None\n        self.history: dict | None = None\n        self.sentence: str | None = None\n        self.reports: list[dict] = []\n        self.outcomes: list[dict] = []\n        self.judge: dict | None = None\n        self.judge_packet: dict | None = None\n        self.scores: list | None = None\n        self.security: str | None = None\n        self.stop = threading.Event()\n        self.began = CLOCK()\n        self.limits: stage2_research_limits.Limits | None = None\n        self.locator_schema: dict | None = None\n        self.locator_schema_text: str | None = None\n        self.lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    # -- small helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def scrub(self, text: str) -> str:\n        return self.runner.scrub(text, self.key) if self.key else text\n\n    @property\n    def deadline(self) -> float:\n        if self.limits is None:\n            raise self.runner.Refused(\"the research swarm time limits are not yet loaded; call open first\")\n        return self.began + self.limits.run_seconds\n\n    def read_data(self) -> dict:\n        data = stage2_availability.read_declaration(self.root)\n        if isinstance(data, str):\n            raise self.runner.Refused(data)\n        return data\n\n    def seat_id(self, entry: dict) -> str:\n        return research_seat_id(entry[\"endpoint\"], entry[\"model\"])\n\n    # -- opening ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def open(self) -> None:\n        runner = self.runner\n        try:\n            self.limits = stage2_research_limits.load(self.root)\n        except stage2_research_limits.LimitsError as error:\n            raise runner.Refused(f\"the research swarm time limits are unusable: {error}\") from error\n        self.data = self.read_data()\n        try:\n            self.roles = stage2_availability.research_roles(self.selection, self.data)\n            free = (self.selection.get(\"free\") or {}).get(\"selected\")\n            self.free = list(free) if isinstance(free, list) else []\n            if not isinstance(free, list):\n                raise stage2_swarm.ResearchCatalogError(\"the consumed selection holds no free selection\", 2)\n            stage2_swarm.role_launches(self.data, self.roles, self.free)\n            stage2_swarm.research_slot_plan(self.roles, self.free)\n        except (KeyError, TypeError) as error:\n            raise runner.Refused(\"the consumed selection does not hold the six seats\") from error\n        except stage2_swarm.ResearchCatalogError as error:\n            raise runner.Refused(str(error)) from error\n        self.given = stage2_availability.given_neighbours(self.root, self.change, runner)\n        author = self.roles[\"topic_author\"]\n      ",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0011-stage-2-reviews-through-opencode-go.md::## Decision",
          "end_line": 154,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **Framework content may also go to `opencode-go`** — at\n   `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, through Pi\n   (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, at the version the runner pins), with\n   the three ids below. Of the stage-2 phases, the review loop (4b) only,\n   with the runner's `probe` that measures its rungs. The\n   sentence of ADR 0007 decision 2 that closes with \"Nothing else goes, and\n   nowhere else\" now closes with Codex, Z.ai's GLM and OpenCode Go; nothing\n   else goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to none of the\n   three. The interactive `session` verb reaches a declared endpoint under\n   its own amendment (bead coding-harness-amp); this declaration is what that\n   verb waits for before it opens its OpenCode path to the three ids.\n2. **The loop's reviewer role moves.** The loop leaves GLM for the ladder;\n   the spec review and the review stay with Codex exactly as ADR 0007 set\n   them (the maintainer, 2026-10-08), and phase 6 keeps resuming the\n   phase-2a session. Codex and GLM remain declared endpoints for what still\n   routes to them — explore and implement stay on GLM 5.3 Flash.\n3. **The ladder is data, not code.** Round *n* of the loop calls\n   `modelle[n-1]` of the `opencode-go` entry (the order at this decision;\n   the yaml is the truth and no doctrine text repeats it): round 1\n   `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, round 2 `mimo-v2.6-flash`, round 3\n   `mimo-v2.6-pro`. Rounds 1 and 2 both run, each still held by an undecided\n   row; round 3 starts only when round 2 wrote at least one row whose status\n   begins `taken`. The loop runs at most three rounds. Reordering the list is\n   a one-line pull request that touches `model-endpoints.yaml` and nothing\n   else.\n4. **The unconfined reads accepted for ADR 0007's reviewers extend to the\n   rungs — measured, not assumed.** A round has `read`, `grep`, `find` and\n   `ls` and nothing that writes or runs a command; but `read` reaches files\n   outside the worktree, and Pi has no switch that confines it. A rung can\n   therefore read what the maintainer's user can read — the secrets file and\n   the customer instance's checkout included — and send it to OpenCode Go.\n   What bounds it is the prompt's request to read nothing outside the\n   worktree and the repository's git directory: a request, not a lock. The\n   leak check scans what this repository presents, not what a rung reads.\n   The maintainer accepted this residual risk for reviewers on 2026-09-30;\n   it reaches the three rungs by this record.\n5. **The key stays in the runner.** It is read from the secrets file at call\n   time, reaches the call only in its environment as `OPENCODE_API_KEY`,\n   never appears in an argument or in a file the runner writes, and an\n   OpenCode Go call carries no other endpoint's key.\n6. **Each round is isolated, and Pi is pinned.** Each call gets a fresh,\n   empty Pi configuration directory whose one file switches Pi's own retries\n   off, a scratch home directory, and the switches that keep extensions, MCP\n   servers, skills, context files, prompt templates, themes, project trust,\n   sessions and every network request but the model call off. The isolation\n   was measured on Pi 1.1.0; the runner refuses any other version, and\n   raising the pin means measuring it again. The effort is Pi's `max`, which\n   Pi clamps to each model's ceiling — `max` for DeepSeek, `high` for both\n   MiMo rungs: a known limit, not a failure.\n7. **The address is measured before anything builds on it.** Three calls,\n   one per rung, run through the runner and Pi in phase 4 of the change that\n   carries this record — declaration and leak check in front of each, as one\n   special run whose commits are named in the pull request body. After the\n   probe, the change's own review loop runs on the ladder, at most three\n   rounds. The probe and that loop are the only content leaving before the\n   merge: the maintainer accepted the probe on 2026-10-07 and the loop on\n   2026-10-08. If OpenCode ",

      "statement": "The documented boundaries a Go work route would move are written down already: ADR 0011 decision 1 admits `opencode-go` for \"the review loop (4b) only, with the runner's `probe`\", and its decision 2 keeps explore and implement on GLM 5.3 Flash; ADR 0017 decision 1 has Codex repair with Sonnet 5.5 as the stage-1 fallback and states repair \"never routes to `glm-coding-plan`\"; the WORKFLOW routing table names GLM 5.3 Flash for phase 4 Implement and gpt-6.1-terra for Repair after 4b and 6; and house rule 9 forbids a second route beside the runner's one entry point, so the change must extend the existing path rather than add a parallel launcher."

  "counter_evidence": [
    "The declared fallback's terms reading expires soon: in model-endpoints.yaml as read in this worktree, opencode-go's `deepseek-v4.1-flash` carries `valid_until: \"2026-11-30\"`, and `terms_problem` refuses the model from the following UTC day. The YAML entry sits inside the `endpunkte` list, so `endpunkte.opencode-go.modelle_terms...` is not a citable mapping-key path; this reading rests on my own file read, not on a resolvable citation, and it matches the finder packet marking those same keys unresolved.",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2).           "end_line": 2391,
          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0019-repository-pinned-pi-and-contract-tests.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 87,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Repository-local npm install with real offline contracts\",\nbecause it separates the runner from global updates and makes the original\nisolation measurement repeatable on every proposed version change.\n\n1. `tools/pi/package.json` holds the exact Pi dependency; its npm lock records\n   the dependency graph and integrity values. `tools/pi/install.sh` uses\n   `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. No installed dependencies are committed.\n2. Every runner Pi path, including loop/probe and interactive-session preflight,\n   extension confirmation and dispatch, uses `tools/pi/pi`. The wrapper refuses\n   a missing or mismatched local install and never installs or falls back globally.\n3. `tools/pi/.node-version` holds the exact CI Node version. The wrapper refuses\n   another major locally; minor/patch moves within that major remain eligible\n   for the same contracts. Pi and Node changes are proposed in pull requests.\n4. The suite starts real pinned Pi with synthetic credentials and a loopback\n   model stand-in, locally and in CI. It holds reviewer tool declarations and\n   refusal, suppression of discovered extension/MCP startup and skill/prompt/theme\n   reads, context-file exclusion and scratch-agent separation from ambient auth\n   and command-valued model configuration, extension input/results, the production session\n   policy's foreign-read blocking, model-list table and Go/Zen provider address\n   and key mapping. Missing prerequisites fail rather than skip these contracts.\n5. This replaces the requirement to repeat a manual measurement alone when the\n   pin moves; the manual Pi 1.1.0 findings remain historical evidence. The normal\n   verification gates and real contracts must pass before a version move ships.\n6. Authentication boundaries stay as decided: scratch reviewer configuration\n   and Go key only in `OPENCODE_API_KEY`; interactive sessions sign in from the\n   maintainer's own Pi agent directory. No paid Zen endpoint is enabled here.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "end_line": 3306,
          "excerpt": "def require_pi() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Refuse unless the repository wrapper prints exactly the pinned version (spec, criterion 27).\n\n    The wrapper is the one path to Pi (ADR 0019): it refuses a missing,\n    mismatched or unusable local install before any model request, and this\n    check ties its answer to the manifest pin. Runs before the prompt check,\n    the call line and any call, in a scratch directory with no key: a Pi off\n    the pin sends nothing. The session verb calls it after its argument and\n    handover checks.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        env = foreign_env({\"HOME\": tmp, \"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": tmp})\n        try:\n            done = launch(\n                [str(PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"],\n                Path(tmp),\n                env,\n                timeout=PI_VERSION_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the version check's limit of {PI_VERSION_SECONDS} seconds\",\n            )\n        except CallFailed as error:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"{PI_WRAPPER} could not be checked ({error}); it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\"\n            ) from None\n    said = (done.stdout or \"\").strip()\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        # The wrapper's own refusal names the defect; its last lines travel with this one.\n        tail = \"\\n\".join((done.stderr or \"\").splitlines()[-5:])\n        detail = f\": {tail}\" if tail else \"\"\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"{PI_WRAPPER} --version ended {done.returncode}; it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; \"\n            f\"no call starts{detail}.\"\n        )\n    if said != PI_VERSION:\n        raise Refused(f\"pi {said or 'printed nothing'} is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\")\n",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0007-stage-2-reviews-by-codex-and-glm.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 133,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30.           "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",

          "end_line": 3269,
          "excerpt": "def run_codex(\n    ctx: Context, prompt: str, resume: str | None = None, writable: bool = False, *, verb: str\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"One Codex call, first or resumed, pinned the same way. Returns (answer, thread id).\n\n    A review reads in the CLI's `read-only` sandbox; a draft writes in\n    `workspace-write`, and the runner puts back what lands outside the change\n    folder. No call takes a bypass flag (spec, criterion 1). The reasoning\n    effort is the caller verb's entry of `CODEX_EFFORTS`, passed explicitly on\n    every argv, a resumed call included; that a resumed thread actually runs at\n    that effort inside Codex is not asserted (bead coding-harness-yzk, Q-6).\n    Only the verbs `CODEX_EFFORTS` names (draft, repair, review) may carry a\n    Codex route; any other verb stops with a `KeyError` before the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    _, model, _ = CODEX\n    effort = CODEX_EFFORTS[verb]\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        answer_file = Path(tmp) / \"answer.md\"\n        command = [\"codex\", \"exec\"]\n        if resume:\n            command += [\"resume\", resume]\n        command += [\n            \"--json\",\n            \"-m\",\n            model,\n            \"-c\",\n            f'model_reasoning_effort=\"{effort}\"',\n            \"-c\",\n            f'sandbox_mode=\"{\"workspace-write\" if writable else \"read-only\"}\"',\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"hooks\",\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"memories\",\n            \"-o\",\n            str(answer_file),\n            prompt,\n        ]\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, foreign_env({}))\n        thread = thread_id(done.stdout or \"\")\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\"), answer_file)\n        if thread is None:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, \"no thread.started event\"), answer_file)\n        try:\n            answer = answer_file.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n            raise fail(\"codex\", done, \"no answer file\") from error\n    return answer, thread\n",

The gates of the targeted check and of the\n    # draft's document check run through `sh -c`; their scripted answers come from the scenario's\n    # `sh` key, and a red or inspected launch uses `LocalCommands`.\n    for name in (\"bash\", \"sh\", \"codex\", \"claude\", \"pi\", \"make\", \"pin-pi\"):\n        program = bin_dir / name\n        rendered = STAND_IN.replace(\"@PYTHON@\", sys.executable)\n        rendered = rendered.replace(\"@PI@\", stage2.PI_VERSION)\n        rendered = rendered.replace(atomic_test_log.MARKER, ATOMIC_LOG_SOURCE)\n        program.write_text(rendered, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        program.chmod(0o755)\n    # The runner's one path to Pi is patched to the wrapper stand-in: its records\n    # carry the program path, so a call that bypasses the wrapper cannot hide.\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"PI_WRAPPER\", bin_dir / \"pin-pi\")\n    # These runner unit tests use a stand-in Pi.           "excerpt": "# Phase 4 · Implement\n\n**Model:** GLM 5.3 Flash — a solid worker given a clear plan; through\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py implement <change>` and its leak check\n(`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). When Stage 2 is off or Z.ai is unavailable, rerun as\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py implement <change> --stage2-off [REASON]`; Sonnet\n5.5 at effort `medium` (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) builds and the reason is recorded.\nA leak-check BLOCK stops; it never falls back.\n**Input:** `@plans/changes/<name>/plan.md @plans/changes/<name>/spec.md`\n**Gate:** `make verify` green on the final head before phase 6; each runner\nattempt passes the targeted check or, where that is unsafe, the full one.\n\nYou follow the plan. You read the spec to know what you are building against.\nUnder the Stage-2 runner an implement attempt has\nfile tools but no command tool (a Codex repair attempt may run tests and\n`make verify`, never commit): write no entry under `## Time used`, because the\nrunner measures each completed attempt itself and writes a line marked\n\"measured by the runner\" (a rejected attempt gets one too); the runner\nruns the targeted check after an implement or a repair attempt (the whole\ntouched and import-linked test files and the gates the touched kinds of file\nfeed; the full `make verify` when the attempt touches shared infrastructure, would run `tests/test_stage2.py` whole, or meets another fallback of the runner's targeted selection (`targeted_selection` in `scripts/stage2.py`: for example a `conftest.py`, production code without a linked test, an unreadable link inventory)), and makes the local checkpoint commit. A\ntargeted red fails the attempt; the full check never overrides it. An\nimplement attempt that adds production code (a Python or shell file) no test\nreaches is refused before any test runs: add the test that reaches it. One full\n`make verify` runs on the final head before phase 6. In an ordinary Stage-1 session, you still run the commands\nand commits this prompt assigns to you, and the interactive session reads its own\nclock and logs its own spans, as the appetite rule below says.\n\n**Run the cheap checks before you hand back.** These are ruff (`ruff check` and\n`ruff format --check` on changed Python files) and selected tests. Implement owes\nevery ledger test. Repair owes its findings' proofs and written ledger entries;\nmissing unwritten entries are named but not owed. With a command tool, run the\nstanding ledger tests and leave the applicable checks green. On a file-only route,\nthe runner runs ruff, then pytest over changed or new test functions, standing\nledger tests and, on a retry, previously failed tests. Missing ledger IDs never\nreach pytest. The first red check ends the attempt (bead coding-harness-5tyh).\n`findings.md` is the runner's: an edit you make there is put back before the checks.\nThat edit is not part of your work, and on its own it never fails the attempt.\n\n**The plan is the contract.** Where it no longer holds — a file does not exist,\nan assumption does not carry, a test cannot be written that way — you **stop**\nand report in four lines:\n\n```\nexpected:   what the plan says\nfound:      what is actually there\nrelevant:   why this changes the solution\nproposal:   how to continue\n```\n\nThe plan is then revised, never silently overwritten. A deviation that lives\nonly in the code is no longer a deviation on the next reading — it is the plan.\n\n**The appetite is a stop.** The plan's card names one (`Appetite:`). *Time used*\nis the sum of the spans of the sessions that worked under this prompt on this\nchange. Read `date` when a session starts or work resumes, between steps, before\neach commit and when it ends (at its stop, resumption line or \"done:\" line);\nnever estimate it or recall it. A break inside a session counts, and the session's\nstatus message says so; the time between two sessions does not. A stop ends the span; work that\nresumes starts a new one, even in the same chat. When a span ends the session\nrecords it with `python3 scripts/harness.p",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::dispatch_go",
          "end_line": 2391,
          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "excerpt": "def parse_processes(ps_text: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> list[ProcessRow]:\n    \"\"\"The runner invocations and verification processes of one `ps` table.\n\n    Token matching only: a string inside an unrelated command - a shell\n    wrapper, an editor, an echo - is discarded, never reported.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for line in ps_text.splitlines():\n        parts = line.split(None, 2)\n        if len(parts) < 3 or not parts[0].isdigit() or not ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1]):\n            continue  # the header line and anything unshaped\n        pid, elapsed, command = parts\n        tokens = command.split()\n        if not tokens:\n            continue\n        row = _stage2_row(tokens, pid, elapsed, changes) or _verify_row(tokens, pid, elapsed)\n        if row is not None:\n            rows.append(row)\n    return rows\n",

          "citation": "scripts/machine_facts.py::jobs_field",
          "end_line": 256,
          "excerpt": "def jobs_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The runner and verification invocations of one `ps` snapshot, recognized by the run report.\n\n    Rows carry PID, elapsed time, verb and a known change or `not read` -\n    never raw command arguments - and invocations are counted, not\n    deduplicated into logical jobs (spec criterion 5). When the shared runner\n    definitions are unavailable, runner recognition says `not read` instead\n    of claiming no runners; a failed process table says so without touching\n    the other fields.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    if run_report.stage2 is None:\n        lines.append(f\"runner recognition: {NOT_READ} (runner verb definitions unavailable)\")\n    changes = frozenset()\n    if worktree is not None:\n        with contextlib.suppress(run_report.SourceError):\n            # attribution stays `not read`; readable rows still render\n            changes = frozenset(run_report.active_changes(worktree))\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"ps\", \"-axo\", \"pid,etime,command\"])\n        table = raw.splitlines()\n        # Validate source readability before the shared recognizer filters out\n        # unrelated processes. A readable header-only table can mean no matches.\n        if table and table[0].split() in ([\"PID\", \"ELAPSED\", \"COMMAND\"], [\"PID\", \"TIME\", \"COMMAND\"]):\n            table = table[1:]\n        elif not table:\n            raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        for line in table:\n            parts = line.split(None, 2)\n            if (\n                len(parts) != 3\n                or not parts[0].isdigit()\n                or not run_report.ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1])\n                or not parts[2].strip()\n            ):\n                raise run_report.SourceError(f\"{NOT_READ} (ps: malformed table)\")\n        rows = run_report.parse_processes(raw, changes)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        lines.append(str(error))\n        return lines\n    if not rows:\n        if run_report.stage2 is not None:\n            lines.append(\"none matched\")\n        return lines\n    lines.extend(f\"pid {row.pid} · {row.label} · change {row.change} · elapsed {row.elapsed}\" for row in rows)\n    return lines\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "end_line": 280,
          "excerpt": "def _pi_pin() -> str:\n    \"\"\"The exact Pi version `tools/pi/package.json` pins - anything else stops the runner.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        manifest = json.loads(PI_MANIFEST.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        pin = manifest[\"dependencies\"][PI_PACKAGE]\n        exact = isinstance(pin, str) and re.fullmatch(r\"\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+\", pin) is not None\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError):\n        exact = False\n    if not exact:\n        raise SystemExit(\n            f\"stage2: {PI_MANIFEST} does not pin an exact {PI_PACKAGE} version; \"\n            \"the runner has no pin to check (see tools/pi/README.md).\"\n        )\n    return pin\n",

          "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Declared expiry with advance warnings\", because it enforces\nthe recorded maintainer answers without granting approval by omission.\n\n1. Every paid `modelle_terms` reading requires a quoted ISO calendar date\n   `valid_until`. Missing, unusable or passed dates exclude and name the model;\n   expiry diagnostics include the recorded date when one has passed.\n2. Current per-call checks apply even to saved run membership.\n3. Preparation and terms-evaluating review-loop invocations warn from seven\n   days before expiry through the expiry day, naming model and date.\n   Warnings remain in successful preparation receipts and written round\n   evidence, including release to findings. Warnings never relax admission.\n4. The agent re-reads the source, records source and reading date, and\n   proposes each new or renewed entry in a decision pull request; the\n   maintainer merges. Use the source's explicit end date, otherwise the\n   reading date plus 30 calendar days. The runner does not renew dates.\n5. Migrate both DeepSeek readings from the documented 2026-10-25 re-read to\n   expiry 2026-10-31. Other existing records keep their reading dates and\n   gain reading date plus 30 days, including explicitly skipped records.\n6. Existing skip, source, retention, training and declaration checks still\n   apply. The discovered free diff-only class keeps ADR 0021's confined\n   exception. Saved membership/history is not rewritten to bypass expiry;\n   refusal may stop a saved round without consuming it or claiming success.\n\n",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`,",
