          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check\",\nbecause it implements the maintainer's model choice without weakening the\nrepair evidence contract.\n\n1. **Codex repairs all taken findings in one batch** through `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`: loop-record rows, released loop rows\n   and phase-6 findings. Each Codex attempt starts `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort\n   `max` in a fresh session, with the existing `workspace-write` configuration,\n   hooks and memories off, and no added directory, automatic approval or\n   bypass. Repair reads no GLM key and never routes to `glm-coding-plan`.\n2. **Only post-run failures advance the chain:** Codex; a fresh Codex attempt\n   with the first attempt's diagnostics; Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` on\n   Stage 1 with both diagnostics. A model call failure stops; with unchanged\n   HEAD, the existing restoration returns the worktree to baseline. When\n   Codex is unavailable, the orchestrator deliberately starts\n   `--stage2-off <reason>`, which uses Sonnet alone and records why. A\n   declaration refusal or leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.**\n   The orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>`, or\n   takes a finding no test can show as `taken — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Repair keeps those inputs, requests one fixed line per row and a measured\n   time entry, and starts no review. The runner checks each exact prompt,\n   prepares and formats the result, runs `make verify`, checks the time and\n   evidence, writes statuses and makes one clean descendant checkpoint.\n   A Codex call that moves HEAD stops before restoration or a runner commit.\n4. **The existing proof and statuses stand.** A code finding requires a\n   defined test the runner demonstrates red against baseline code; a finding\n   taken as `not a test` is proven by the separate re-check. Fixed rows read\n   `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Failed attempts retain their audit, quoted diagnostics and changed-file\n   evidence, while their model-written statuses are restored. Private loop\n   rows are marked only after the checkpoint; unreleased rows reach the\n   repair in the prompt rather than a worktree file.\n5. **The same model may repair phase-6 findings; a fresh session re-checks.**\n   A phase-6 verdict after an earlier `## Phase 6` block in `findings.md` — a\n   re-check — runs Codex read-only without resuming the repair, a prior\n   verdict or a historical phase-2a session; the first phase-6 review keeps\n   the resume rule of ADR 0016. Loop marks may\n   resume only that new verdict thread after its verdict. This replaces ADR\n   0015's blanket reviewer/repairer separation; it does not give review calls\n   write tools or move any review to another model.\n6. **The loop budget and run count stand.** A fixed row counts as taken;\n   round 3 requires a taken or fixed row in round 2, and the maximum stays\n   three rounds. The orchestrator writes `Broke a test` from the repair\n   evidence before the next round or release. Audit lines and historical GLM\n   counts retain their format. Initial implementation, Explore and draft's\n   GLM fallback retain their models.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1506,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuse",

          "excerpt": "### 6.6 What a phase needs — the requirement table that replaces model names\n\n| Phase | Needs | Example configuration (stage 1, Anthropic-only, lives in `model-routing.yaml`) |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 Explore | much input, little output, no deep reasoning | a small fast model |\n| 1a Interview · 2 Spec · 2b Design · 3 Plan | the highest reasoning available, little output; an error here is the most expensive | the strongest model |\n| 2a Spec review · 6 Review | a fresh context that never saw the author's reasoning; a different lineage where residency allows, otherwise at least a different model | a second strong model; stage 2: another vendor behind the leak check |\n| 4 Implement | a reliable worker given a clear plan; the token-heavy phase | a mid-class model |\n| 5 Verify | deterministic — no model | — |\n| 7 Commit | cheap and sufficient | a small model |\n| Escalation | two failed review rounds, or security/concurrency, or a change above roughly 200k tokens → the strongest model; back down after a pass | — |\n\nThe doctrine carries the left two columns.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Repository-local npm install with real offline contracts\",\nbecause it separates the runner from global updates and makes the original\nisolation measurement repeatable on every proposed version change.\n\n1. `tools/pi/package.json` holds the exact Pi dependency; its npm lock records\n   the dependency graph and integrity values. `tools/pi/install.sh` uses\n   `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. No installed dependencies are committed.\n2. Every runner Pi path, including loop/probe and interactive-session preflight,\n   extension confirmation and dispatch, uses `tools/pi/pi`. The wrapper refuses\n   another major locally; minor/patch moves within that major remain eligible\n   for the same contracts. Pi and Node changes are proposed in pull requests.\n4. The suite starts real pinned Pi with synthetic credentials and a loopback\n   model stand-in, locally and in CI. It holds reviewer tool declarations and\n   refusal, suppression of discovered extension/MCP startup and skill/prompt/theme\n   reads, context-file exclusion and scratch-agent separation from ambient auth\n   and command-valued model configuration, extension input/results, the production session\n   policy's foreign-read blocking, model-list table and Go/Zen provider address\n   and key mapping. Missing prerequisites fail rather than skip these contracts.\n5. This replaces the requirement to repeat a manual measurement alone when the\n   pin moves; the manual Pi 1.1.0 findings remain historical evidence. The normal\n   verification gates and real contracts must pass before a version move ships.\n6. Authentication boundaries stay as decided: scratch reviewer configuration\n   and Go key only in `OPENCODE_API_KEY`; interactive sessions sign in from the\n   maintainer's own Pi agent directory. No paid Zen endpoint is enabled here.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def require_pi() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Refuse unless the repository wrapper prints exactly the pinned version (spec, criterion 27).\n\n    The wrapper is the one path to Pi (ADR 0019): it refuses a missing,\n    mismatched or unusable local install before any model request, and this\n    check ties its answer to the manifest pin. Runs before the prompt check,\n    the call line and any call, in a scratch directory with no key: a Pi off\n    the pin sends nothing. The session verb calls it after its argument and\n    handover checks.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        env = foreign_env({\"HOME\": tmp, \"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": tmp})\n        try:\n            done = launch(\n                [str(PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"],\n                Path(tmp),\n                env,\n                timeout=PI_VERSION_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the version check's limit of {PI_VERSION_SECONDS} seconds\",\n            )\n        except CallFailed as error:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"{PI_WRAPPER} could not be checked ({error}); it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\"\n            ) from None\n    said = (done.stdout or \"\").strip()\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        # The wrapper's own refusal names the defect; its last lines travel with this one.\n        tail = \"\\n\".join((done.stderr or \"\").splitlines()[-5:])\n        detail = f\": {tail}\" if tail else \"\"\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"{PI_WRAPPER} --version ended {done.returncode}; it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; \"\n            f\"no call starts{detail}.\"\n        )\n    if said != PI_VERSION:\n        raise Refused(f\"pi {said or 'printed nothing'} is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\")\n",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008).           "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8).           "end_line": 136,
          "excerpt": "## Communication and session continuity\n\n- Speak German with the maintainer; keep repository artifacts English.\n- Use short, plainly worded messages with clear headings. Explain technical\n  terms and identifiers at first use in every message. Lead with the main\n  point and one concrete next action; show at most three immediate priorities.\n  Keep optional detail separate.\n- **Every question carries its context** (ADR 0018): before any options, short\n  Topic; Intention (why now); Today; Repository change; Architecture change,\n  in plain words, the question last on its own line. It covers every question\n  — interviews, spec decisions, review ambiguities, plan cards, conversation\n  — in every harness, for everyone; the reason is ADHD (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`,\n  \"The question protocol\").\n- Say what behavior changed and why it matters; mark proposed, implemented and\n  tested work apart. Ask one decision at a time, with a recommendation and its\n  consequence; do not re-ask settled decisions or existing permission. An open question for the maintainer is written at once, with its context and recommendation, into the notes of the bead it concerns (`tools/bd update <id> --append-notes`, then `tools/bd dolt push`), never only into chat or a session scratchpad; the handover gathers them under \"Needed from the maintainer\" (maintainer, 2026-11-06).\n- An orchestrating session shows a sub-agent's plan card to the maintainer\n  unchanged; the veto stays the maintainer's (`prompts/03-plan.md`).\n- At session start or after a break, read the latest relevant handover and its addenda;\n  check the working tree and current PR state before acting. Begin with a short orientation:\n  **Where we are / Next step / Needed from you**. Say \"nothing right now\" when no answer is\n  needed; never make the user rebuild the chat or read the whole backlog.\n- Before ending or handing over a session, maintain a dated file under\n  `docs/journal/handover/`. Record the objective, completed work and evidence,\n  decisions and preferences, unfinished work/blockers, branch/commit/PR,\n  parallel-session ownership, and one concrete resumption action. Preserve\n  prior records with a dated addendum; task status stays in Beads.\n- Link the handover in the closing message; the next session resumes from it.\n- A bead for a change names its class (`spike` … `architectural`) in its description (2026-10-22).\n- **Night runs stay plain** (maintainer, 2026-10-12): `ROADMAP.md` is the one map and the\n  morning handover the one report; no Kanban board, canvas or dashboard (Grafana included)\n  is proposed or built for the night run until the maintainer states that the plain form\n  has carried. Collecting data is not covered: a s",

          "excerpt": "### The review loop (phase 4b)\n\n**Fresh availability-enabled runs (Q-16, ADR 0021):** first run\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py prepare-loop <change>`. The runner refreshes Pi's\ncatalog and probes admitted candidates with static input and no tools.\nTimed exclusions are skipped without a call; GLM through OpenCode Go is not\nexcluded (the 2026-10-21 GLM outage covers the Z.ai route only). Paid candidates require known cost, admitted terms and catalog presence.\nReport its timestamped reachable/failed/skipped list and selected stages in\nthe main Claude Code or Codex conversation, then invoke `review-loop <change>\n--availability-reported <id>` with the printed report id. This acknowledges\nthe report; the runner cannot inspect the conversation UI. The external\nreceipt is bound to the worktree, configuration and diff and expires after\n900 seconds. Changed inputs or failed preparation invalidate it. Preparation\nadds one actual call per tested candidate and is no review-quality or billing\nmeasurement. Up to three cheapest reachable paid candidates dynamically fill\nthe Flash swarm; the remaining reachable paid candidates form the ladder.\nExisting snapshots and legacy declarations without the rule retain the\nbehavior below. A run with history cannot be reset by preparation.\n\n**Paid terms expire (ADR 0022, bead coding-harness-abra).** Every\n`modelle_terms` record of a paid model carries `valid_until`, a quoted ISO\ncalendar date the reading is valid through; the following UTC day it is\nexpired, and the judgement reads UTC, never the local calendar. A record\nwithout a usable `valid_until` — missing, not a quoted date, or an impossible\ncalendar date — grants no admission, and the runner never infers, extends or\nrenews a date at runtime. A refusal names the model, says whether the expiry\nis missing, invalid or passed, and names the recorded date once it has\npassed. From seven UTC days before expiry through the expiry day,\npreparation and every round — fresh, legacy or resumed — print a warning\nwith the model id and date, and the round's notes carry it, so the released\nfindings keep it; a warning neither admits nor refuses, an expired reading\nis a skip with its reason, not a warning, and a skipped record with a valid\ndate warns too. A saved selection or a fresh receipt does not keep an\nexpired member admissible: the round is refused before the call, and the\nrun's history stands. Renewal is not the runner's: a reading is introduced\nor renewed by an agent's dated source re-read and a decision pull request\nmerged by the maintainer; where the source states an end date it is\nrecorded, and otherwise a record expires `gelesen` plus 30 calendar days.\nMigrated 2026-10-26 on that rule; both DeepSeek readings carry the\ndocumented 2026-10-25 source re-read and expire 2026-10-31.\n\nAfter implementation and before phase 6, `review-loop` runs one round per\ncall, and the loop runs **until a round is clean — every row of a round\ndecided and none accepted (ADR 0021).** Round 1 is the **free swarm**: a\nforced live catalog refresh (`pi update --models` before `pi --list-models`,\nno stale cache listed) discovers the models the `opencode-go` provider offers,\nand the `free_stage` rule in `model-endpoints.yaml` — provider, id suffix,\nincludes, excludes — selects the members; they review in parallel, each with\nno tools, from a scratch directory, and their only input is the\nimplementation diff: bounded hunks of source and test code against the merge\nbase with `origin/main`, uncommitted and untracked code included. The catalog\nis a live intermediary (`pi.dev`): the check proves which catalog was read,\nnot what OpenCode Go bills. The prompt carries the implementation diff up to\nthe bound of `REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES` (2000 lines); a cut is recorded in the\nround, and a round over a cut diff never counts as clean (R-12, R-15).           "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"fe",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_go_path_reads_the_one_address_record(world, monkeypatch, capsys):\n    \"\"\"Criterion 1: no caller keeps its own Go origin rule or missing-address default.\n\n    Fault: a caller that prepared against one record and dispatched from a\n    private one would send after the record changed, or would run when the\n    record is gone.\n    \"\"\"\n    model = TEST_LADDER[0]\n    harness = Harness(world, monkeypatch)\n    store = go_store(row(model))\n    seat_lines: list[str] = []\n    seat = harness.seat(model, store, seat_lines)\n    calls = [\n        harness.reviewer(model, store),\n        harness.reviewer(model, store, free=True),\n        harness.probe(model, store)[0],\n        seat,\n    ]\n    for call in calls:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        call()\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a family did not dispatch under the admitted record\"\n    # The record alone changes; every family's next launch refuses.\n    edit_entry(world, lambda e: e[\"adresse\"].update({\"host\": \"elsewhere.invalid\"}))\n    for call in calls:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        with pytest.raises((stage2.Refused, stage2_go.DestinationRefused)) as raised:\n            call()\n        assert \"not the admitted host\" in str(raised.value)\n    # A refused member aborts the swarm: an admission refusal is no answer to replace.\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused) as raised:\n        harness.swarm(model, store)()\n    assert \"not the admitted host\" in str(raised.value)\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a changed record dispatched a further send\"\n    # The record disappears: fail closed, no caller fills a default in.\n    edit_entry(world, lambda e: e.pop(\"adresse\"))\n    for call in calls:\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused) as raised:\n            call()\n        assert \"unusable\" in str(raised.value)\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused) as raised:\n        harness.swarm(model, store)()\n    assert \"unusable\" in str(raised.value)\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a missing record admitted a launch\"\n",

          "end_line": 866,
          "excerpt": "def test_every_send_rechecks_current_policy(world, monkeypatch, capsys):\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a saved selection, resumed round, replacement or retry dispatches no now-refused base.\n\n    Fault: an old receipt or saved overlay authorized the send; here the\n    record turns hostile after every preparation and nothing dispatches.\n    \"\"\"\n    model = TEST_LADDER[0]\n    harness = Harness(world, monkeypatch)\n    store = go_store(row(model))\n    seat_lines: list[str] = []\n    seat = harness.seat(model, store, seat_lines)\n    probe_call, _audit = harness.probe(model, store)\n    prepared = [harness.reviewer(model, store), harness.reviewer(model, store, free=True), probe_call, seat]\n    for call in prepared:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        call()\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(prepared), \"preparation itself failed\"\n    history = (list(harness.sent), list(seat_lines))\n    # The record turns hostile after preparation: no saved evidence dispatches.\n    edit_entry(world, lambda e: e[\"adresse\"].update({\"host\": \"elsewhere.invalid\"}))\n    for call in prepared:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        with pytest.raises((stage2.Refused, stage2_go.DestinationRefused)) as raised:\n            call()\n        assert \"not the admitted host\" in str(raised.value)\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused):\n        harness.swarm(model, store)()\n    assert (list(harness.sent), list(seat_lines)) == history, \"earlier completed history was rewritten\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_real_reviewer_tool_contract(project: Path, transport) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a real reviewer-shaped call declares exactly read,grep,find,ls; an undeclared tool cannot execute.\"\"\"\n    standin = StandIn(\n        [\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"read\", \"arguments\": {\"path\": \"sentinel.txt\"}}]},\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": f\"echo pwned >> {project / 'sentinel.txt'}\"}}]},\n            {\"content\": \"No finding.\"},\n        ]\n    )\n    transport.providers[\"opencode-go\"] = {\"baseUrl\": standin.url}\n    try:\n        answer = stage2.run_reviewer(\n            contract_ctx(project),\n            \"contract-rung\",\n            \"Review the change demo as the appended instructions say.\",\n            SYNTHETIC_KEY,\n        )\n        assert \"No finding.\" in answer, \"the scripted stop never reached the runner\"\n        assert len(standin.requests) == 3, f\"expected the scripted three turns, saw {len(standin.requests)}\"\n        declared = tool_names(standin.requests[0])\n        assert declared == {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, (\n            f\"the model saw {sorted(declared)}, not the four reviewer tools\"\n        )\n        assert SENTINEL_IN in message_text(standin.requests[1]), \"the positive control read never executed\"\n        for exchange in standin.requests:\n            assert tool_names(exchange) <= {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, \"a foreign tool was declared\"\n        assert (project / \"sentinel.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == SENTINEL_IN + \"\\n\", (\n            \"an undeclared tool changed the sentinel\"\n        )\n    finally:\n        standin.close()\n    # the launch was the runner's own construction, through the wrapper, under the guard\n    (call,) = transport.calls\n    assert call[\"argv\"][0] == str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"the reviewer did not start through the repository wrapper\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--tools\") + 1] == \"read,grep,find,ls\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--model\") + 1] == \"opencode-go/contract-rung\"\n    assert \"NODE_OPTIONS\" in call[\"env\"] and \"pi_network_guard\" in call[\"env\"][\"NODE_OPTIONS\"]\n    assert call[\"env\"][\"OPENCODE_API_KEY\"] == SYNTHETIC_KEY\n",

      ],
      "statement": "Real pinned-Pi contracts exist for the reviewer shape and the interactive session only: `test_real_reviewer_tool_contract` asserts the declared tool set `read,grep,find,ls` on real Pi and that an undeclared `bash` tool cannot execute; `test_real_free_reviewer_has_only_the_implementation_diff` asserts `--no-tools` and a diff-only payload; the session test asserts the interactive argv (`--no-extensions`, `--no-mcp`, discovery flags off, `-e` the policy copy, `--model`, `-- <prompt>`) and that no `--print`, `-p`, `--mode` or `--pure` appears. No real-Pi contract measures a writable, headless Pi call, while ADR 0019 requires every runner Pi path to use `tools/pi/pi` and to be held by offline contracts that fail rather than skip."
    },

    "A Pi work route's unit tests need no new harness: the work-run fixture installs stand-ins for `bash`, `sh`, `codex`, `claude`, `pi`, `make` and `pin-pi`, patches `stage2.PI_WRAPPER` to the `pin-pi` stand-in and disables the overlay check (tests/test_stage2.py::world), and the stand-in records argv, env, cwd and argv[-1] for a prompt (tests/test_stage2.py::STAND_IN).",
    "The non-Codex repair prompt branch is not unexercised in principle: tests/test_stage2_fail_fast.py passes `endpoint=stage2.GLM_FLASH` to `repair_prompt` and asserts the `You cannot run commands` branch, so the file-tools wording a Pi repair attempt would receive is already asserted for another endpoint.",
    "Most of these tests name their fault only in prose (`Fault: …`, `Planted fault: …` docstrings) and realise it through scripted stand-in steps; the executed red-first proof machinery (a named test proven red then green, and a guard test proven with `STAGE2_PLANT_FAULT=1`) is reached only through the repair verb, so none of the route tests cited above proves its own redness against production code.",
    "The section-4 routing prose about the launcher is not held by any test I found: `routing_problems` compares only model cells and effort/sandbox clauses, and no test asserts the string \"through Claude Code against Z.ai\" (tests/test_stage2.py::test_workflow_section_4_routes_the_three_reviews).",
    "The Go-access harness docstring scopes itself deliberately (\"Every test drives the real caller functions — reviewer, swarm, probe and research seat\"), so the absence of a work verb there reads as a declared scope, not as a claim that no work path exists."
  ],

          "excerpt": "def test_real_reviewer_tool_contract(project: Path, transport) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a real reviewer-shaped call declares exactly read,grep,find,ls; an undeclared tool cannot execute.\"\"\"\n    standin = StandIn(\n        [\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"read\", \"arguments\": {\"path\": \"sentinel.txt\"}}]},\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": f\"echo pwned >> {project / 'sentinel.txt'}\"}}]},\n            {\"content\": \"No finding.\"},\n        ]\n    )\n    transport.providers[\"opencode-go\"] = {\"baseUrl\": standin.url}\n    try:\n        answer = stage2.run_reviewer(\n            contract_ctx(project),\n            \"contract-rung\",\n            \"Review the change demo as the appended instructions say.\",\n            SYNTHETIC_KEY,\n        )\n        assert \"No finding.\" in answer, \"the scripted stop never reached the runner\"\n        assert len(standin.requests) == 3, f\"expected the scripted three turns, saw {len(standin.requests)}\"\n        declared = tool_names(standin.requests[0])\n        assert declared == {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, (\n            f\"the model saw {sorted(declared)}, not the four reviewer tools\"\n        )\n        assert SENTINEL_IN in message_text(standin.requests[1]), \"the positive control read never executed\"\n        for exchange in standin.requests:\n            assert tool_names(exchange) <= {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, \"a foreign tool was declared\"\n        assert (project / \"sentinel.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == SENTINEL_IN + \"\\n\", (\n            \"an undeclared tool changed the sentinel\"\n        )\n    finally:\n        standin.close()\n    # the launch was the runner's own construction, through the wrapper, under the guard\n    (call,) = transport.calls\n    assert call[\"argv\"][0] == str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"the reviewer did not start through the repository wrapper\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--tools\") + 1] == \"read,grep,find,ls\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--model\") + 1] == \"opencode-go/contract-rung\"\n    assert \"NODE_OPTIONS\" in call[\"env\"] and \"pi_network_guard\" in call[\"env\"][\"NODE_OPTIONS\"]\n    assert call[\"env\"][\"OPENCODE_API_KEY\"] == SYNTHETIC_KEY\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_go_path_reads_the_one_address_record(world, monkeypatch, capsys):\n    \"\"\"Criterion 1: no caller keeps its own Go origin rule or missing-address default.\n\n    Fault: a caller that prepared against one record and dispatched from a\n    private one would send after the record changed, or would run when the\n    record is gone.\n    \"\"\"\n    model = TEST_LADDER[0]\n    harness = Harness(world, monkeypatch)\n    store = go_store(row(model))\n    seat_lines: list[str] = []\n    seat = harness.seat(model, store, seat_lines)\n    calls = [\n        harness.reviewer(model, store),\n        harness.reviewer(model, store, free=True),\n        harness.probe(model, store)[0],\n        seat,\n    ]\n    for call in calls:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        call()\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a family did not dispatch under the admitted record\"\n    # The record alone changes; every family's next launch refuses.\n    edit_entry(world, lambda e: e[\"adresse\"].update({\"host\": \"elsewhere.invalid\"}))\n    for call in calls:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        with pytest.raises((stage2.Refused, stage2_go.DestinationRefused)) as raised:\n            call()\n        assert \"not the admitted host\" in str(raised.value)\n    # A refused member aborts the swarm: an admission refusal is no answer to replace.\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused) as raised:\n        harness.swarm(model, store)()\n    assert \"not the admitted host\" in str(raised.value)\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a changed record dispatched a further send\"\n    # The record disappears: fail closed, no caller fills a default in.\n    edit_entry(world, lambda e: e.pop(\"adresse\"))\n    for call in calls:\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused) as raised:\n            call()\n        assert \"unusable\" in str(raised.value)\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused) as raised:\n        harness.swarm(model, store)()\n    assert \"unusable\" in str(raised.value)\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a missing record admitted a launch\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_send_rechecks_current_policy(world, monkeypatch, capsys):\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a saved selection, resumed round, replacement or retry dispatches no now-refused base.\n\n    Fault: an old receipt or saved overlay authorized the send; here the\n    record turns hostile after every preparation and nothing dispatches.\n    \"\"\"\n    model = TEST_LADDER[0]\n    harness = Harness(world, monkeypatch)\n    store = go_store(row(model))\n    seat_lines: list[str] = []\n    seat = harness.seat(model, store, seat_lines)\n    probe_call, _audit = harness.probe(model, store)\n    prepared = [harness.reviewer(model, store), harness.reviewer(model, store, free=True), probe_call, seat]\n    for call in prepared:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        call()\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(prepared), \"preparation itself failed\"\n    history = (list(harness.sent), list(seat_lines))\n    # The record turns hostile after preparation: no saved evidence dispatches.\n    edit_entry(world, lambda e: e[\"adresse\"].update({\"host\": \"elsewhere.invalid\"}))\n    for call in prepared:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        with pytest.raises((stage2.Refused, stage2_go.DestinationRefused)) as raised:\n            call()\n        assert \"not the admitted host\" in str(raised.value)\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused):\n        harness.swarm(model, store)()\n    assert (list(harness.sent), list(seat_lines)) == history, \"earlier completed history was rewritten\"\n",

          "end_line": 2391,
          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "end_line": 2023,
          "excerpt": "def checked_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n):\n    \"\"\"Check the admission and exact prompt immediately before one call.\n\n    `admission_problem`, when given, replaces the individual declaration (the\n    free class, ADR 0021 decision 3); the leak check is mandatory either way.\n    A subscription endpoint's expiry notice prints first (bead coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    subscription_terms_warnings(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise AdmissionRefused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(ctx.change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), ctx.root, [(\"prompt\", prompt)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the call does not start.\")\n    # A scan can cross UTC midnight: an earlier admission cannot authorize\n    # dispatch after expiry, including retry and replacement calls.\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return result\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). Before the failure is decided, findings.md is restored outright: every post-run check, cheap\n    or full, reads the runner's file, an edit alone fails nothing, and a completed attempt that edited\n    it carries a quoted restore notice under its audit line (spec, criteria 8 and 9).\n\n    A verb that passes `retain_answer` keeps every attempt's full answer: right at the model-return\n    boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can stop the run, the protected\n    answer is saved as local evidence and its location joins the attempt's diagnostics - the parser's\n    rejections, ",

The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8).           "excerpt": "def checked_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n):\n    \"\"\"Check the admission and exact prompt immediately before one call.\n\n    `admission_problem`, when given, replaces the individual declaration (the\n    free class, ADR 0021 decision 3); the leak check is mandatory either way.\n    A subscription endpoint's expiry notice prints first (bead coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    subscription_terms_warnings(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise AdmissionRefused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(ctx.change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), ctx.root, [(\"prompt\", prompt)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the call does not start.\")\n    # A scan can cross UTC midnight: an earlier admission cannot authorize\n    # dispatch after expiry, including retry and replacement calls.\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return result\n",

          "excerpt": "def install_policy(private: Path, runner) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Copy the extension into the session's private directory; the copy, not the source, is what Pi loads.\n\n    The extension refuses writes to its own file, and a copy under `.stage2-sessions/` is one the session's\n    file tools may not touch either, whereas `scripts/` holds a tracked file of the worktree.\n    \"\"\"\n    copy = private / POLICY_FILE\n    try:\n        shutil.copyfile(POLICY_SOURCE, copy)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise runner.Refused(f\"the policy extension {POLICY_SOURCE.name} could not be copied: {error}\") from error\n    return copy\n",

Decider: maintainer ·\n  prepared by Codex. Acceptance is the merge commit; the review header\n  remains pending.\n* Date: 2026-10-31 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nAt `b126fce7`, inspected 2026-10-31, the research selector permits only\n`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, while the review overlay activates catalog\naddresses without a destination check. Research reproduced the former's\nrefusal of `/inference/go/v1`; the real-Pi contract expects a foreign host\nto survive overlay activation. The two paths therefore disagree about\nwhere the same provider may receive content (destination finding DL-B-8;\n`plans/changes/go-access-point/research.md`).\n\nThe five interview answers require one rule for review, research, probes\nand interactive launch, permit a new path on the admitted host with notice,\nand let an agent maintain sourced same-host paths. The address record lives\non the `opencode-go` entry of `model-endpoints.yaml`. The runner holds that\nwhole file from foreign model attempts; the orchestrating session maintains\nit, with no new maintainer approval for each documented same-host path\nmove. These directions are answered; this draft takes effect on merge.\n\n## Decision Drivers\n\n* A catalog must not choose an undeclared host for a key or change content.\n* A same-host path move must not stop every swarm.\n* All Go launches must agree without duplicating destination policy.\n* Address maintenance must not grant model, terms or credential authority.\n* The Go address component must fit the coming provider/model registry.\n\n## Considered Options\n\n* **Shared provider-entry policy and explicit Pi binding** — one rule,\n  with cross-caller migration and orchestrator-owned record maintenance.\n* **Separate writable address record** — attempts could update paths,\n  but a second record splits provider governance; Q-5 chose the entry.\n* **Repair only the research allow-list** — unblocks that selector but\n  leaves review/probes/session destination trust inconsistent.\n* **Require exact known paths everywhere** — refuses foreign hosts but\n  contradicts the answered permission to continue after a same-host move.\n\n## Decision\n\nChosen proposal: \"Shared provider-entry policy and explicit Pi binding\",\nbecause it implements the five answered intentions at one destination\nboundary and fits the future central registry without another model list.\n\n1. Every runner-controlled Go launch uses one current provider address\n   policy, including probes, retries and calls using saved selections.\n2. Bases require HTTPS, the exact admitted host `opencode.ai` and the default\n   port, with no credentials, query, fragment or ambiguous URL form.\n3. A different path on that origin is preserved and visibly reported with\n   the model and old/new paths. It does not update the known path by itself.\n4.     "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",
      "subject": "feat(adr): the gate adr-answers and the command decide adr",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "provenance.yaml"
      ]
    },

It stood without a class while docs/governance/regelwerk.md beside it is\nhuman-decided; the commit guard of the review-swarm runner could only refuse it\nthrough a hard-coded list (R-22 of the review-swarm review).\n\nThe maintainer's answer in the night interview of 2026-10-20 (Q-1, option A): the\nsame class as the rulebook. Gate changes then always travel as a decision pull\nrequest.\n",

      "author_utc": "2026-11-08T21:31:52Z",
      "body": "Main (bead coding-harness-wb40) moved the research swarm's free selection\ninto the shared `stage2_free.select`, which keeps a drift notice only for an\neligible id. This branch requires every address-admissible candidate's notice\nto reach `address_notices` before any eligibility filter, each model once\n(spec criterion 3).\n\nResolution in `select_research_catalog`: main's shared selection stays the one\nrule (paid admission, declaration exclusion, destination refusal); the branch's\n`collect_notice` still runs for every free candidate before that selection, and\nthe selection's own notices are merged without repeats. `stage2_free.select` is\nunchanged: the review loop takes its notices from `activate_overlay`, which\nalready sees every row before selection, so the research swarm is the only\ncaller that needed the guarantee. Changing the shared module would have changed\nits documented contract for both callers without need.\n\nTests: the branch's two research-catalog calls pass main's new required\n`paid=()` and `exclusion=None`, as main did for the existing calls. A new test\ncovers the case only the merge creates: a `-free` row vetoed as paid-admitted\nby the shared selection keeps its notice, once (it fails without the\npre-filter collection). No test from either side was weakened or removed.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9FFLqLWsj1biQidvPo\n",

      "author_utc": "2026-11-20T10:27:07Z",
      "body": "The orchestrator applies the held-path step of the plan, as the maintainer\ndecided on 2026-11-20:\n\n- model-endpoints.yaml declares the `spec_review` block the runner reads:\n  call limit 30 minutes, pause 30 seconds, fallback deepseek-v4.1-flash on\n  opencode-go (L3-2).\n- AGENTS.md and docs/WORKFLOW.md no longer call phase 2a optional; the class\n  table requires the review for bounded, feature and architectural changes;\n  the class paragraph says implement checks the class on every route; the\n  draft chain repeats draft and review up to round three, with the final\n  draft and the recorded fourth-round form; a new subsection states what\n  counts, currency, retry and fallback, the re-check and the inventory\n  (L2-8, L2-11, L3-3, L3-4). README's phase line follows.\n- prompts/02-spec.md and prompts/02a-spec-review.md state the re-review, the\n  strict severities and the exact `No finding.` answer (L3-6).\n- The handover skill runs `--spec-review-inventory` in the morning handover\n  (L3-10).\n- The criterion 1-3 tests read every workflow text and went red against the\n  old texts by hand; new tests anchor the prompt format, the repository's\n  declaration and the skill (L2-12, L3-5). The test world drops the real\n  `spec_review` block so fixtures declare their own.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). Before the failure is decided, findings.md is restored outright: every post-run check, cheap\n    or full, reads the runner's file, an edit alone fails nothing, and a completed attempt that edited\n    it carries a quoted restore notice under its audit line (spec, criteria 8 and 9).\n\n    A verb that passes `retain_answer` keeps every attempt's full answer: right at the model-return\n    boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can stop the run, the protected\n    answer is saved as local evidence and its location joins the attempt's diagnostics - the parser's\n    rejections, the call and verify failures included - and is printed on success (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). A failed call keeps the output it returned.\n\n    A verb that passes `protect_lifecycle` snapshots the change's lifecycle fields (`status`,\n    `implementation_status`) in spec, optional design and plan right before every call.           "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_fallback_review(\n    ctx: Context, config: dict, opus_failure: CallFailed\n) -> tuple[bytes, str, list[list[str]], str, tuple[str, str, str | None], object]:\n    \"\"\"The declared fallback review through Pi, after the Opus route failed twice (spec criteria 13-15).\n\n    The leak check runs first and a BLOCK still refuses - no fallback call starts. The\n    fallback reads the spec body fresh at its own call start, and the body on disk must still\n    be those bytes when the call ends. A failed or unreadable fallback fails the whole call.\n    \"\"\"\n    if config[\"fallback_model\"] is None:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the Opus review produced no readable review ({opus_failure}); no fallback model is declared \"\n            \"in model-endpoints.yaml's `spec_review` block, so no fallback call starts.\"\n        )\n    endpoint = (str(config[\"fallback_endpoint\"]), str(config[\"fallback_model\"]), None)\n    if endpoint[0] != OPENCODE:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the spec review's fallback endpoint must be {OPENCODE}, where the runner's Pi reviews; \"\n            f\"{endpoint[0]} is not.\"\n        )\n    problem = terms_problem(endpoint_entry(ctx.root), endpoint[1])\n    if problem is not None:\n        raise CallFailed(f\"the fallback review is not admitted on its declared terms: {problem}\")\n    require_committed_review_spec(ctx.root, ctx.change)\n    commit = _git_output(ctx.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    body = spec_body_bytes(ctx.folder / \"spec.md\")\n    if body != spec_body_of(_git_bytes(ctx.root, \"show\", f\"{commit}:plans/changes/{ctx.change}/spec.md\")):\n        raise CallFailed(\"the spec changed while the review snapshot was read.\")\n    prompt = spec_review_prompt(ctx.root, ctx.change, body)\n    result = checked_prompt(ctx, endpoint, prompt)\n    require_pi()\n    discovery = discover_free(ctx.root, allow_empty=True)\n    ctx.models_store = discovery.get(\"models_store\")\n    require_committed_review_spec(ctx.root, ctx.change)\n    try:\n        answer = run_reviewer(\n            ctx,\n            endpoint[1],\n            prompt,\n            reviewer_key(),\n            free=False,\n            timeout_seconds=int(config[\"timeout_seconds\"]),\n        )\n    except CallFailed as error:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the Opus review produced no readable review ({opus_failure}) and the fallback review \"\n            f\"failed too ({error}).\"\n        ) from error\n    rows = readable_review(answer)\n    if spec_body_bytes(ctx.folder / \"spec.md\") != body:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the spec body changed during the fallback review; no block is written for bytes the reviewer did not read.\"\n        )\n    return body, commit, rows, answer, endpoint, result\n",

          "excerpt": "def install_policy(private: Path, runner) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Copy the extension into the session's private directory; the copy, not the source, is what Pi loads.\n\n    The extension refuses writes to its own file, and a copy under `.stage2-sessions/` is one the session's\n    file tools may not touch either, whereas `scripts/` holds a tracked file of the worktree.\n    \"\"\"\n    copy = private / POLICY_FILE\n    try:\n        shutil.copyfile(POLICY_SOURCE, copy)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise runner.Refused(f\"the policy extension {POLICY_SOURCE.name} could not be copied: {error}\") from error\n    return copy\n",

          "excerpt": "def checked_session_model(root: Path, bare: str, runner) -> tuple[dict, stage2_go.Assessment]:\n    \"\"\"The checked definition a session's initial Go model binds, resolved offline.\n\n    The definition's own fields come from the pinned install's shipped catalog\n    (a runner-owned file, never the user's agent directory). Its explicit base\n    is preserved; only an omitted base takes the record's wire-API default.\n    A same-host path move carries a notice into the launch audit. No\n    credential-bearing file is read, and the user's saved\n    login stays where it is: the binding composes with it inside Pi.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise runner.Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    catalog = (\n        Path(runner.PI_WRAPPER).resolve().parent\n        / \"node_modules\"\n        / \"@earendil-works\"\n        / \"pi-ai\"\n        / \"dist\"\n        / \"providers\"\n        / \"data\"\n        / f\"{stage2_go.PROVIDER}.json\"\n    )\n    try:\n        data = json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):\n        raise runner.Refused(\n            f\"the pinned install's {stage2_go.PROVIDER} catalog cannot be read; \"\n            \"the session cannot bind its model offline.\"\n        ) from None\n    sections = [(api, part) for api, part in data.items() if isinstance(part, dict) and f\"chat:{bare}\" in part]\n    if len(sections) != 1:\n        raise runner.Refused(\n            f\"the pinned install's catalog carries {bare} under {len(sections)} wire apis; \"\n            \"the session binds no ambiguous model.\"\n        )\n    api, part = sections[0]\n    definition = part[f\"chat:{bare}\"]\n    if not isinstance(definition, dict) or (\"api\" in definition and definition[\"api\"] != api):\n        raise runner.Refused(\n            f\"the pinned install's catalog section and entry disagree on the wire api for {bare}; \"\n            \"the session binds no inconsistent model.\"\n        )\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, bare, {**definition, \"api\": api})\n    if not verdict.admitted:\n        raise runner.Refused(verdict.problem)\n    return {name: verdict.definition[name] for name in MODEL_SIDECAR_FIELDS if name in verdict.definition}, verdict\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_pi_settings_writer_uses_shared_constant() -> None:\n    \"\"\"One settings definition prevents discovery, reviews, probes and research from drifting.\n\n    Planting the old inline literal at any writer must fail even while its JSON\n    still matches today's content; the contract here is shared ownership.\n    \"\"\"\n    expected = {\n        \"stage2.py\": (2, \"PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"),\n        \"stage2_availability.py\": (1, \"runner.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"),\n        \"stage2_research_run.py\": (1, \"self.runner.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"),\n    }\n    assert hasattr(stage2, \"PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"), \"all Pi settings writers need one shared production constant\"\n    assert stage2.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS == {\"retry\": {\"enabled\": False}, \"compaction\": {\"enabled\": False}}\n    for filename, (count, reference) in expected.items():\n        tree = ast.parse((REPO_ROOT / \"scripts\" / filename).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        writes = [\n            node\n            for node in ast.walk(tree)\n            if isinstance(node, ast.Call)\n            and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute)\n            and node.func.attr == \"write_text\"\n            and isinstance(node.func.value, ast.BinOp)\n            and isinstance(node.func.value.right, ast.Constant)\n            and node.func.value.right.value == \"settings.json\"\n        ]\n        assert len(writes) == count, f\"{filename}: the settings writer inventory changed\"\n        for write in writes:\n            value = write.args[0]\n            assert isinstance(value, ast.Call) and ast.unparse(value.func) == \"json.dumps\", filename\n            assert len(value.args) == 1 and ast.unparse(value.args[0]) == reference, (\n                f\"{filename}:{write.lineno}: settings must serialize the shared {reference}\"\n            )\n",
