It gives the reviews to Codex and GLM: the spec review\n  and the review to Codex, the loop between implementation and phase 6 to\n  GLM, and, since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3\n  Flash.\n* **The maintainer decided otherwise on 2026-10-07** (bead\n  coding-harness-ymx): the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go with a fixed\n  ladder of three models for its rounds. On 2026-10-08 the maintainer put\n  the ladder to the loop alone — the spec review and the review stay with\n  Codex, because Codex's phase 6 found two real BLOCKERs in a change the\n  loop had passed, as on every change of the night run — and, the same day,\n  named Pi as the program that starts each round (\"ich möchte pi nutzen\"),\n  the OpenAI-compatible address as its path, and accepted the residual risk\n  of OpenCode's terms. Without this record the runner's declaration of\n  `opencode-go` would run against ADR 0007's decision 2, which is a decision\n  nobody made.\n* **What OpenCode Go is** (`plans/changes/stage2-mimo/research.md` §E to\n  §K, read 2026-10-07; §Q, read 2026-10-08): OpenCode (Operator Anomaly\n  Inn",

          "excerpt": "# Spec — stage2-session\n\nStart a declared interactive Pi (for OpenCode Go models) or Codex session from\none checked runner invocation, in the change's worktree, with an auditable\nhandover. Research and settled instructions: `research.md`, `decisions.md`\n(coding-harness-amp). Since 2026-10-09 the OpenCode Go path launches Pi, not\nthe OpenCode CLI (maintainer, German: \"ich will keine opencode mehr\nbenutzen\"; answers Q-1 to Q-6 in `decisions.md`). The OpenCode Go service and\nits endpoint declaration are unchanged.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe runner has no interactive launch verb on main at `1c79860`. Direct TUI\nlaunches skip its declaration, prompt scan and audit. Budget takeover must\nnot open a second unchecked entry point. The Flash runner (`11abf42`,\nPR #89), which changes the same file, is on main (read 2026-10-09). Pi asks for no approval and has no sandbox\n(`docs/security.md` of the pinned Pi 1.1.0), so the repository must supply\nthe session policy itself, as an extension loaded explicitly by the runner\n(`research.md`, addendum of 2026-10-09).\n\n## Terms\n\n- **Dispatch:** Terminal accepted the launch command; not evidence that the\n  CLI started, model authenticated, answered, finished the workflow or passed\n  verification. Executables must exist at preflight; later startup failures\n  appear in the new window.\n- **Launch snapshot:** the state scanned before dispatch, not later edits,\n  later prompts or later UI model switches.\n\n## Supported models and prerequisites\n\nThe currently usable positive path is `--model gpt-6.1-sol`, through the\ndeclared `openai-codex` endpoint and official Codex CLI. The Pi path accepts\n`opencode-go/<model>` only when the `opencode-go` endpoint lists that model\nfor framework content in `model-endpoints.yaml` (declared by ADR 0011; the\nid names the endpoint, not the launcher, Q-5).           "excerpt": "## Consequences\n\n- The scan covers launch only, with existing exclusions; later edits/prompts,\n  approved arbitrary shell code and UI model/agent changes are not scanned.\n  Another model re-enters through the runner.\n- This change approves no new endpoint, credential or review order; the\n  `opencode-go` declaration is ADR 0011's.\n- Initial support is macOS Terminal only, with no silent fallback.\n- The proof of the policy is weaker than OpenCode's read-back: a bug in the\n  extension that its tests miss is not seen at launch.\n- Only dangerous `bash` patterns ask; a command outside the list runs unasked.\n- `~/.pi/agent` may hold other providers' credentials, so a model switched\n  inside the session can leave the declared endpoint unscanned.\n- `.git/` stays writable for the session.\n- Bead coding-harness-0al (the OpenCode 2.x failure) is superseded: no\n  `opencode` call remains.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "# Draft ADR 0007 amendment — interactive sessions use the checked runner\n\nStatus: moved on 2026-10-10 into the decision record `docs/adr/0012-interactive-stage-2-sessions-run-through-the-checked-runner.md` (ADR 0012), which the merge of its pull request accepts. Interactive foreign sessions start\nonly through `python3 scripts/stage2.py session <change> --model <id>` in the\ncanonical worktree.           "end_line": 40,
          "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(not for a spike)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | a current review of the spec, no open `[AMBIGUITY]`; at most three spec-review rounds — the final draft after round three needs no new review, a fourth round only by a recorded maintainer answer |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one.           "citation": "AGENTS.md::The workflow in one screen",
          "end_line": 40,
          "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(not for a spike)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | a current review of the spec, no open `[AMBIGUITY]`; at most three spec-review rounds — the final draft after round three needs no new review, a fourth round only by a recorded maintainer answer |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one. GLM 5.3 Flash explores a `bounded` change or a `spike` (a `feature` or `architectural` change goes to the research swarm, ADR 0020) and implements, and Codex repairs the findings the orchestrator takes (`repair <change>`, ADR 0017: a fresh Codex attempt after a failed post-run check, then Sonnet 5.5; phase 6 re-checks in a fresh read-only Codex session — a reviewer's own session never repairs); `explore <change>`, `draft <change>`, `implement <change>` and `repair <change>` are live;\n`--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 and records why when Stage 2 is off or Z.ai unavailable. A leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback. Reviews go by class, and so does phase 1 now (ADR 0020): a `feature` or `architectural` change explores through the research swarm (ADR 0020; a finder trio maps the sources, six seats research eleven topics, online topics on public sources only, Opus 5.5 reconciling; `prepare-explore <change>` first, its report shown to the maintainer, then `explore <change> --availability-reported <id>`; an aborted run resumes; the gate `research-handoff` holds interview and spec to the findings), a `bounded` change or a `spike` through GLM 5.3 Flash; `explore` reads the class from `--class` and the headers of `research.md` and `spec.md`, wherever stated, and refuses missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).           "excerpt": "def test_every_pi_settings_writer_uses_shared_constant() -> None:\n    \"\"\"One settings definition prevents discovery, reviews, probes and research from drifting.\n\n    Planting the old inline literal at any writer must fail even while its JSON\n    still matches today's content; the contract here is shared ownership.\n    \"\"\"\n    expected = {\n        \"stage2.py\": (2, \"PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"),\n        \"stage2_availability.py\": (1, \"runner.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"),\n        \"stage2_research_run.py\": (1, \"self.runner.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"),\n    }\n    assert hasattr(stage2, \"PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"), \"all Pi settings writers need one shared production constant\"\n    assert stage2.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS == {\"retry\": {\"enabled\": False}, \"compaction\": {\"enabled\": False}}\n    for filename, (count, reference) in expected.items():\n        tree = ast.parse((REPO_ROOT / \"scripts\" / filename).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        writes = [\n            node\n            for node in ast.walk(tree)\n            if isinstance(node, ast.Call)\n            and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute)\n            and node.func.attr == \"write_text\"\n            and isinstance(node.func.value, ast.BinOp)\n            and isinstance(node.func.value.right, ast.Constant)\n            and node.func.value.right.value == \"settings.json\"\n        ]\n        assert len(writes) == count, f\"{filename}: the settings writer inventory changed\"\n        for write in writes:\n            value = write.args[0]\n            assert isinstance(value, ast.Call) and ast.unparse(value.func) == \"json.dumps\", filename\n            assert len(value.args) == 1 and ast.unparse(value.args[0]) == reference, (\n                f\"{filename}:{write.lineno}: settings must serialize the shared {reference}\"\n            )\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_real_reviewer_tool_contract(project: Path, transport) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a real reviewer-shaped call declares exactly read,grep,find,ls; an undeclared tool cannot execute.\"\"\"\n    standin = StandIn(\n        [\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"read\", \"arguments\": {\"path\": \"sentinel.txt\"}}]},\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": f\"echo pwned >> {project / 'sentinel.txt'}\"}}]},\n            {\"content\": \"No finding.\"},\n        ]\n    )\n    transport.providers[\"opencode-go\"] = {\"baseUrl\": standin.url}\n    try:\n        answer = stage2.run_reviewer(\n            contract_ctx(project),\n            \"contract-rung\",\n            \"Review the change demo as the appended instructions say.\",\n            SYNTHETIC_KEY,\n        )\n        assert \"No finding.\" in answer, \"the scripted stop never reached the runner\"\n        assert len(standin.requests) == 3, f\"expected the scripted three turns, saw {len(standin.requests)}\"\n        declared = tool_names(standin.requests[0])\n        assert declared == {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, (\n            f\"the model saw {sorted(declared)}, not the four reviewer tools\"\n        )\n        assert SENTINEL_IN in message_text(standin.requests[1]), \"the positive control read never executed\"\n        for exchange in standin.requests:\n            assert tool_names(exchange) <= {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, \"a foreign tool was declared\"\n        assert (project / \"sentinel.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == SENTINEL_IN + \"\\n\", (\n            \"an undeclared tool changed the sentinel\"\n        )\n    finally:\n        standin.close()\n    # the launch was the runner's own construction, through the wrapper, under the guard\n    (call,) = transport.calls\n    assert call[\"argv\"][0] == str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"the reviewer did not start through the repository wrapper\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--tools\") + 1] == \"read,grep,find,ls\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--model\") + 1] == \"opencode-go/contract-rung\"\n    assert \"NODE_OPTIONS\" in call[\"env\"] and \"pi_network_guard\" in call[\"env\"][\"NODE_OPTIONS\"]\n    assert call[\"env\"][\"OPENCODE_API_KEY\"] == SYNTHETIC_KEY\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_pi(\n    project: Path,\n    scratch: Path,\n    *args: str,\n    key: str = SYNTHETIC_KEY,\n    providers: dict | None = None,\n    timeout: int = 180,\n    env_extra: dict | None = None,\n) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    \"\"\"Start the actual pinned Pi through the repository wrapper, offline and guarded.\n\n    Scratch HOME and agent directory, a synthetic `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, the\n    network guard preloaded, the provider addresses repointed at a loopback\n    stand-in through the scratch `models.json` - the measured override seam.\n    \"\"\"\n    agent = scratch / \"agent\"\n    home = scratch / \"home\"\n    agent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    home.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # Use the runner's settings directly so helper launches follow `run_reviewer`.\n    (agent / \"settings.json\").write_text(json.dumps(stage2.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    if providers:\n        (agent / \"models.json\").write_text(json.dumps({\"providers\": providers}), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    env = {\n        **contract_environment(),\n        \"HOME\": str(home),\n        \"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": str(agent),\n        \"OPENCODE_API_KEY\": key,\n        \"NODE_OPTIONS\": f\"--import {GUARD}\",\n        **(env_extra or {}),\n    }\n    try:\n        return subprocess.run(\n            [str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), *args],\n            cwd=project,\n            env=env,\n            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n            capture_output=True,\n            text=True,\n            errors=\"replace\",\n            timeout=timeout,\n            check=False,\n        )\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:\n        raise ContractFailure(f\"Pi did not end within {timeout}s: {error}\") from None\n",

          "excerpt": "def repair(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4b and 6: Codex repairs every taken finding in one call, checked and committed by the runner.\n\n    The attempts are Codex, one fresh Codex repair attempt with the first one's diagnostics, and one\n    Sonnet 5.5 stage-1 fallback after two failed post-run checks; a failed call or a leak-check BLOCK\n    stops without a fallback (ADR 0017). The orchestrator decides taken or rejected and re-checks with\n    the loop's next round and `review`, a fresh read-only Codex session; the verb writes no\n    `Broke a test` and starts no review. Every selected row's `Origin` is checked before any call\n    or write, an older block's selected row included (bead coding-harness-3h96). A taken Status that\n    already names a fix in the old hand-written form (`; fixed by`, `; fixed:`, `; repaired by`)\n    refuses before any call.\n\n    A selected row whose `Where` names a path the checkpoint cannot commit is handed to the\n    orchestrator before any model call: the runner reports it with the reason `runner-held path`,\n    appends the dated hand-step listing to findings.md once, and leaves the row's Status and\n    `Broke a test` cells unchanged (bead coding-harness-0zhf). Every row held, the existing\n    checkpoint commits that listing and the run exits 0 with no model call; a mixed batch dispatches\n    only the committable rows, names the held ones in the commit body, and ignores answer lines that\n    mention them.\n    \"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else CODEX\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    record = read_record(change, root)\n    current = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n    resolved = resolve_finding_rows(record, current)\n    taken, waiting = repair_targets(ctx, record, current, resolved=resolved)\n    if waiting:\n        raise Refused(f\"rows are waiting for a decision ({', '.join(waiting)}); decide them first.\")\n    # Both checks share the resolver's current rows. The target check covers older selected\n    # rows too; the shared check retains its scope without re-admitting superseded history.\n    target_refusal = target_origin_refusal(record, current, resolved=resolved)\n    if target_refusal:\n        raise Refused(target_refusal)\n    refusal = origin_refusal(record, current, resolved=resolved)\n    if refusal:\n        raise Refused(refusal)\n    if not taken:\n        raise Refused(\"no row is taken; nothing to repair.\")\n    legacy = [row[0] for _, row in taken if legacy_completed(row[7])]\n    if legacy:\n        # A legacy marker may name a completed fix or merely occur in an unrepaired reason.\n        # Refuse without rewriting and explain both corrections (spec, criterion 7).\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"rows carry a taken status that already names a fix ({', '.join(legacy)}); book the hand repair \"\n            \"by replacing the Status with `fixed — tests/<path>:",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_send_rechecks_current_policy(world, monkeypatch, capsys):\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a saved selection, resumed round, replacement or retry dispatches no now-refused base.\n\n    Fault: an old receipt or saved overlay authorized the send; here the\n    record turns hostile after every preparation and nothing dispatches.\n    \"\"\"\n    model = TEST_LADDER[0]\n    harness = Harness(world, monkeypatch)\n    store = go_store(row(model))\n    seat_lines: list[str] = []\n    seat = harness.seat(model, store, seat_lines)\n    probe_call, _audit = harness.probe(model, store)\n    prepared = [harness.reviewer(model, store), harness.reviewer(model, store, free=True), probe_call, seat]\n    for call in prepared:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        call()\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(prepared), \"preparation itself failed\"\n    history = (list(harness.sent), list(seat_lines))\n    # The record turns hostile after preparation: no saved evidence dispatches.\n    edit_entry(world, lambda e: e[\"adresse\"].update({\"host\": \"elsewhere.invalid\"}))\n    for call in prepared:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        with pytest.raises((stage2.Refused, stage2_go.DestinationRefused)) as raised:\n            call()\n        assert \"not the admitted host\" in str(raised.value)\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused):\n        harness.swarm(model, store)()\n    assert (list(harness.sent), list(seat_lines)) == history, \"earlier completed history was rewritten\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_model_in_the_routing_table_resolves() -> None:\n    \"\"\"The doctrine names models too, and they must resolve as well.\n\n    Otherwise the rule holds for agent definitions and not for the table from\n    which a person picks a model.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    tabelle = routing_models(text)\n    assert tabelle, \"no model found in the routing of docs/WORKFLOW.md (RB-G7)\"\n    # The table names display names (\"Haiku 4.5\"), the declaration ids.\n    ids = zugelassene_modelle()\n    for anzeige in tabelle:\n        if anzeige in {\"the ladder\", \"the swarms, then the ladder\", \"none (a local command)\"}:\n            continue  # a local command has no model; ladder ids are checked in the endpoint declaration\n        if anzeige == \"the research swarm\":\n            # No single model id: the swarm is a declared role roster. The row\n            # resolves only while the declaration itself is complete and every\n            # id it names sits on its declared endpoint.\n            assert swarm_block_problems(_erklaerung()) == [], (\n                \"docs/WORKFLOW.md routes to 'the research swarm', but the declared swarm is incomplete\"\n            )\n            continue\n        assert _loest_auf(anzeige, ids), (\n            f\"docs/WORKFLOW.md routes to '{anzeige}', which no endpoint lists. \"\n            f\"Looked for: {' or '.join(sorted(_kandidaten(anzeige)))}\"\n        )\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_new_paid_model_carries_its_terms_reading() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a paid model is admitted only with a dated terms reading or a dated skip.\n\n    Every `modelle` id holds a `modelle_terms` record; an admitted one carries\n    the date and the source of the retention/training reading, a skipped one\n    its date and reason - so no paid model is silently omitted.\n    \"\"\"\n    entry = _endpunkt(\"opencode-go\")\n    modelle = entry.get(\"modelle\") or []\n    assert modelle and len(modelle) == len(set(modelle))\n    terms = entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {}\n    admitted, skipped = [], []\n    for model in modelle:\n        record = terms.get(model) or {}\n        if record.get(\"uebersprungen\"):\n            assert record.get(\"grund\"), f\"{model} is skipped without its reason\"\n            assert re.fullmatch(r\"\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\", str(record[\"uebersprungen\"]))\n            skipped.append(model)\n            continue\n        assert record.get(\"gelesen\"), f\"{model} has no dated terms reading and no skip\"\n        assert re.fullmatch(r\"\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\", str(record[\"gelesen\"]))\n        assert record.get(\"quelle\"), f\"{model} names no source for its terms reading\"\n        assert record.get(\"training\") == \"Not used\", f\"{model} permits training or leaves it unread\"\n        assert record.get(\"aufbewahrung\"), f\"{model} leaves retention unread\"\n        admitted.append(model)\n    assert set(admitted) | set(skipped) == set(modelle)\n\n    import sys\n\n    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"scripts\"))\n    import stage2\n\n    # Q-13: every ladder model declares its dated cost value; the runner's ladder follows it, cheapest first.\n    terms = entry[\"modelle_terms\"]\n    for model in admitted:\n        record = terms[model]\n        value = record.get(\"anfragen_5h\")\n        assert isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0, f\"{model}: no cost value\"\n        assert re.fullmatch(r\"\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\", str(record.get(\"anfragen_gelesen\"))), f\"{model}: no reading date\"\n        assert \"opencode.ai/docs/go\" in str(record.get(\"anfragen_quelle\")), f\"{model}: no source\"\n    order = stage2.ordered_models(entry, admitted)\n    values = [terms[model][\"anfragen_5h\"] for model in order]\n    assert values == sorted(values, reverse=True), \"the ladder is not cheapest first\"\n    assert set(order) == set(admitted)\n    # The hand-kept Flash swarm may drift as new cheaper models are declared.\n    notice = stage2.cheapest_notice(entry, order, entry[\"flash_swarm\"])\n    assert bool(notice) == (set(entry[\"flash_swarm\"]) != set(order[:3]))",

          "excerpt": "def run_pi(\n    project: Path,\n    scratch: Path,\n    *args: str,\n    key: str = SYNTHETIC_KEY,\n    providers: dict | None = None,\n    timeout: int = 180,\n    env_extra: dict | None = None,\n) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    \"\"\"Start the actual pinned Pi through the repository wrapper, offline and guarded.\n\n    Scratch HOME and agent directory, a synthetic `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, the\n    network guard preloaded, the provider addresses repointed at a loopback\n    stand-in through the scratch `models.json` - the measured override seam.\n    \"\"\"\n    agent = scratch / \"agent\"\n    home = scratch / \"home\"\n    agent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    home.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # Use the runner's settings directly so helper launches follow `run_reviewer`.\n    (agent / \"settings.json\").write_text(json.dumps(stage2.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    if providers:\n        (agent / \"models.json\").write_text(json.dumps({\"providers\": providers}), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    env = {\n        **contract_environment(),\n        \"HOME\": str(home),\n        \"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": str(agent),\n        \"OPENCODE_API_KEY\": key,\n        \"NODE_OPTIONS\": f\"--import {GUARD}\",\n        **(env_extra or {}),\n    }\n    try:\n        return subprocess.run(\n            [str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), *args],\n            cwd=project,\n            env=env,\n            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n            capture_output=True,\n            text=True,\n            errors=\"replace\",\n            timeout=timeout,\n            check=False,\n        )\n    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:\n        raise ContractFailure(f\"Pi did not end within {timeout}s: {error}\") from None\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_real_reviewer_tool_contract(project: Path, transport) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a real reviewer-shaped call declares exactly read,grep,find,ls; an undeclared tool cannot execute.\"\"\"\n    standin = StandIn(\n        [\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"read\", \"arguments\": {\"path\": \"sentinel.txt\"}}]},\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": f\"echo pwned >> {project / 'sentinel.txt'}\"}}]},\n            {\"content\": \"No finding.\"},\n        ]\n    )\n    transport.providers[\"opencode-go\"] = {\"baseUrl\": standin.url}\n    try:\n        answer = stage2.run_reviewer(\n            contract_ctx(project),\n            \"contract-rung\",\n            \"Review the change demo as the appended instructions say.\",\n            SYNTHETIC_KEY,\n        )\n        assert \"No finding.\" in answer, \"the scripted stop never reached the runner\"\n        assert len(standin.requests) == 3, f\"expected the scripted three turns, saw {len(standin.requests)}\"\n        declared = tool_names(standin.requests[0])\n        assert declared == {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, (\n            f\"the model saw {sorted(declared)}, not the four reviewer tools\"\n        )\n        assert SENTINEL_IN in message_text(standin.requests[1]), \"the positive control read never executed\"\n        for exchange in standin.requests:\n            assert tool_names(exchange) <= {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, \"a foreign tool was declared\"\n        assert (project / \"sentinel.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == SENTINEL_IN + \"\\n\", (\n            \"an undeclared tool changed the sentinel\"\n        )\n    finally:\n        standin.close()\n    # the launch was the runner's own construction, through the wrapper, under the guard\n    (call,) = transport.calls\n    assert call[\"argv\"][0] == str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"the reviewer did not start through the repository wrapper\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--tools\") + 1] == \"read,grep,find,ls\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--model\") + 1] == \"opencode-go/contract-rung\"\n    assert \"NODE_OPTIONS\" in call[\"env\"] and \"pi_network_guard\" in call[\"env\"][\"NODE_OPTIONS\"]\n    assert call[\"env\"][\"OPENCODE_API_KEY\"] == SYNTHETIC_KEY\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_pi_off_the_pin_is_refused(\n    world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], verb: str, fault: dict | str\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 27: a Pi that is not exactly the pinned version starts no leak check, no call line and no call.\"\"\"\n    manifest = json.loads((REPO_ROOT / \"tools\" / \"pi\" / \"package.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    assert manifest[\"dependencies\"][\"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent\"] == stage2.PI_VERSION, (\n        \"the runner's pin must be the manifest's, not a literal of its own\"\n    )\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"PI_VERSION_SECONDS\", 0.5)\n    programs = None\n    steps = {\"pi\": [{\"stdout\": rows(1)}] * 3}\n    if fault == \"absent\":\n        (world.bin / \"pin-pi\").unlink()\n        world.script(**steps)\n    elif fault == \"too-slow\":\n        # A probe past the pin limit is stopped at the injected expiry, never waited out on the\n        # machine: the doubled communicate raises what a hung wrapper would have caused.\n        clock = FakeClock(monkeypatch, UTC_START)\n        version_argv = [str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"]\n        plans = [(lambda command: command == version_argv, {\"duration\": 30.0})]\n        programs = ScriptedPrograms(monkeypatch, clock, plans)\n        world.script(**steps)\n    else:\n        world.script(**steps, **fault)\n    assert world.run(verb) == 2, \"a Pi off the pin must refuse with exit 2\"\n    if programs is not None:\n        (handed,) = programs.waits([str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"])\n        assert handed[\"timeout\"] == 0.5 and handed[\"outcome\"] == \"timeout\", handed\n    assert world.calls() == [], \"a call started\"\n    assert not world.record().exists()\n    text = world.text() if world.findings.exists() else \"\"\n    assert text.count(\"Stage-2 call,\") <= 1, \"a call line was written\"\n    assert \"leak check\" not in capsys.readouterr().out.lower(), \"the leak check ran before the pin\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_pi_settings_writer_uses_shared_constant() -> None:\n    \"\"\"One settings definition prevents discovery, reviews, probes and research from drifting.\n\n    Planting the old inline literal at any writer must fail even while its JSON\n    still matches today's content; the contract here is shared ownership.\n    \"\"\"\n    expected = {\n        \"stage2.py\": (2, \"PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"),\n        \"stage2_availability.py\": (1, \"runner.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"),\n        \"stage2_research_run.py\": (1, \"self.runner.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"),\n    }\n    assert hasattr(stage2, \"PI_AGENT_SETTINGS\"), \"all Pi settings writers need one shared production constant\"\n    assert stage2.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS == {\"retry\": {\"enabled\": False}, \"compaction\": {\"enabled\": False}}\n    for filename, (count, reference) in expected.items():\n        tree = ast.parse((REPO_ROOT / \"scripts\" / filename).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        writes = [\n            node\n            for node in ast.walk(tree)\n            if isinstance(node, ast.Call)\n            and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute)\n            and node.func.attr == \"write_text\"\n            and isinstance(node.func.value, ast.BinOp)\n            and isinstance(node.func.value.right, ast.Constant)\n            and node.func.value.right.value == \"settings.json\"\n        ]\n        assert len(writes) == count, f\"{filename}: the settings writer inventory changed\"\n        for write in writes:\n            value = write.args[0]\n            assert isinstance(value, ast.Call) and ast.unparse(value.func) == \"json.dumps\", filename\n            assert len(value.args) == 1 and ast.unparse(value.args[0]) == reference, (\n                f\"{filename}:{write.lineno}: settings must serialize the shared {reference}\"\n            )\n",

          "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses.           "excerpt": "def remove_changed_credential(\n    root: Path,\n    key: str,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None = None,\n    against: str = \"HEAD\",\n    findings: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[Path]:\n    \"\"\"Remove an exact GLM credential from changed regular files and name those files.\n\n    \"Changed\" is tracked changes, untracked files, and - when the run's earlier snapshot of the\n    gitignored files is given - every ignored file created or touched since that snapshot. A skip does not establish whether the path holds a credential.\n    \"\"\"\n    paths = changed_paths(root, against=against)\n    if ignored_before is not None:\n        paths |= {p for p, stat in ignored_snapshot(root).items() if ignored_before.get(p) != stat}\n    # Scanning is not recovery: skip unsafe parents without reading or writing\n    # through them, while retaining credential removal in contained files.\n    found = []\n    for relative in sorted(paths, key=lambda path: path.as_posix()):\n        path = root / relative\n        problem = restoration_parent_problem(root, path)\n        if problem is not None:\n            diagnostic = protect_diagnostics(\n                f\"credential scan skipped {relative.as_posix()}: its parent {problem}; contents were not inspected\",\n                key,\n            )\n            print(diagnostic, file=sys.stderr)\n            record_credential_scan_skips(root, findings, [diagnostic], key)\n            continue\n        if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():\n            continue\n        try:\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n        except OSError:\n            continue\n        if not credential_spans(content, key):\n            continue\n        path.write_bytes(replace_credential(content, key))\n        found.append(relative)\n    return found\n",

          "excerpt": "def protect_diagnostics(text: str, key: str | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"`text` as failed-check diagnostics may be published: secret-rule matches redacted, the key scrubbed.\n\n    Every secret rule of the active denylist is read now, on every route - a keyless Codex or Stage-1 route\n    included. A match is replaced in place by `[<rule name>]` (the name already starts `secret:`); the spans\n    are found in the original text, overlapping ones merge with credential spans into one marker run, and the\n    replacement keeps the line breaks it covered, so a traceback keeps its shape. Known credentials are\n    protected with their credential marker. Every rule reads the original text, before any replacement,\n    in full and line by line to preserve multiline and anchored matches; a match wholly inside the known\n    credential is left to the credential marker. Non-secret rules refuse first\n    - redaction must not hide a blocking rule - and so does a denylist that cannot be read, or\n    text that still matches a secret rule after the replacement. A refusal names a rule or a reason and a\n    line, never a value.\n    \"\"\"\n    return _protect_diagnostics(text, key)[0]\n",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). Before the failure is decided, findings.md is restored outright: every post-run check, cheap\n    or full, reads the runner's file, an edit alone fails nothing, and a completed attempt that edited\n    it carries a quoted restore notice under its audit line (spec, criteria 8 and 9).\n\n    A verb that passes `retain_answer` keeps every attempt's full answer: right at the model-return\n    boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can stop the run, the protected\n    answer is saved as local evidence and its location joins the attempt's diagnostics - the parser's\n    rejections, the call and verify failures included - and is printed on success (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). A failed call keeps the output it returned.\n\n    A verb that passes `protect_lifecycle` snapshots the change's lifecycle fields (`status`,\n    `implementation_status`) in spec, optional design and plan right before every call. Once the\n    attempt's changed-file measurement stands, changed effective values restore the trusted whole\n    frontmatter block, preserving body edits and YAML anchors - before verification, the\n    derived preparation or the checkpoint reads the documents. The same per-attempt snapshot serves\n    the early exits: a failed call and a retry recover whole snapshotted inputs, a moved HEAD keeps\n    its commit while the safe working-tree fields go back, a refused checkpoint puts the fields back\n    before the run stops, and every attempt's bookkeeping names what was restored or says the fields\n    stayed unchanged (status-fields-restore). A deleted document or an unreadable header is the\n    existing snapshotted-input recovery's to repair; the attempt is rejected, never accepted on\n    invented surrounding content.\n\n    The failed-check listing and the changed-file entries pass through `protect_diagnostics` once, on\n    every route, the keyless ones included; the block in findings.md and the retry prompt both take that\n    one safe text, so a fixture secret a check printed blocks neither the next attempt's l",

          "end_line": 2391,
          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "excerpt": "def require_pi() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Refuse unless the repository wrapper prints exactly the pinned version (spec, criterion 27).\n\n    The wrapper is the one path to Pi (ADR 0019): it refuses a missing,\n    mismatched or unusable local install before any model request, and this\n    check ties its answer to the manifest pin. Runs before the prompt check,\n    the call line and any call, in a scratch directory with no key: a Pi off\n    the pin sends nothing. The session verb calls it after its argument and\n    handover checks.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        env = foreign_env({\"HOME\": tmp, \"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": tmp})\n        try:\n            done = launch(\n                [str(PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"],\n                Path(tmp),\n                env,\n                timeout=PI_VERSION_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the version check's limit of {PI_VERSION_SECONDS} seconds\",\n            )\n        except CallFailed as error:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"{PI_WRAPPER} could not be checked ({error}); it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\"\n            ) from None\n    said = (done.stdout or \"\").strip()\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        # The wrapper's own refusal names the defect; its last lines travel with this one.\n        tail = \"\\n\".join((done.stderr or \"\").splitlines()[-5:])\n        detail = f\": {tail}\" if tail else \"\"\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"{PI_WRAPPER} --version ended {done.returncode}; it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; \"\n            f\"no call starts{detail}.\"\n        )\n    if said != PI_VERSION:\n        raise Refused(f\"pi {said or 'printed nothing'} is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_pi_off_the_pin_is_refused(\n    world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], verb: str, fault: dict | str\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 27: a Pi that is not exactly the pinned version starts no leak check, no call line and no call.\"\"\"\n    manifest = json.loads((REPO_ROOT / \"tools\" / \"pi\" / \"package.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    assert manifest[\"dependencies\"][\"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent\"] == stage2.PI_VERSION, (\n        \"the runner's pin must be the manifest's, not a literal of its own\"\n    )\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"PI_VERSION_SECONDS\", 0.5)\n    programs = None\n    steps = {\"pi\": [{\"stdout\": rows(1)}] * 3}\n    if fault == \"absent\":\n        (world.bin / \"pin-pi\").unlink()\n        world.script(**steps)\n    elif fault == \"too-slow\":\n        # A probe past the pin limit is stopped at the injected expiry, never waited out on the\n        # machine: the doubled communicate raises what a hung wrapper would have caused.\n        clock = FakeClock(monkeypatch, UTC_START)\n        version_argv = [str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"]\n        plans = [(lambda command: command == version_argv, {\"duration\": 30.0})]\n        programs = ScriptedPrograms(monkeypatch, clock, plans)\n        world.script(**steps)\n    else:\n        world.script(**steps, **fault)\n    assert world.run(verb) == 2, \"a Pi off the pin must refuse with exit 2\"\n    if programs is not None:\n        (handed,) = programs.waits([str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"])\n        assert handed[\"timeout\"] == 0.5 and handed[\"outcome\"] == \"timeout\", handed\n    assert world.calls() == [], \"a call started\"\n    assert not world.record().exists()\n    text = world.text() if world.findings.exists() else \"\"\n    assert text.count(\"Stage-2 call,\") <= 1, \"a call line was written\"\n    assert \"leak check\" not in capsys.readouterr().out.lower(), \"the leak check ran before the pin\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_new_paid_model_carries_its_terms_reading() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a paid model is admitted only with a dated terms reading or a dated skip.\n\n    Every `modelle` id holds a `modelle_terms` record; an admitted one carries\n    the date and the source of the retention/training reading, a skipped one\n    its date and reason - so no paid model is silently omitted.\n    \"\"\"\n    entry = _endpunkt(\"opencode-go\")\n    modelle = entry.get(\"modelle\") or []\n    assert modelle and len(modelle) == len(set(modelle))\n    terms = entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {}\n    admitted, skipped = [], []\n    for model in modelle:\n        record = terms.get(model) or {}\n        if record.get(\"uebersprungen\"):\n            assert record.get(\"grund\"), f\"{model} is skipped without its reason\"\n            assert re.fullmatch(r\"\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\", str(record[\"uebersprungen\"]))\n            skipped.append(model)\n            continue\n        assert record.get(\"gelesen\"), f\"{model} has no dated terms reading and no skip\"\n        assert re.fullmatch(r\"\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\", str(record[\"gelesen\"]))\n        assert record.get(\"quelle\"), f\"{model} names no source for its terms reading\"\n        assert record.get(\"training\") == \"Not used\", f\"{model} permits training or leaves it unread\"\n        assert record.get(\"aufbewahrung\"), f\"{model} leaves retention unread\"\n        admitted.append(model)\n    assert set(admitted) | set(skipped) == set(modelle)\n\n    import sys\n\n    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"scripts\"))\n    import stage2\n\n    # Q-13: every ladder model declares its dated cost value; the runner's ladder follows it, cheapest first.\n    terms = entry[\"modelle_terms\"]\n    for model in admitted:\n        record = terms[model]\n        value = record.get(\"anfragen_5h\")\n        assert isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0, f\"{model}: no cost value\"\n        assert re.fullmatch(r\"\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\", str(record.get(\"anfragen_gelesen\"))), f\"{model}: no reading date\"\n        assert \"opencode.ai/docs/go\" in str(record.get(\"anfragen_quelle\")), f\"{model}: no source\"\n    order = stage2.ordered_models(entry, admitted)\n    values = [terms[model][\"anfragen_5h\"] for model in order]\n    assert values == sorted(values, reverse=True), \"the ladder is not cheapest first\"\n    assert set(order) == set(admitted)\n    # The hand-kept Flash swarm may drift as new cheaper models are declared.\n    notice = stage2.cheapest_notice(entry, order, entry[\"flash_swarm\"])\n    assert bool(notice) == (set(entry[\"flash_swarm\"]) != set(order[:3]))\n",

          "end_line": 95,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: ",

    "171fb2185a25edcf71d8281f0eb4d3c2626eccc7": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-09T13:56:58Z",
      "body": "Work package 4 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi. An\nopencode-go/<model> id names the endpoint; it now starts the pinned Pi in the\nTerminal window, with discovery off and one policy extension loaded from a copy\nin the session's private directory, the declared model, and the prompt after\n`--`. The runner checks the pin with require_pi, confirms by `pi --help` in a\nscratch home that the extension's flag is listed, and refuses otherwise,\nremoving what it made. It hands over no key and sets no agent directory: Pi\nsigns in from the maintainer's own ~/.pi/agent (Q-6). A prompt that starts with\n@ is refused, because Pi would read it as a file name.\n\nThe seven OpenCode-only functions, AGENT and GUARDED are gone. The tests get a\npi stand-in beside codex and osascript, and an opencode stand-in that must\nnever be called; the 25 canned effective-policy answers are replaced by tests of\nthe version pin, the read-back, the @ prompt, the scratch home and the absence\nof a key. 19 planted faults in the runner all turn a test red.\n\nDocuments that describe the verb to a reader still say OpenCode until package 5.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",

    "821c248d484c4802053a5837203fecacc1252e4a": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-14T00:02:33Z",
      "body": "Orchestrator hand implementation after three rejected runner attempts (two\npost-run checks red, the third model call ended with exit 1), approved by\nthe maintainer on 2026-11-13. Second step on top of e2c8657d.\n\nCode:\n- stage2: a gate command without shell syntax starts as its own argument\n  vector (the world's `make verify`, the docs subset's `bash\n  scripts/verify_all.sh --job docs`); anything else runs through `bash -c`.\n  Each gate gets timeout=VERIFY_SECONDS cut to the shared deadline. A gate\n  program found only through a PATH entry inside the worktree is resolved\n  without it (O188-2, as `make verify` was); the cheap checks keep the\n  verify environment (state root, memory floor) outside the admission.\n- verify_run: `admission_command` names the check in the holder record\n  (Stage 2 passes `make verify` or the docs vector); the hard-coded cache\n  directory names are gone (decisions Q-5: no tool or path outside the one\n  gate list) — git's ignore rules leave the caches out.\n- kit manifest: the new scheduler's reason in English.\n- docs/WORKFLOW.md: an unmeasurable or changing tree refuses the run.\n- plan.md: criterion ledger entries no longer \"not yet written\".\n\nExisting tests changed because the spec changes the behaviour they pin\n(criteria 9 and 10: the scheduler frames every gate, Stage 2 takes no\nwhole-run admission, the docs subset is a seconds member of the verify job):\n- the repair-prompt frame tests: the gate that blocked is proved with three\n  gates the scheduler frames itself; the noisy run is bounded by the\n  per-gate window; the tail fallback is proved on verify_evidence_text; the\n  frame guard reads verify_run.py.\n- the call-sequence and review call-count tests count the docs gate the\n  full check now runs; the draft's document check carries no admission\n  marker; ruff's environment equals the gate's minus the scheduler's own\n  additions; the refused-docs case rebases its commit count after the\n  test's own commit.\n- the attempt's new budget/timeout tests: the queue-wait spy measures at\n  admission entry (the wait happens there), and the outside-timeout proof\n  holds the queue 2.5 s so a charged wait would still exceed the limit.\n- every new test names its planted fault in its docstring.\n\nChecked: ruff check/format clean; tests/test_stage2.py 1841 passed,\n1 skipped (335 s); the direct test files plus tests/test_ci.py 284 passed,\n2 skipped; kit probe --strict exit 0 (1391 of 1435 cases carry);\nci_gates --check-schema and --check-ci green; criterion ledger,\nfrontmatter and plans registry green.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "821c248d484c4802053a5837203fecacc1252e4a",

    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,

    "d225f50d1ef4364395547863788297ef0959eaf3": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-09T13:12:52Z",
      "body": "Work package 3 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi. Pi asks\nfor no approval and has no sandbox, so the runner has to supply the policy: a\nplain ESM extension, scripts/stage2_session_policy.mjs, that the runner will\ncopy into the session's private directory and load explicitly.\n\nIt keeps read, grep, find, ls, edit and write inside the worktree as Pi\nresolves a path (a leading @, ~, file://, symlinks), keeps edit and write off\nits own file, .stage2-sessions/ and .pi/, asks before a dangerous bash command\nand blocks it when no UI can ask, blocks when its own handler fails, and\nregisters a flag that `pi --help` lists, which is how the runner will confirm\nthe load. 200 cases run it through a node driver without Pi and without a\nmodel; 25 planted faults, one rule removed each, all turn a test red. The\nfirst run caught `git -C . push` running unasked; the patterns now allow\nglobal git options before the verb.\n\nThe runner does not use the extension yet (package 4); nothing in\nscripts/stage2_session.py changes.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "d225f50d1ef4364395547863788297ef0959eaf3",
      "subject": "feat(stage2-session): add the policy extension of a Pi session and its tests",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/stage2_session_policy.mjs",
        "tests/test_stage2_session_policy.py"
      ]
    },

      "body": "Main (bead coding-harness-wb40) moved the research swarm's free selection\ninto the shared `stage2_free.select`, which keeps a drift notice only for an\neligible id. This branch requires every address-admissible candidate's notice\nto reach `address_notices` before any eligibility filter, each model once\n(spec criterion 3).\n\nResolution in `select_research_catalog`: main's shared selection stays the one\nrule (paid admission, declaration exclusion, destination refusal); the branch's\n`collect_notice` still runs for every free candidate before that selection, and\nthe selection's own notices are merged without repeats. `stage2_free.select` is\nunchanged: the review loop takes its notices from `activate_overlay`, which\nalready sees every row before selection, so the research swarm is the only\ncaller that needed the guarantee. Changing the shared module would have changed\nits documented contract for both callers without need.\n\nTests: the branch's two research-catalog calls pass main's new required\n`paid=()` and `exclusion=None`, as main did for the existing calls. A new test\ncovers the case only the merge creates: a `-free` row vetoed as paid-admitted\nby the shared selection keeps its notice, once (it fails without the\npre-filter collection). No test from either side was weakened or removed.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9FFLqLWsj1biQidvPo\n",

      "body": "The shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py) behind\nscripts/verify_all.sh and Stage 2: every unprotected (seconds) gate runs\nbefore admission and all red ones are reported together; only protected\ngates (cost minutes, or needs_admission) run under one admission; an\nunchanged tree reuses the cheap results, a changed one reruns them.\n\nOrchestrator hand implementation after three rejected runner attempts (two\npost-run checks red, the third model call ended with exit 1), approved by\nthe maintainer on 2026-11-13. (B): the stop\n  at the first blocking gate is now proved among minutes gates, since the\n  cheap phase runs through every seconds gate (decisions Q-3).\n- the attempt's other changes to tests/test_ci.py, test_verify_cheap_first,\n  test_gate_catalog and test_stage2 (cost classes in fixtures, a git HEAD\n  for the tree measurement, the admission column, no whole-run admission\n  for the seconds-only document subset) follow the same spec criteria 2,\n  3, 5 and 10.\n\nChecked: ruff check and format clean over scripts/ and tests/; the new and\ndirectly touched test files 105 passed; tests/test_ci.py 179 passed,\n2 skipped.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

          "excerpt": "def repair_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    baseline: str,\n    taken: list[tuple[str, list[str]]],\n    diagnostics: list[str],\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None] = CODEX,\n    inputs: dict[Path, bytes] | None = None,\n    held_rows: list[tuple[str, list[str], list[str]]] | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The implement contract with the repair block: the format, the must-runs, the baseline, the rows.\"\"\"\n    rows = \"\\n\".join(f\"- {row[0]} [{row[1]}, {row[2]}] {row[4]}: {row[5]} — Status: {row[7]}\" for _, row in taken)\n    spec = prompt_input(ctx.folder / \"spec.md\", inputs)\n    plan = prompt_input(ctx.plan, inputs)\n    extra = [\n        REPAIR_FORMAT if endpoint == CODEX else REPAIR_FORMAT_FILE_TOOLS,\n        # A command-capable Codex runs the must-runs itself; the file-tools route delegates the same\n        # checks to the runner. The references come from the accepted plan's cached snapshot, so a retry rereads\n        # nothing the attempt may have edited (spec, criteria 13, 14 and 16).\n        \"## Must-run checks before handback\\n\\n\"\n        + (MUST_RUN_COMMANDS if endpoint == CODEX else MUST_RUN_DELEGATED_REPAIR)\n        + \"\\n\\nLedger tests:\\n\"\n        + repair_must_run_refs(ctx.root, plan.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        f\"Repair baseline: {baseline}\",\n        f\"## Taken rows\\n\\n{rows}\",\n        f\"## Accepted spec\\n\\n{spec}\",\n        f\"## Accepted plan\\n\\n{plan}\",\n    ]\n    if held_rows:\n        # The model is told the held rows are not its work (spec, criterion 18); the rows stay\n        # readable in the findings record it already receives.\n        ids = \", \".join(row[0] for _, row, _ in held_rows)\n        extra.append(\n            \"## Held rows — not your work\\n\\n\"\n            f\"The runner handed {ids} to the orchestrator before your call: each row's `Where` names \"\n            \"a path the runner does not commit. They are not your work: do not repair, answer or \"\n            \"book them, and answer only the taken rows above.\"\n        )\n    if diagnostics:\n        extra.append(\"## Earlier post-run diagnostics\\n\\n\" + \"\\n\\n\".join(diagnostics))\n    return work_prompt(ctx.root, \"04-implement.md\", ctx.change, \"\\n\\n\".join(extra), inputs)\n",

          "excerpt": "def terms_problem(entry: dict, model: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why the paid model's data terms are unread or no longer valid, or None when it is admitted.\n\n    A dated, sourced reading must explicitly rule out training and carry a\n    usable end date `valid_until`, valid through that UTC day; the following day\n    the reading is expired (bead coding-harness-abra). A dated skip keeps the\n    model out and names its reason for the handover (ADR 0021, decision 5).\n    The declared dates rule: the runner never infers, extends or renews one.\n    \"\"\"\n    record = _terms(entry, model)\n    problem = _reading_problem(record, model)\n    if problem:\n        return problem\n    retention = record.get(\"aufbewahrung\")\n    if not isinstance(retention, str) or not retention.strip():\n        return f\"the model {model} has no retention reading (aufbewahrung missing or unreadable)\"\n    if record.get(\"training\") != \"Not used\":\n        return f\"the model {model} has disallowed or unread training terms (training must be Not used)\"\n    return _expiry_problem(record, model)\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "end_line": 4650,
          "excerpt": "def run_fallback_review(\n    ctx: Context, config: dict, opus_failure: CallFailed\n) -> tuple[bytes, str, list[list[str]], str, tuple[str, str, str | None], object]:\n    \"\"\"The declared fallback review through Pi, after the Opus route failed twice (spec criteria 13-15).\n\n    The leak check runs first and a BLOCK still refuses - no fallback call starts. The\n    fallback reads the spec body fresh at its own call start, and the body on disk must still\n    be those bytes when the call ends. A failed or unreadable fallback fails the whole call.\n    \"\"\"\n    if config[\"fallback_model\"] is None:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the Opus review produced no readable review ({opus_failure}); no fallback model is declared \"\n            \"in model-endpoints.yaml's `spec_review` block, so no fallback call starts.\"\n        )\n    endpoint = (str(config[\"fallback_endpoint\"]), str(config[\"fallback_model\"]), None)\n    if endpoint[0] != OPENCODE:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the spec review's fallback endpoint must be {OPENCODE}, where the runner's Pi reviews; \"\n            f\"{endpoint[0]} is not.\"\n        )\n    problem = terms_problem(endpoint_entry(ctx.root), endpoint[1])\n    if problem is not None:\n        raise CallFailed(f\"the fallback review is not admitted on its declared terms: {problem}\")\n    require_committed_review_spec(ctx.root, ctx.change)\n    commit = _git_output(ctx.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    body = spec_body_bytes(ctx.folder / \"spec.md\")\n    if body != spec_body_of(_git_bytes(ctx.root, \"show\", f\"{commit}:plans/changes/{ctx.change}/spec.md\")):\n        raise CallFailed(\"the spec changed while the review snapshot was read.\")\n    prompt = spec_review_prompt(ctx.root, ctx.change, body)\n    result = checked_prompt(ctx, endpoint, prompt)\n    require_pi()\n    discovery = discover_free(ctx.root, allow_empty=True)\n    ctx.models_store = discovery.get(\"models_store\")\n    require_committed_review_spec(ctx.root, ctx.change)\n    try:\n        answer = run_reviewer(\n            ctx,\n            endpoint[1],\n            prompt,\n            reviewer_key(),\n            free=False,\n            timeout_seconds=int(config[\"timeout_seconds\"]),\n        )\n    except CallFailed as error:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the Opus review produced no readable review ({opus_failure}) and the fallback review \"\n            f\"failed too ({error}).\"\n        ) from error\n    rows = readable_review(answer)\n    if spec_body_bytes(ctx.folder / \"spec.md\") != body:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the spec body changed during the fallback review; no block is written for bytes the reviewer did not read.\"\n        )\n    return body, commit, rows, answer, endpoint, result\n",
