      "statement": "No existing code switches to another model when a declared `valid_until` lapses. `terms_problem` and `_expiry_problem` only refuse a model past its end date, `run_fallback_review` raises `CallFailed` when its single declared `spec_review.fallback_model` fails `terms_problem`, and `ladder` merely filters ineligible `opencode-go` ids and orders the rest by `anfragen_5h` for review rounds.           "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2).           "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def spec_review_call_config(root: Path) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The centrally configured spec-review call settings (spec criteria 13 and 15).\n\n    Defaults: a 30-minute call limit, a 30-second pause before the single retry, and no\n    fallback model - the fallback runs only when declared. The top-level `spec_review:`\n    block of `model-endpoints.yaml` overrides each in one place: `call_limit_minutes` (the\n    call limit in minutes), `pause_seconds` (the retry pause), `fallback_endpoint` (the\n    fallback reviews through the runner's own Pi) and `fallback_model`. The model is read\n    at call time, so a later configuration change never invalidates a written block: the\n    block records the model declared when it was written.\n    \"\"\"\n    settings: dict = {\n        \"timeout_seconds\": 30 * 60,\n        \"pause_seconds\": 30,\n        \"fallback_endpoint\": OPENCODE,\n        \"fallback_model\": None,\n    }\n    try:\n        data = yaml.safe_load((root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if data is None:\n            data = {}\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read ({error}).\") from error\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\n        raise Refused(\"model-endpoints.yaml is not a field mapping; repair it.\")\n    block = data.get(\"spec_review\")\n    if block is None:\n        return settings\n    if not isinstance(block, dict):\n        raise Refused(\"the `spec_review:` block of model-endpoints.yaml is not a field mapping; repair it.\")\n    minutes = block.get(\"call_limit_minutes\")\n    if minutes is not None and (not isinstance(minutes, int) or isinstance(minutes, bool) or minutes <= 0):\n        raise Refused(\"spec_review's `call_limit_minutes` must be a positive whole number of minutes.\")\n    if minutes is not None:\n        settings[\"timeout_seconds\"] = minutes * 60\n    seconds = block.get(\"pause_seconds\")\n    if seconds is not None and (not isinstance(seconds, int) or isinstance(seconds, bool) or seconds < 0):\n        raise Refused(\"spec_review's `pause_seconds` must be a whole number of seconds.\")\n    if seconds is not None:\n        settings[\"pause_seconds\"] = seconds\n    endpoint = block.get(\"fallback_endpoint\")\n    if endpoint is not None:\n        if not isinstance(endpoint, str) or not endpoint.strip():\n            raise Refused(\"spec_review's `fallback_endpoint` must name an endpoint.\")\n        if endpoint.strip() != OPENCODE:\n            raise Refused(f\"spec_review's `fallback_endpoint` must be {OPENCODE}.\")\n        settings[\"fallback_endpoint\"] = endpoint.strip()\n    model = block.get(\"fallback_model\")\n    if model is not None:\n        if not isinstance(model, str) or not model.strip():\n            raise Refused(\"spec_review's `fallback_model` must name a model id.\")\n        settings[\"fallback_model\"] = model.strip()\n    return settings\n",

          "excerpt": "export function decide(event, env) {\n  const tool = event.toolName;\n  const input = event.input;\n  if (tool === \"bash\") {\n    const command = input && input.command;\n    if (typeof command !== \"string\") return block(\"a bash call without a command\");\n    // A backslash-newline joins the lines the way the shell reads them.\n    const joined = command.replace(/\\\\\\r?\\n/g, \" \");\n    const hit = DANGEROUS.find((entry) => entry.pattern.test(joined));\n    return hit\n      ? { action: \"ask\", title: `Dangerous command (${hit.id}):\\n\\n  ${command}\\n\\nAllow?` }\n      : { action: \"allow\" };\n  }\n  if (!PATH_TOOLS.includes(tool)) return { action: \"allow\" };\n\n  const root = canonical(resolve(env.cwd));\n  const given = input.path;\n  const required = tool === \"read\" || tool === \"edit\" || tool === \"write\";\n  if (given === undefined && !required) {\n    // grep, find and ls search the working directory when no path is given.\n  } else {\n    const target = canonical(resolveToolPath(given, env.cwd, env.home));\n    if (!isInside(root, target, env.caseInsensitive)) {\n      return block(`${tool} on a path outside the worktree`);\n    }\n    if (WRITE_TOOLS.includes(tool)) {\n      const own = canonical(env.ownFile);\n      const guarded = PROTECTED_DIRS.map((name) => canonical(join(root, name)));\n      if (fold(target, env.caseInsensitive) === fold(own, env.caseInsensitive)) {\n        return block(`${tool} on the policy's own file`);\n      }\n      if (guarded.some((dir) => isInside(dir, target, env.caseInsensitive))) {\n        return block(`${tool} on a protected directory`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (tool === \"find\" && reachesOut(input.pattern)) return block(\"a find pattern that reaches outside the worktree\");\n  if (tool === \"grep\" && reachesOut(input.glob)) return block(\"a grep glob that reaches outside the worktree\");\n  return { action: \"allow\" };\n}\n\n// Bind the checked initial model from one sidecar's text.           "excerpt": "export function registerResearchTools(pi, transport = nodeTransport, sink = undefined) {\n  if (!pi || typeof pi.registerTool !== \"function\") {\n    throw new Error(\"this extension needs a Pi host with registerTool; it refuses to load anywhere else\");\n  }\n  pi.registerTool({\n    name: \"public_search\",\n    label: \"Public search\",\n    description:\n      \"Search the public web with a query. Returns result titles, destination URLs and snippets; a \" +\n      \"snippet is not a retrieved page. Records a source receipt. No local access exists.\",\n    parameters: SEARCH_PARAMETERS,\n    execute: async (_toolCallId, params) => toolResult(await executeSearch(params?.query, transport(), sink)),\n  });\n  pi.registerTool({\n    name: \"public_fetch\",\n    label: \"Public fetch\",\n    description: \"Retrieve one public https page. Records a source receipt. No local access exists.\",\n    parameters: FETCH_PARAMETERS,\n    execute: async (_toolCallId, params) => toolResult(await executeFetch(params?.url, transport(), sink)),\n  });\n  pi.on(\"tool_call\", async (event) => {\n    const name = event && event.toolName;\n    if (PUBLIC_TOOLS.includes(name)) return undefined;\n    return {\n      block: true,\n      reason:\n        `the tool '${name}' does not exist in a free researcher context: only ` +\n        \"public_search and public_fetch are available, and every file, shell and \" +\n        \"network tool is blocked at the extension boundary\",\n    };\n  });\n}\n\nexport default function (pi) {\n  registerResearchTools(pi);\n}\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_reviewer(\n    ctx: Context,\n    model: str,\n    prompt: str,\n    key: str,\n    *,\n    free: bool = False,\n    timeout_seconds: int | None = None,\n    task: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One reviewer call through Pi with this run's refreshed OpenCode Go definitions.\n\n    The launch is the measured set (spec, criterion 8), started through the\n    repository wrapper (ADR 0019): the rung's id under the `opencode-go`\n    provider, thinking `max` (Pi clamps it per model), the read-only tools,\n    every discovery switched off, no session, retries off. Each call gets its\n    own scratch directory: a `HOME`, an agent directory whose settings set retries and turn compaction off\n    and the run's refreshed provider definitions, and the prompt file. The key reaches Pi as\n    `OPENCODE_API_KEY` only. Returns the scrubbed answer. A call that has not\n    ended after `REVIEWER_MINUTES` is stopped (criterion 15).\n\n    A free call (`free=True`, ADR 0021 decision 3) gets `--no-tools` instead of\n    the read tools and starts in its scratch directory, not the worktree: its\n    only input is the prompt it is given.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        scratch = Path(tmp)\n        agent = scratch / \"agent\"\n        agent.mkdir()\n        (agent / \"settings.json\").write_text(json.dumps(PI_AGENT_SETTINGS), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        # The launch resolves and assesses its model offline, against the one\n        # address record read fresh from the held declaration. Without the\n        # run's refreshed definitions there is no checked destination, and no\n        # unchecked launch stands in for one (criterion 2).\n        try:\n            policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(ctx.root)\n        except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n        store = getattr(ctx, \"models_store\", None)\n        if store is None:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"no refreshed provider definitions accompany the reviewer call for {model}; \"\n                \"its destination cannot be assessed and the call does not start.\"\n            )\n        (agent / \"models-store.json\").write_text(json.dumps(store), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        _dropped, notices = activate_overlay(agent, store, policy)\n        retain_address_notices(notices)\n        for notice in notices:\n            print(f\"Address notice: {notice}\", file=sys.stderr)\n     ",

          "excerpt": "### The routing\n\nThe rows are in the form of §3's table. the Go seats are open and filled per run with the maintainer's choice on a cost-against-intelligence recommendation, Q-18) research eleven topics on the same brief, selected Go free models add public topics best-effort, and one fresh Opus 5.5 context reconciles; the runner dispatches every call through the declared endpoints, leak-checks each prompt, and an incomplete run exits 1 |\n| 2 Spec | **gpt-6.1-terra** | effort [`CODEX_EFFORTS[\"draft\"]`](../scripts/stage2.py), one call for 2, 2b and 3 through the Codex CLI and `draft`, writing in the CLI's workspace-write sandbox; `glm-5.3` drafts through Claude Code against Z.ai after two failed Codex attempts (ADR 0016) |\n| 2b Design | **gpt-6.1-terra** | effort [`CODEX_EFFORTS[\"draft\"]`](../scripts/stage2.py), drafted in the same call as 2 and 3 |\n| 3 Plan | **gpt-6.1-terra** | effort [`CODEX_EFFORTS[\"draft\"]`](../scripts/stage2.py), drafted in the same call as 2 and 2b |\n| 2a Spec review | **Opus 5.5** | effort `xhigh`, through Claude Code and `spec-review`, read-only tools |\n| 4 Implement | **GLM 5.3 Flash** | a worker given a clear plan; through Claude Code against Z.ai and the runner, for every change |\n| 4b Review loop | **the swarms, then the ladder** | round 1: every model the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live Pi catalog refresh of the `opencode-go` provider, in parallel, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2: up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid members in parallel for availability-enabled runs (legacy declarations use `flash_swarm`); then one eligible `modelle` id per round by `anfragen_5h` descending (ties by id, missing values last) — through Pi, effort `max` (Pi clamps it to `high` for a rung that takes no `max`) |\n| 4b Triage | none (a local command) | a local runner command for the orchestrator's already-made decision: it records one row's `Status` in this worktree's loop record and calls no model; a test-only `taken` is refused without `taken — not a test — <reason>`, and `Broke a test` stays the repair's proof mark |\n| Repair after 4b and 6 | **gpt-6.1-terra** | a Codex attempt in the configured `workspace-write` sandbox, effort [`CODEX_EFFORTS[\"repair\"]`](../scripts/stage2.py); one fresh Codex attempt after a failed post-run check, and Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` after two failed ones; no GLM credential (`repair`, ADR 0017) |\n| 6 Review | **gpt-6.1-terra** | effort [`CODEX_EFFORTS[\"review\"]`](../scripts/stage2.py), through the Codex CLI and `review`, a fresh Codex session |\n\nThe effort text in ADR 0016 and ADR 0017 awaits its separately agreed\namendments;           "excerpt": "def declaration_problem(root: Path, endpoint: str, model: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why the declaration does not clear this endpoint and model for framework content, or None.\n\n    For the `opencode-go` endpoint a model is also refused while its data terms\n    are unread or its declaration records a dated skip (ADR 0021, decision 5):\n    no paid or interactive call runs on unread terms.           "excerpt": "export function resolveToolPath(input, cwd, home) {\n  if (typeof input !== \"string\" || input.includes(\"\\0\")) {\n    throw new Error(\"the path is not a string, or holds a NUL byte\");\n  }\n  let path = input.replace(UNICODE_SPACES, \" \");\n  if (path.startsWith(\"@\")) path = path.slice(1);\n  if (path === \"~\") path = home;\n  else if (path.startsWith(\"~/\")) path = join(home, path.slice(2));\n  if (/^file:\\/\\//.test(path)) path = fileURLToPath(path);\n  return isAbsolute(path) ? resolve(path) : resolve(cwd, path);\n}\n\n// The real path of the deepest part that exists, with the rest appended, so a\n// symlink inside the worktree cannot lead a new file out of it. Any other\n// failure (a loop, no permission) throws, and a throw blocks the call.\nexport function canonical(path) {\n  const tail = [];\n  let head = path;\n  for (;;) {\n    try {\n      const real = realpathSync.native(head);\n      return tail.length ? join(real, ...tail.reverse()) : real;\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error.code !== \"ENOENT\" && error.code !== \"ENOTDIR\") throw error;\n      const parent = dirname(head);\n      if (parent === head) throw error;\n      tail.push(basename(head));\n      head = parent;\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nfunction fold(path, caseInsensitive) {\n  return caseInsensitive ? path.toLowerCase() : path;\n}\n\nexport function caseInsensitiveOn(platform) {\n  return platform === \"darwin\" || platform === \"win32\";\n}\n\nexport function isInside(root, target, caseInsensitive) {\n  const rel = relative(fold(root, caseInsensitive), fold(target, caseInsensitive));\n  return rel === \"\" || (rel !== \"..\" && !rel.startsWith(`..${sep}`) && !isAbsolute(rel));\n}\n\n// A find pattern or grep glob that is anchored elsewhere or climbs out.\nfunction reachesOut(glob) {\n  if (typeof glob !== \"string\") return false;\n  const text = glob.replace(UNICODE_SPACES, \" \");\n  return /^[/~@]/.test(text) || /^file:/.test(text) || text.split(/[\\\\/]/).includes(\"..\");\n}\n\nfunction block(reason) {\n  return { action: \"block\", reason: `stage2 session policy: ${reason}` };\n}\n\n// The decision for one tool call. Pure apart from reading the file system:\n// `env` is { cwd, home, ownFile, caseInsensitive }. Returns\n// { action: \"allow\" } | { action: \"block\", reason } | { action: \"ask\", title }.\nexport function decide(event, env) {\n  const tool = event.toolName;\n  const input = event.input;\n  if (tool === \"bash\") {\n    const command = input && input.command;\n    if (typeof command !== \"string\") return block(\"a bash call without a command\");\n    // A backslash-newline joins the lines the way the shell reads them.\n    const joined = command.replace(/\\\\\\r?\\n/g, \" \");\n    const hit = DANGEROUS.find((entry) => entry.pattern.test(joined));\n    return hit\n      ? { action: \"ask\", title: `Dangerous command (${hit.id}):\\n\\n  ${command}\\n\\nAllow?` }\n      : { action: \"allow\" };\n  }\n  if (!PATH_TOOLS.includes(tool)) return { action: \"allow\" };\n\n  const root = canonical(resolve(env.cwd));\n  const given = input.path;\n  const required = tool === \"read\" || tool === \"edit\" || tool === \"write\";\n  if (given === undefined && !required) {\n    // grep, find and ls search the working directory when no path is given.\n  } else {\n    const target = canonical(resolveToolPath(given, env.cwd, env.home));\n    if (!isInside(root, target, env.caseInsensitive)) {\n      return block(`${tool} on a path outside the worktree`);\n    }\n    if (WRITE_TOOLS.includes(tool)) {\n      const own = canonical(env.ownFile);\n      const guarded = PROTECTED_DIRS.map((name) => canonical(join(root, name)));\n      if (fold(target, env.caseInsensitive) === fold(own, env.caseInsensitive)) {\n        return block(`${tool} on the policy's own file`);\n      }\n      if (guarded.some((dir) => isInside(dir, target, env.caseInsensitive))) {\n        return block(`${tool} on a protected directory`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (tool === \"find\" && reachesOut(input.pattern)) return block(\"a find pattern that reaches outside the worktree\");\n  if (tool === \"grep\" && reachesOut(input.glob)) return block(",

          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_implement_flash_has_file_tools_and_the_complete_contract(world: World) -> None:\n    successful_implementation(world)\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 0\n    call = world.calls(\"claude\")[0]\n    argv, prompt = call[\"argv\"], call[\"prompt_file\"]\n    assert argv[argv.index(\"--model\") + 1] == \"glm-5.3-flash\"\n    assert set(argv[argv.index(\"--tools\") + 1].split(\",\")) == {\"Read\", \"Grep\", \"Glob\", \"Edit\", \"Write\"}\n    assert \"Bash\" not in argv[argv.index(\"--tools\") + 1]\n    assert \"--restricted\" in argv and \"--safe-mode\" in argv and \"--strict-mcp-config\" in argv\n    assert \"--add-dir\" not in argv and call[\"cwd\"] == str(world.root)\n    assert argv[argv.index(\"--permission-mode\") + 1] == \"acceptEdits\"\n    assert argv[argv.index(\"--permission-prompts\") + 1] == \"none\"\n    for forbidden in (\"WebFetch\", \"bypassPermissions\", \"--dangerously-skip-permissions\", \"--allowedTools\"):\n        assert forbidden not in argv\n    assert \"# Agent rules\" in prompt and \"# Spec\" in prompt and \"# Plan\" in prompt\n    assert \"Implementation baseline:\" in prompt and \"the post-run targeted check for implement and repair\" in prompt\n    assert \"Write no entry under `## Time used`\" in prompt, \"the prompt still asks the model to measure time\"\n    assert world.calls(\"make\") == [], \"the covered implement still waited on the full `make verify`\"\n    assert git(world.root, \"log\", \"-1\", \"--pretty=%s\") == \"feat(demo): implement accepted plan\"\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\") == \"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def explore(\n    root: Path,\n    change: str,\n    stage2_off: str | None = None,\n    klass: str | None = None,\n    availability_reported: str | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 1: the swarm for a feature or architectural change, GLM Flash for a bounded\n    change or a spike, or the explicit Haiku fallback - the answer lands in research.md.\"\"\"\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        klass = declared_class(root, change, klass)\n        if klass in SWARM_CLASSES:\n            import stage2_availability\n            import stage2_swarm\n\n            # The reported receipt comes first: no research call, probe or catalog read starts without it.\n            selection = stage2_availability.consume_research(\n                root, change, availability_reported, sys.modules[__name__], klass\n            )\n            stage2_swarm.run(root, change, sys.modules[__name__], klass, selection=selection)\n            return\n        if availability_reported is not None:\n            raise Refused(f\"--availability-reported belongs to a swarm class; this change is {klass}.\")\n        endpoint = GLM_FLASH\n    else:\n        if availability_reported is not None or klass is not None:\n            raise Refused(\"--stage2-off explores without a class or a selection receipt.\")\n        # The explicit Stage-1 route skips the class entirely: Haiku explores,\n        # and only the reason is carried for the later plan (spec, criterion 20).\n        endpoint = HAIKU\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, endpoint, bead_file=\"research.md\")\n    key = None\n    route = \"stage-1\" if stage2_off is not None else \"flash\"\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n    extra = (\n        f\"{EXPLORER_ROLE} \"\n        \"Report repository facts with source paths as prose ready to append to `research.md`. \"\n        \"Do not design, recommend, edit a file or use review-table formatting.\"\n    )\n    prompt = work_prompt(root, \"01-explore.md\", change, extra)\n    begin_work_call(ctx, \"explore\", endpoint, prompt, 1, route, ctx.research, stage2_off)\n    answer = run_work_model(ctx, prompt, endpoint, writable=False, key=key)\n    if not names_a_repository_file(root, answer):\n        # Research names its sources; an answer that names no file of the repository is a refusal or a\n        # question, not research, and is shown rather than appended (bead coding-harness-e7m).\n        tail = \"\\n\".join(answer.strip().splitlines()[-40:])\n        print(f\"explore: the answer, as it came:\\n{tail}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        raise CallFailed(\"the exploration answer names no file of the repository; nothing was appended\")\n    # The publication, not a plain append: the header's provenance fields are corrected and the skeleton's\n    # opening notices removed in the same atomic replacement that lands the answer (spec, criteria 1-5).\n    prepared = research_publication(\n        ctx.research.read_bytes(), producer=producer_for(endpoint), day=today(), model=endpoint[1]\n    )\n    publish_research(\n        ctx.research,\n        prepared,\n        f\"## Runner exploration — {today()}\\n\\n{quote_research_records(answer.strip())}\",\n    )\n    print(f\"explore: answer appended to {ctx.research.relative_to(root)} · route {route}\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_reviewer(\n    ctx: Context,\n    model: str,\n    prompt: str,\n    key: str,\n    *,\n    free: bool = False,\n    timeout_seconds: int | None = None,\n    task: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One reviewer call through Pi with this run's refreshed OpenCode Go definitions.\n\n    The launch is the measured set (spec, criterion 8), started through the\n    repository wrapper (ADR 0019): the rung's id under the `opencode-go`\n    provider, thinking `max` (Pi clamps it per model), the read-only tools,\n    every discovery switched off, no session, retries off. Each call gets its\n    own scratch directory: a `HOME`, an agent directory whose settings set retries and turn compaction off\n    and the run's refreshed provider definitions, and the prompt file. The key reaches Pi as\n    `OPENCODE_API_KEY` only. Returns the scrubbed answer. A call that has not\n    ended after `REVIEWER_MINUTES` is stopped (criterion 15).\n\n    A free call (`free=True`, ADR 0021 decision 3) gets `--no-tools` instead of\n    the read tools and starts in its scratch directory, not the worktree: its\n    only input is the prompt it is given.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        scratch = Path(tmp)\n        agent = scratch / \"agent\"\n        agent.mkdir()\n        (agent / \"settings.json\").write_text(json.dumps(PI_AGENT_SETTINGS), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        # The launch resolves and assesses its model offline, against the one\n        # address record read fresh from the held declaration. Without the\n        # run's refreshed definitions there is no checked destination, and no\n        # unchecked launch stands in for one (criterion 2).\n        try:\n            policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(ctx.root)\n        except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n        store = getattr(ctx, \"models_store\", None)\n        if store is None:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"no refreshed provider definitions accompany the reviewer call for {model}; \"\n                \"its destination cannot be assessed and the call does not start.\"\n            )\n        (agent / \"models-store.json\").write_text(json.dumps(store), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        _dropped, notices = activate_overlay(agent, store, policy)\n        retain_address_notices(notices)\n        for notice in notices:\n            print(f\"Address notice: {notice}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        home = scratch / \"home\"\n        home.mkdir()\n        check_overlay(agent, home, model, policy=policy)\n        row = stage2_go.definition_of(store, stage2_go.PROVIDER, model)\n        if row is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"the refreshed definitions of {model} are missing or duplicated; no reviewer starts.\")\n        assessment = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, row)\n        if not assessment.admitted:\n            raise Refused(assessment.problem)\n        prompt_file = scratch / \"review-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            str(PI_WRAPPER),\n            \"--print\",\n            \"--no-session\",\n            \"--no-approve\",\n            \"--no-extensions\",\n            \"--no-mcp\",\n            \"--no-skills\",\n            \"--no-context-files\",\n            \"--no-prompt-templates\",\n            \"--no-themes\",\n            \"--offline\",\n            *([\"--no-tools\"] if free else [\"--tools\", PI_TOOLS]),\n            \"--thinking\",\n            \"max\",\n            \"--model\",\n            f\"{OPENCODE}/{model}\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            task or f\"Review the change {ctx.change} as the appended instructions say.\",\n        ]\n        env = foreign_env({\"HOME\": str(home), \"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": str(agent), \"OPENCODE_API_KEY\": key})\n        # Every key of the secrets file is scrubbed, not the OpenCode key alone: a member with read\n        # tools can quote the GLM k",

          "citation": "prompts/04-implement.md::Phase 4 · Implement",

          "excerpt": "# Phase 4 · Implement\n\n**Model:** GLM 5.3 Flash — a solid worker given a clear plan; through\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py implement <change>` and its leak check\n(`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). When Stage 2 is off or Z.ai is unavailable, rerun as\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py implement <change> --stage2-off [REASON]`; Sonnet\n5.5 at effort `medium` (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) builds and the reason is recorded.\nA leak-check BLOCK stops; it never falls back.\n**Input:** `@plans/changes/<name>/plan.md @plans/changes/<name>/spec.md`\n**Gate:** `make verify` green on the final head before phase 6; each runner\nattempt passes the targeted check or, where that is unsafe, the full one.\n\nYou follow the plan. You read the spec to know what you are building against.\nUnder the Stage-2 runner an implement attempt has\nfile tools but no command tool (a Codex repair attempt may run tests and\n`make verify`, never commit): write no entry under `## Time used`, because the\nrunner measures each completed attempt itself and writes a line marked\n\"measured by the runner\" (a rejected attempt gets one too); the runner\nruns the targeted check after an implement or a repair attempt (the whole\ntouched and import-linked test files and the gates the touched kinds of file\nfeed; the full `make verify` when the attempt touches shared infrastructure, would run `tests/test_stage2.py` whole, or meets another fallback of the runner's targeted selection (`targeted_selection` in `scripts/stage2.py`: for example a `conftest.py`, production code without a linked test, an unreadable link inventory)), and makes the local checkpoint commit. A\ntargeted red fails the attempt; the full check never overrides it. An\nimplement attempt that adds production code (a Python or shell file) no test\nreaches is refused before any test runs: add the test that reaches it. One full\n`make verify` runs on the final head before phase 6. In an ordinary Stage-1 session, you still run the commands\nand commits this prompt assigns to you, and the interactive session reads its own\nclock and logs its own spans, as the appetite rule below says.\n\n**Run the cheap checks before you hand back.** These are ruff (`ruff check` and\n`ruff format --check` on changed Python files) and selected tests. Implement owes\nevery ledger test. Repair owes its findings' proofs and written ledger entries;\nmissing unwritten entries are named but not owed. With a command tool, run the\nstanding ledger tests and leave the applicable checks green. On a file-only route,\nthe runner runs ruff, then pytest over changed or new test functions, standing\nledger tests and, on a retry, previously failed tests. Missing ledger IDs never\nreach pytest. The first red check ends the attempt (bead coding-harness-5tyh).\n`findings.md` is the runner's: an edit you make there is put back before the checks.\nThat edit is not part of your work, and on its own it never fails the attempt.\n\n**The plan is the contract.** Where it no longer holds — a file does not exist,\nan assumption does not carry, a test cannot be written that way — you **stop**\nand report in four lines:\n\n```\nexpected:   what the plan says\nfound:      what is actually there\nrelevant:   why this changes the solution\nproposal:   how to continue\n```\n\nThe plan is then revised, never silently overwritten. A deviation that lives\nonly in the code is no longer a deviation on the next reading — it is the plan.\n\n**The appetite is a stop.** The plan's card names one (`Appetite:`). *Time used*\nis the sum of the spans of the sessions that worked under this prompt on this\nchange. Read `date` when a session starts or work resumes, between steps, before\neach commit and when it ends (at its stop, resumption line or \"done:\" line);\nnever estimate it or recall it. A break inside a session counts, and the session's\nstatus message says so; the time between two sessions does not. A stop ends the span; work that\nresumes starts a new one, even in the same chat. When a span ends the session\nrecords it with `python3 scripts/harness.p",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it. Until that is built, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3 runs the two phases:\n   Haiku 4.5 explores and Sonnet 5.5 implements. This is an open item of the\n   change, not a claim that it works.\n6. **Endpoints are architecture; the models on them are declaration\n   (amended on 2026-10-30).** Which endpoints framework content may reach\n   stays this ADR's matter (decision 2) and its amendments'. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture. A newly admitted\n   model takes a place in the review loop's ladder only; any other role\n   (explore, implem",

          "excerpt": "def examine(root: Path) -> Examination:\n    ex = Examination(anchors=anchors(root))\n    read: list[Feature] = []\n    for anchor in ex.anchors:\n        cls, problem = read_class(anchor.path)\n        if cls is None:\n            ex.anchor_findings.append(\n                (anchor, f\"adr-answers: {anchor.rel}: {problem} — whether this change owes an ADR answer is unknown\")\n            )\n            continue\n        ex.classes[anchor.rel] = cls\n        if cls != \"feature\":\n            continue\n        feature, problems = read_feature(anchor)\n        if feature is None:\n            ex.anchor_findings.append(\n                (\n                    anchor,\n                    f\"adr-answers: {anchor.rel}: a feature whose header breaks its shape — {'; '.join(problems)} — \"\n                    \"whether it has the answer it owes is unknown until the header reads\",\n                )\n            )\n            continue\n        read.append(feature)\n\n    by_change: dict[str, list[Feature]] = {}\n    for f in read:\n        by_change.setdefault(f.change, []).append(f)\n    for change, group in by_change.items():\n        if len(group) > 1:\n            rels = \" and \".join(f.anchor.rel for f in group)\n            for f in group:\n                ex.anchor_findings.append(\n                    (\n                        f.anchor,\n                        f\"adr-answers: {f.anchor.rel}: two features name change `{change}` ({rels}) — \"\n                        \"whether each has the answer it owes is unknown\",\n                    )\n                )\n    ex.features = [f for f in read if len(by_change[f.change]) == 1]\n\n    for f in ex.features:\n        path = root / answer_rel(f.change)\n        if not path.exists():\n            ex.missing.append(f)\n            continue\n        data, problems = load_answer(path)\n        where = f\"anchor {f.anchor.rel}; fix: {REFUSED_FIX}\"\n        if problems:\n            ex.answer_findings.append(\n                (f, f\"adr-answers: {f.change}: {answer_rel(f.change)} is refused ({'; '.join(problems)}) — {where}\")\n            )\n        elif data[\"change\"] != f.change:\n            ex.answer_findings.append(\n                (f, f\"adr-answers: {f.change}: {answer_rel(f.change)} names change `{data['change']}` — {where}\")\n            )\n    return ex\n",

          "citation": "prompts/02-spec.md::The form of a `[DECISION]`",
          "end_line": 127,
          "excerpt": "## The form of a `[DECISION]`\n\nIt is answerable by someone who has not read the code. Never a mechanism\nquestion — those are `[DETAIL]` or `[GAP]`, and asking one of an intent owner is\na protocol violation, not thoroughness.\n\n```\nTopic:                 <what this is about, in plain words>\nIntention:             <why this comes up now and what it is for>\nToday:                 <what happens today>\nRepository change:     <what changes in the repository if it is built>\nArchitecture change:   <what changes in its architecture; an unchanged\n                       area says why it stays as it is>\n\nGoal in one sentence:  <what this is about, in plain words>\nOptions:               each named after what it does, with its consequence\n                       for users, operations or risk — not its mechanism\nRecommendation:        <one option> — because <one sentence>\nIf you say \"ok\":       <exactly what will then be built>\nWhat is lost:          <what the other option would have given>\nDownside you accept:   <per option, the downside that comes with choosing it>\n```\n\nThe five context lines come first, in the maintainer's language, before any\noption; identifiers are explained at first use, and the actual question\nstands last, on its own line. When the answer is recorded, the context shown\nhere goes into the record's own `context` field\n(`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, \"The question protocol\").\n\nThe question asks which downside the maintainer accepts with the choice, as\nthe interview does (`prompts/01a-interview.md`, \"How you ask\"): every option\nnames its downside, an answer accepts only a downside that was shown or that\nthe maintainer stated, and where it is not settled the record stays `open` —\nyou never invent it. The answered record carries the complete decision\nstatement with its `accepting` clause and the date of the day it is\nrecorded; `draft` refuses a change whose answered record has none.\n\nAnswers are: **ok** · **option N** · **change criterion N to \"…\"** · **no,\nbecause …**. That is the decision record (MADR) in question form. Shorthand\n(work item, A-/G-point, invariant) only as a trailing note, never carrying the\nsentence. You ask only once all of the above stands.\n\nFrontmatter per `plans/_README.md`: `status`, `implementation_status`, `date`,\n`last_reviewed`, `bead`. Also `class:` — one of `spike`, `bounded`, `feature`,\n`architectural` (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, \"Change classes, the ADR question and\ndecision pull requests\"). For a `feature`, also `change: <folder name>` and\n`adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\", reason: \"<one sentence>\"}` — quote\n`\"yes\"` and `\"no\"`: bare, YAML reads them as booleans, and the gate\n`adr-answers` refuses the header. The proposal only proposes; the maintainer\nanswers, with `python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr`.\n\nEvery class lists under `adr_files: [docs/adr/<file>, …]` each file under\n`docs/adr/` the change creates, changes or removes — `[]` or no line when it\ntouches none. The header lists every ADR file the change touches: the gate\n`interview-minimums` attributes an ADR edit to that claim alone and holds a\nfeature's answer to it, \"yes\" with at least one claimed file and \"no\" with none\n(ADR 0014, `docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n\n",

          "end_line": 81,
          "excerpt": "## Q-4 · How the decision is recorded\n\nasked: 2026-11-25\nanswer: \"A new ADR 'Work verbs through Pi on OpenCode Go' records route, order Go → Codex → Claude, default model and write boundary; it explicitly supersedes the affected parts of ADR 0007, 0011 and 0015, which each get a pointer.\"\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the decision record.\n  Intention: one place that states the work-verb routing.\n  Today: model routing is spread over ADR 0007, 0011 and 0015.\n  Repository change: docs/adr/<next>-work-verbs-through-pi.md and three pointer lines.\n  Architecture change: the routing decision moves into the new ADR.\n\nIn the context of recording the work-verb routing, facing three ADRs that each hold a part, we decided one new ADR that supersedes the affected parts with pointers, to achieve one place for the routing decision, accepting three pointer edits. — 2026-11-25\n\n",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0007-stage-2-reviews-by-codex-and-glm.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 133,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included.           "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check\",\nbecause it implements the maintainer's model choice without weakening the\nrepair evidence contract.\n\n1. **Codex repairs all taken findings in one batch** through `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`: loop-record rows, released loop rows\n   and phase-6 findings. Each Codex attempt starts `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort\n   `max` in a fresh session, with the existing `workspace-write` configuration,\n   hooks and memories off, and no added directory, automatic approval or\n   bypass. Repair reads no GLM key and never routes to `glm-coding-plan`.\n2. **Only post-run failures advance the chain:** Codex; a fresh Codex attempt\n   with the first attempt's diagnostics; Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` on\n   Stage 1 with both diagnostics. A model call failure stops; with unchanged\n   HEAD, the existing restoration returns the worktree to baseline. When\n   Codex is unavailable, the orchestrator deliberately starts\n   `--stage2-off <reason>`, which uses Sonnet alone and records why. A\n   declaration refusal or leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.**\n   The orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>`, or\n   takes a finding no test can show as `taken — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Repair keeps those inputs, requests one fixed line per row and a measured\n   time entry, and starts no review. The runner checks each exact prompt,\n   prepares and formats the result, runs `make verify`, checks the time and\n   evidence, writes statuses and makes one clean descendant checkpoint.\n   A Codex call that moves HEAD stops before restoration or a runner commit.\n4. **The existing proof and statuses stand.** A code finding requires a\n   defined test the runner demonstrates red against baseline code; a finding\n   taken as `not a test` is proven by the separate re-check. Fixed rows read\n   `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Failed attempts retain their audit, quoted diagnostics and changed-file\n   evidence, while their model-written statuses are restored. Private loop\n   rows are marked only after the checkpoint; unreleased rows reach the\n   repair in the prompt rather than a worktree file.\n5. **The same model may repair phase-6 findings; a fresh session re-checks.**\n   A phase-6 verdict after an earlier `## Phase 6` block in `findings.md` — a\n   re-check — runs Codex read-only without resuming the repair, a prior\n   verdict or a historical phase-2a session; the first phase-6 review keeps\n   the resume rule of ADR 0016. Loop marks may\n   resume only that new verdict thread after its verdict. This replaces ADR\n   0015's blanket reviewer/repairer separation; it does not give review calls\n   write tools or move any review to another model.\n6. **The loop budget and run count stand.** A fixed row counts as taken;\n   round 3 requires a taken or fixed row in round 2, and the maximum stays\n   three rounds. The orchestrator writes `Broke a test` from the repair\n   evidence before the next round or release. Audit lines and historical GLM\n   counts retain their format. Initial implementation, Explore and draft's\n   GLM fallback retain their models.\n\n",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **Framework content may also go to `opencode-go`** — at\n   `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, through Pi\n   (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, at the version the runner pins), with\n   the three ids below. The interactive `session` verb reaches a declared endpoint under\n   its own amendment (bead coding-harness-amp); this declaration is what that\n   verb waits for before it opens its OpenCode path to the three ids.\n2. **The loop's reviewer role moves.** The loop leaves GLM for the ladder;\n   the spec review and the review stay with Codex exactly as ADR 0007 set\n   them (the maintainer, 2026-10-08), and phase 6 keeps resuming the\n   phase-2a session. The row\n            # resolves only while the declaration itself is complete and every\n            # id it names sits on its declared endpoint.\n            assert swarm_block_problems(_erklaerung()) == [], (\n                \"docs/WORKFLOW.md routes to 'the research swarm', but the declared swarm is incomplete\"\n            )\n            continue\n        assert _loest_auf(anzeige, ids), (\n            f\"docs/WORKFLOW.md routes to '{anzeige}', which no endpoint lists. \"\n            f\"Looked for: {' or '.join(sorted(_kandidaten(anzeige)))}\"\n        )\n",

          "end_line": 90,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen proposal: \"Shared provider-entry policy and explicit Pi binding\",\nbecause it implements the five answered intentions at one destination\nboundary and fits the future central registry without another model list.\n\n1. Every runner-controlled Go launch uses one current provider address\n   policy, including probes, retries and calls using saved selections.\n2. Bases require HTTPS, the exact admitted host `opencode.ai` and the default\n   port, with no credentials, query, fragment or ambiguous URL form.\n3. A different path on that origin is preserved and visibly reported with\n   the model and old/new paths. It does not update the known path by itself.\n4. Missing bases use a recorded default for the resolved API; invalid bases\n   and absent mappings never fall through to unchecked Pi defaults.\n5. Agent maintenance of documented paths records source and reading date;\n   changing the host, model permissions or terms is outside that delegation.\n   The one record is the address part of the `opencode-go` entry in\n   `model-endpoints.yaml`; the orchestrating session owns its edits.\n   Foreign model attempts never edit it, and no held-path exemption is\n   added. A catalog observation alone never updates the record.\n6. Address admission supplements, rather than replaces, model terms,\n   data-class, free-class, measured-API and leak checks.\n\n",

The interactive `session` verb reaches a declared endpoint under\n   its own amendment (bead coding-harness-amp); this declaration is what that\n   verb waits for before it opens its OpenCode path to the three ids.\n2. **The loop's reviewer role moves.** The loop leaves GLM for the ladder;\n   the spec review and the review stay with Codex exactly as ADR 0007 set\n   them (the maintainer, 2026-10-08), and phase 6 keeps resuming the\n   phase-2a session.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else.           "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

Candidate\nadmission and cost values live in `model-endpoints.yaml`.\n\n| Phase | Model | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 Explore | **GLM 5.3 Flash** | much input, little output, no deep reasoning; through Claude Code against Z.ai and the runner, for a `bounded` change or a `spike` (ADR 0020) |\n| 1 Explore swarm | **the research swarm** | for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020): a finder trio maps the sources, six seats (three repository, three online;
