          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"GLM 5.3 through a runner verb `repair`\", because it takes the\nrepairs off Claude's budget behind the guards every other GLM call passes,\nwhile the reviewers stay read-only.\n\n1. **The repair of taken findings runs on GLM 5.3** — `glm-5.3` on\n   `glm-coding-plan`, through Claude Code, started only by `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`. One call takes every loop row and every\n   phase-6 finding whose Status begins `taken`. The attempts are GLM 5.3, one\n   GLM 5.3 repair attempt that carries the first one's diagnostics, and one\n   Sonnet 5.5 stage-1 fallback; `--stage2-off [REASON]` runs Sonnet 5.5 alone\n   and records why; a leak-check BLOCK stops without a fallback. The guards of\n   `implement` hold: the declaration and the leak check before each attempt,\n   file tools without a command tool, the credential clean-up, `make verify`\n   run by the runner, a measured line in the time log, one checkpoint commit.\n   This amends ADR 0011's decision 2, whose last sentence names what still\n   routes to GLM: the repair joins explore and implement there, on GLM 5.3.\n2. **A reviewer never repairs its own findings.** The rungs and Codex keep\n   their read-only tools; the repair is a separate call by a model no review\n   phase routes to. A change that routes a review phase to `glm-coding-plan`\n   again has to say who repairs that phase's findings.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.** The\n   orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>` into a\n   phase-6 finding as into a loop row, and `taken — not a test — <reason>` for\n   a finding no test can show. The verb repairs only the taken rows and ends\n   with its checkpoint commit; the orchestrator then re-checks with the loop's\n   next round and with `review`.\n4. **A repaired row reads `fixed`.** Its Status becomes `fixed —\n   tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`, the forms of\n   ADR 0013's criterion ledger.           "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When a runner repair has determinable targeted coverage, its post-run\n   verification uses the targeted check instead of full `make verify`.\n   *Refuted by:* a narrow, covered Python repair invoking full verification.\n\n2. When a targeted repair is checked, every surviving touched test file and\n   every surviving linked test file is executed in full from current content.\n   *Refuted by:* an unchanged linked test's failing sibling being omitted,\n   an untracked or index-only touch being missed, a removed path losing its\n   baseline-linked tests, or a retry losing an earlier retained edit.\n\n3. When a repair touches surviving Python files, read-only ruff lint and\n   format checks cover those files after the runner's existing formatting.\n   *Refuted by:* accepting a touched file with a remaining lint or format\n   fault because it was outside the check's targets.\n\n4. When targeted verification runs, it measures the existing locally\n   runnable gates applicable to the touched file kinds with their declared\n   enforcement unchanged.\n   *Refuted by:* omitting the document gates after derived plan/index edits,\n   omitting a changed gate's own check, or treating an unmeasured blocking\n   gate as passing.\n\n5. If a repair touches `prompts/` or its targeted coverage cannot be\n   determined safely, full `make verify` is required for that attempt.\n   *Refuted by:* targeted acceptance of a prompt edit, an unclassified input,\n   an unreadable link inventory or production code with no linked test.\n\n6. When targeted post-run commands execute, they run outside the\n   machine-wide verify admission.\n   *Refuted by:* a targeted command acquiring or claiming inherited ownership\n   of that admission; full fallback and phase-6 checks still owe admission.\n\n7. If a required targeted command fails, cannot start or exceeds its time\n   bound, the repair cannot checkpoint or mark its findings fixed.\n   *Refuted by:* a checkpoint or fixed row despite that failure, or an\n   unbounded/unprotected diagnostic reaching the existing retry flow.\n\n8. When repair uses targeted verification, the existing preparation,\n   accepted-ledger/retry selections, fixed-line validation and red-first\n   proof remain prerequisites for its checkpoint.\n   *Refuted by:* a missing derived refresh, a planted ledger-selected failure\n   being skipped, acceptance of an invalid fixed answer, or a proof failure\n   becoming a fixed row merely because targeted commands passed.\n\n9. When phase 6 is requested, the runner obtains a fresh green full\n   `make verify` for the current head before starting the reviewer.\n   *Refuted by:* a reviewer call after a red, unstartable or timed-out full\n   check, after the checked head or substantive tree changed, or using only\n   an earlier repair's green result.\n\n10. When implement or draft runs, its existing verification scope and\n    admission behavior remain unchanged.\n    *Refuted by:* implement checkpointing after targeted checks alone, or\n    draft losing its existing document/full verification choice.\n\n11.           "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When a finder is launched through Claude Code, its call enforces the shared locator JSON Schema.\n   *Refuted by:* a finder call missing the schema or using a different schema.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-3.\n2. When a finder is launched through Pi, its prompt includes the same locator JSON Schema.\n   *Refuted by:* a Pi finder prompt omitting or differing from that schema.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-3.\n3. When a finder report is validated, the locator rules derive from the same schema used by the finder calls.\n   *Refuted by:* a change to a schema rule is ignored by validation or a call receives a different rule.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-3.\n4. When a process-successful first answer has the four nonempty category lists but contains malformed entries, every valid entry and no malformed entry reaches map merge without another finder call.\n   *Refuted by:* a valid entry is lost, an invalid entry reaches merge, the merge stops solely because entries were dropped, or a correction is requested.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-2.\n5. When an entry is not an object, has missing, extra or invalid fields, or has a required string consisting only of whitespace or empty, that entry is dropped and its own validation errors are recorded.\n   *Refuted by:* an invalid entry is retained or a dropped entry has no applicable error.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-2; decisions.md, agent details S-1, S-2, S-4 and S-6.\n6. When filtering removes every entry of a category, the retained report contains exactly `{\"not_read\": \"every entry of this category was dropped by locator validation (finder-partial-report)\"}` in that category, provided at least one entry of the answer survives (otherwise criterion 12 applies).\n   *Refuted by:* an empty category, another marker, or a marker alongside a retained entry.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md, agent detail S-7.\n7. When entries are dropped, the published partial fence and manifest identify their finder seat, category, original entries and exact per-entry validation errors as filtered gaps.\n   *Refuted by:* either record omits or misidentifies a dropped entry, category, seat or error, or represents it as retained evidence.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-2; decisions.md, agent details S-1, S-4 and S-5.\n8. When entries are dropped, they are excluded from the map's `gaps` and `not_read` lists except for the fixed marker for an emptied category.\n   *Refuted by:* a dropped entry or its validation error is inserted into either map list.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md, agent detail S-5.\n9. When a filtered finder answer is stored, its outcome is `ok` and its dropped entries are recorded in a `filtered` list beside it.\n   *Refuted by:* a different outcome or missing filtered details in the stored record.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md, agent detail S-8.\n10. When a run resumes with a reusable filtered finder record, it reuses the retained answer and publishes the same filtered gaps without launching that finder again.\n    *Refuted by:* a repeat finder call, changed retained entries or missing or changed gaps on resume.\n    *Basis:* decisions.md, agent detail S-8.\n11. When a map is merged, the existing exact-union check uses the retained reports of all three finder seats.\n    *Refuted by:* an added or missing retained locator or altered finder origin passes the check.\n    *Basis:* research.md, Map merge; decisions.md#Q-2.\n12. If the outer answer is invalid JSON, has duplicate keys or non-finite values, lacks exactly the four categories, or has a non-list or originally empty category, the existing invalid-report outcome stops the run before map merge.           "excerpt": "## 4 · Stage 2 — Codex and the review loop on OpenCode Go (active for framework content)\n\nSince ADR 0007 (2026-09-30) a reviewer from another vendor reads a change\nbefore it merges — for **framework content only**: this repository's own tree,\nthe class `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`. Codex (OpenAI; `gpt-6.1-terra` since 2026-11-15, `gpt-6.1-sol` before)\ndrafts the spec, the design and the plan (2, 2b and 3, the `draft` verb) and\nreviews the code (6). **Since ADR 0016 (2026-10-12)** the spec review (2a) runs\non Opus 5.5 through the `spec-review` verb — a fresh context, and a model other\nthan the Codex or GLM 5.3 that drafted the artefacts it reads: no model reviews\nits own draft.\n**Since ADR 0011 (2026-10-08)** the\nreview loop (4b) between implementation and the code review runs on OpenCode\nGo (`opencode-go` in `model-endpoints.yaml`) through Pi — **since ADR 0019\n(2026-10-15)** the repository's own pinned install under `tools/pi/`, whose\nexact version `tools/pi/package.json` pins — calling OpenCode Go's\nchat-completions address, and which\nmodel answers a round follows the free swarm, the selected paid Flash swarm,\nthen the `modelle` set ordered by `anfragen_5h` descending (ties by id;\nmissing values last), the paid ladder. The maintainer put the ladder to the\nloop alone on 2026-10-08 — after\nCodex's phase 6 found two real BLOCKERs in a change the loop had passed, as on\nevery change of the night run — so GLM has left the reviewer roles.\n**Since 2026-10-06** (maintainer) GLM 5.3 Flash\n(`glm-5.3-flash`, the Z.ai endpoint) also explores (phase 1) and implements\n(phase 4) — the two phases that read the repository broadly and write its\ncode. **Since 2026-10-12** (ADR 0015) GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`, the same endpoint)\nrepaired the findings the orchestrator takes, of the loop (4b) and of phase 6;\n**since the merge of ADR 0017** Codex (`gpt-6.1-sol` until 2026-11-15, `gpt-6.1-terra` since) does, with Sonnet 5.5\nafter two failed post-run checks, through the runner's `repair` verb — since the\nfirst day `taken` on a row means\ndecided and waiting for the repair, and `fixed` means repaired.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. This is an open item of the\n   change, not a claim that it works.\n6. **Endpoints are architecture; the models on them are declaration\n   (amended on 2026-10-30).** Which endpoints framework content may reach\n   stays this ADR's matter (decision 2) and its amendments'. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture.           "end_line": 36,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Scope of the change\n\nasked: 2026-11-25\nanswer: \"All three parts: (1) fallback — when the normal implement/repair route fails, implement and repair run through Pi on OpenCode Go; (2) model choice — GLM 5.3 Flash or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as a declared parameter of the one route (house rule 9), not a second verb; (3) GLM off Claude Code — GLM 5.3 / 5.3 Flash for explore, implement and loop start through Pi instead of Claude Code.\"\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: what this change delivers.\n  Intention: implement and repair keep running when Claude Code or Z.ai is exhausted (both were on 2026-11-25).\n  Today: GLM 5.3 Flash starts only through Claude Code on Z.ai; DeepSeek through Pi only interactively (session verb).\n  Repository change: scripts/stage2.py routes, model-endpoints.yaml (opencode-go widened to work verbs), tests.\n  Architecture change: the work verbs gain a Pi route on OpenCode Go (new ADR, Q-4).\n\nIn the context of work verbs that stop when Claude Code or Z.ai is exhausted, facing a narrow or a full scope, we decided to build all three parts (fallback, model choice, GLM off Claude Code), to achieve one Pi route for every work verb, accepting a larger architectural change. — 2026-11-25\n\n",

Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there.           "citation": "docs/adr/0015-glm-5-3-repairs-taken-findings.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 136,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"GLM 5.3 through a runner verb `repair`\", because it takes the\nrepairs off Claude's budget behind the guards every other GLM call passes,\nwhile the reviewers stay read-only.\n\n1. **The repair of taken findings runs on GLM 5.3** — `glm-5.3` on\n   `glm-coding-plan`, through Claude Code, started only by `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`. One call takes every loop row and every\n   phase-6 finding whose Status begins `taken`. The attempts are GLM 5.3, one\n   GLM 5.3 repair attempt that carries the first one's diagnostics, and one\n   Sonnet 5.5 stage-1 fallback; `--stage2-off [REASON]` runs Sonnet 5.5 alone\n   and records why; a leak-check BLOCK stops without a fallback. The guards of\n   `implement` hold: the declaration and the leak check before each attempt,\n   file tools without a command tool, the credential clean-up, `make verify`\n   run by the runner, a measured line in the time log, one checkpoint commit.\n   This amends ADR 0011's decision 2, whose last sentence names what still\n   routes to GLM: the repair joins explore and implement there, on GLM 5.3.\n2. **A reviewer never repairs its own findings.** The rungs and Codex keep\n   their read-only tools; the repair is a separate call by a model no review\n   phase routes to. A change that routes a review phase to `glm-coding-plan`\n   again has to say who repairs that phase's findings.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.** The\n   orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>` into a\n   phase-6 finding as into a loop row, and `taken — not a test — <reason>` for\n   a finding no test can show. The verb repairs only the taken rows and ends\n   with its checkpoint commit; the orchestrator then re-checks with the loop's\n   next round and with `review`.\n4. **A repaired row reads `fixed`.** Its Status becomes `fixed —\n   tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`, the forms of\n   ADR 0013's criterion ledger. A finding on code is fixed only with a test\n   that the runner ran against the baseline's code and saw fail; a finding on\n   text is proven by the re-check.\n5. **A fixed row counts as a taken one.** Round 3 starts when round 2 wrote a\n   row whose Status begins `taken` or `fixed`, which amends ADR 0011's\n   decision 3; the stage-2 run count counts a fixed loop row as take",

          "excerpt": "def test_real_reviewer_tool_contract(project: Path, transport) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a real reviewer-shaped call declares exactly read,grep,find,ls; an undeclared tool cannot execute.\"\"\"\n    standin = StandIn(\n        [\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"read\", \"arguments\": {\"path\": \"sentinel.txt\"}}]},\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": f\"echo pwned >> {project / 'sentinel.txt'}\"}}]},\n            {\"content\": \"No finding.\"},\n        ]\n    )\n    transport.providers[\"opencode-go\"] = {\"baseUrl\": standin.url}\n    try:\n        answer = stage2.run_reviewer(\n            contract_ctx(project),\n            \"contract-rung\",\n            \"Review the change demo as the appended instructions say.\",\n            SYNTHETIC_KEY,\n        )\n        assert \"No finding.\" in answer, \"the scripted stop never reached the runner\"\n        assert len(standin.requests) == 3, f\"expected the scripted three turns, saw {len(standin.requests)}\"\n        declared = tool_names(standin.requests[0])\n        assert declared == {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, (\n            f\"the model saw {sorted(declared)}, not the four reviewer tools\"\n        )\n        assert SENTINEL_IN in message_text(standin.requests[1]), \"the positive control read never executed\"\n        for exchange in standin.requests:\n            assert tool_names(exchange) <= {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, \"a foreign tool was declared\"\n        assert (project / \"sentinel.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == SENTINEL_IN + \"\\n\", (\n            \"an undeclared tool changed the sentinel\"\n        )\n    finally:\n        standin.close()\n    # the launch was the runner's own construction, through the wrapper, under the guard\n    (call,) = transport.calls\n    assert call[\"argv\"][0] == str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"the reviewer did not start through the repository wrapper\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--tools\") + 1] == \"read,grep,find,ls\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--model\") + 1] == \"opencode-go/contract-rung\"\n    assert \"NODE_OPTIONS\" in call[\"env\"] and \"pi_network_guard\" in call[\"env\"][\"NODE_OPTIONS\"]\n    assert call[\"env\"][\"OPENCODE_API_KEY\"] == SYNTHETIC_KEY\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_go_path_reads_the_one_address_record(world, monkeypatch, capsys):\n    \"\"\"Criterion 1: no caller keeps its own Go origin rule or missing-address default.\n\n    Fault: a caller that prepared against one record and dispatched from a\n    private one would send after the record changed, or would run when the\n    record is gone.\n    \"\"\"\n    model = TEST_LADDER[0]\n    harness = Harness(world, monkeypatch)\n    store = go_store(row(model))\n    seat_lines: list[str] = []\n    seat = harness.seat(model, store, seat_lines)\n    calls = [\n        harness.reviewer(model, store),\n        harness.reviewer(model, store, free=True),\n        harness.probe(model, store)[0],\n        seat,\n    ]\n    for call in calls:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        call()\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a family did not dispatch under the admitted record\"\n    # The record alone changes; Pure apart from reading the file system:\n// `env` is { cwd, home, ownFile, caseInsensitive }. Returns\n// { action: \"allow\" } | { action: \"block\", reason } | { action: \"ask\", title }.\nexport function decide(event, env) {\n  const tool = event.toolName;\n  const input = event.input;\n  if (tool === \"bash\") {\n    const command = input && input.command;\n    if (typeof command !== \"string\") return block(\"a bash call without a command\");\n    // A backslash-newline joins the lines the way the shell reads them.\n    const joined = command.replace(/\\\\\\r?\\n/g, \" \");\n    const hit = DANGEROUS.find((entry) => entry.pattern.test(joined));\n    return hit\n      ? { action: \"ask\", title: `Dangerous command (${hit.id}):\\n\\n  ${command}\\n\\nAllow?` }\n      : { action: \"allow\" };\n  }\n  if (!PATH_TOOLS.includes(tool)) return { action: \"allow\" };\n\n  const root = canonical(resolve(env.cwd));\n  const given = input.path;\n  const required = tool === \"read\" || tool === \"edit\" || tool === \"write\";\n  if (given === undefined && !required) {\n    // grep, find and ls search the working directory when no path is given.\n  } else {\n    const target = canonical(resolveToolPath(given, env.cwd, env.home));\n    if (!isInside(root, target, env.caseInsensitive)) {\n      return block(`${tool} on a path outside the worktree`);\n    }\n    if (WRITE_TOOLS.includes(tool)) {\n      const own = canonical(env.ownFile);\n      const guarded = PROTECTED_DIRS.map((name) => canonical(join(root, name)));\n      if (fold(target, env.caseInsensitive) === fold(own, env.caseInsensitive)) {\n        return block(`${tool} on the policy's own file`);\n      }\n      if (guarded.some((dir) => isInside(dir, target, env.caseInsensitive))) {\n        return block(`${tool} on a protected directory`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (tool === \"find\" && reachesOut(input.pattern)) return block(\"a find pattern that reaches outside the worktree\");\n  if (tool === \"grep\" && reachesOut(input.glob)) return block(\"a grep glob that reaches outside the worktree\");\n  return { action: \"allow\" };\n}\n\n// Bind the checked initial model from one sidecar's text. Exported pure over\n// its inputs, so the handler tests run it without Pi: a sidecar that is not a\n// binding throws, and the runner's preparation refuses before any window opens.\nexport function registerCheckedModel(pi, sidecar) {\n  const bind",

the launch was the runner's own construction, through the wrapper, under the guard\n    (call,) = transport.calls\n    assert call[\"argv\"][0] == str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"the reviewer did not start through the repository wrapper\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--tools\") + 1] == \"read,grep,find,ls\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--model\") + 1] == \"opencode-go/contract-rung\"\n    assert \"NODE_OPTIONS\" in call[\"env\"] and \"pi_network_guard\" in call[\"env\"][\"NODE_OPTIONS\"]\n    assert call[\"env\"][\"OPENCODE_API_KEY\"] == SYNTHETIC_KEY\n",

Each call gets its\n    own scratch directory: a `HOME`, an agent directory whose settings set retries and turn compaction off\n    and the run's refreshed provider definitions, and the prompt file. The key reaches Pi as\n    `OPENCODE_API_KEY` only. Returns the scrubbed answer. A call that has not\n    ended after `REVIEWER_MINUTES` is stopped (criterion 15).\n\n    A free call (`free=True`, ADR 0021 decision 3) gets `--no-tools` instead of\n    the read tools and starts in its scratch directory, not the worktree: its\n    only input is the prompt it is given.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        scratch = Path(tmp)\n        agent = scratch / \"agent\"\n        agent.mkdir()\n        (agent / \"settings.json\").write_text(json.dumps(PI_AGENT_SETTINGS), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        # The launch resolves and assesses its model offline, against the one\n        # address record read fresh from the held declaration. \"\n                \"its destination cannot be assessed and the call does not start.\"\n            )\n        (agent / \"models-store.json\").write_text(json.dumps(store), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        _dropped, notices = activate_overlay(agent, store, policy)\n        retain_address_notices(notices)\n        for notice in notices:\n            print(f\"Address notice: {notice}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        home = scratch / \"home\"\n        home.mkdir()\n        check_overlay(agent, home, model, policy=policy)\n        row = stage2_go.definition_of(store, stage2_go.PROVIDER, model)\n        if row is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"the refreshed definitions of {model} are missing or duplicated;           "excerpt": "def holding_key(key: str) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"One runner per loop record at a time (R-14 of the review-swarm review), by the record's key.\n\n    Two runners that both read `consumed: []` pay the same members and number the same round twice,\n    and the doubled ids then block `repair`. The lock is advisory, held by the open descriptor, and\n    a descriptor dies with its process - so a crashed run leaves no lock behind to break the next.\n    Supersession holds its own and every selected worktree's lock in one deterministic order, so it\n    cannot bypass a normal user of either record (bead coding-harness-e82i, criterion 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    path = record_base() / f\"{key}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"another run holds the loop record `{key}`; one runner at a time\") from error\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "end_line": 11369,
          "excerpt": "def restoration_parent_problem(root: Path, path: Path) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why a recovery must not touch `path`, or None when every existing ancestor stands inside.\n\n    Each existing ancestor between the worktree root and the destination is resolved and compared\n    with the canonical root by path containment, never string prefixes. One whose resolved location\n    falls outside the worktree makes the destination unsafe, including relative or nested links\n    and dangling links to missing external targets. A dangling link to a missing target inside the\n    worktree remains recoverable when its chain can be resolved. An ancestor whose chain cannot\n    be resolved is also unsafe: a resolver that gives up (an error) or\n    one that walks in circles (a link loop, self-linked or paired) leaves containment\n    unestablishable, which is why the ancestor's link chain is walked by hand instead of trusting a\n    resolver's partial answer for a loop. A missing ordinary parent stays recoverable: restoration\n    recreates it from trusted bytes, following nothing. The leaf is not followed merely to decide\n    containment, so detaching a leaf alias or a hard link stays safe.\n    \"\"\"\n    canonical = root.resolve()\n    parent = root\n    for part in path.relative_to(root).parts[:-1]:\n        parent = parent / part\n        try:\n            standing, link = parent.exists(), parent.is_symlink()\n        except OSError:\n            return f\"{parent.relative_to(root).as_posix()} cannot be resolved\"\n        if not link and not standing:\n            continue\n        # The ancestor's link chain is walked by hand with a revisit and hop bound: a resolver's\n        # answer for a loop is partial and can name a place inside the worktree, which would hide\n        # the escape, and a readlink that fails leaves containment as unestablishable as a loop.\n        seen: set[Path] = set()\n        probe = parent\n        while True:\n            try:\n                link = probe.is_symlink()\n            except OSError:\n                return f\"{parent.relative_to(root).as_posix()} cannot be resolved\"\n            if not link:\n                break\n            if probe in seen:\n                return f\"{parent.relative_to(root).as_posix()} cannot be resolved\"\n            if len(seen) >= RESTORATION_PARENT_LINK_LIMIT:\n                return (\n                    f\"{parent.relative_to(root).as_posix()} cannot be resolved \"\n                    f\"(more than {RESTORATION_PARENT_LINK_LIMIT} links)\"\n                )\n            seen.add(probe)\n            try:\n                target = probe.readlink()\n            except OSError:\n                return f\"{parent.relative_to(root).as_posix()} cannot be resolved\"\n            try:\n                # Resolve the containing directory before interpreting a relative target's `..`:\n                # its lexical depth can differ from its real depth through an ancestor link.\n                probe = target if target.is_absolute() else probe.parent.resolve() / target\n            except (OSError, RuntimeError):\n                return f\"{parent.relative_to(root).as_posix()} cannot be resolved\"\n        try:\n            resolved = probe.resolve()\n        except (OSError, RuntimeError):\n            return f\"{parent.relative_to(root).as_posix()} cannot be resolved\"\n        if not resolved.is_relative_to(canonical):\n            return f\"{parent.relative_to(root).as_posix()} escapes the worktree\"\n        if not standing and (resolved == parent or resolved in parent.parents):\n            return f\"{parent.relative_to(root).as_posix()} cannot be resolved\"\n    return None\n",

          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 95,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_go_path_reads_the_one_address_record(world, monkeypatch, capsys):\n    \"\"\"Criterion 1: no caller keeps its own Go origin rule or missing-address default.\n\n    Fault: a caller that prepared against one record and dispatched from a\n    private one would send after the record changed, or would run when the\n    record is gone.\n    \"\"\"\n    model = TEST_LADDER[0]\n    harness = Harness(world, monkeypatch)\n    store = go_store(row(model))\n    seat_lines: list[str] = []\n    seat = harness.seat(model, store, seat_lines)\n    calls = [\n        harness.reviewer(model, store),\n        harness.reviewer(model, store, free=True),\n        harness.probe(model, store)[0],\n        seat,\n    ]\n    for call in calls:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        call()\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a family did not dispatch under the admitted record\"\n    # The record alone changes; every family's next launch refuses.\n    edit_entry(world, lambda e: e[\"adresse\"].update({\"host\": \"elsewhere.invalid\"}))\n    for call in calls:\n        capsys.readouterr()\n        with pytest.raises((stage2.Refused, stage2_go.DestinationRefused)) as raised:\n            call()\n        assert \"not the admitted host\" in str(raised.value)\n    # A refused member aborts the swarm: an admission refusal is no answer to replace.\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused) as raised:\n        harness.swarm(model, store)()\n    assert \"not the admitted host\" in str(raised.value)\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a changed record dispatched a further send\"\n    # The record disappears: fail closed, no caller fills a default in.\n    edit_entry(world, lambda e: e.pop(\"adresse\"))\n    for call in calls:\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused) as raised:\n            call()\n        assert \"unusable\" in str(raised.value)\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.Refused) as raised:\n        harness.swarm(model, store)()\n    assert \"unusable\" in str(raised.value)\n    assert len(harness.sent) == len(calls), \"a missing record admitted a launch\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_real_reviewer_tool_contract(project: Path, transport) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 6: a real reviewer-shaped call declares exactly read,grep,find,ls; an undeclared tool cannot execute.\"\"\"\n    standin = StandIn(\n        [\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"read\", \"arguments\": {\"path\": \"sentinel.txt\"}}]},\n            {\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": f\"echo pwned >> {project / 'sentinel.txt'}\"}}]},\n            {\"content\": \"No finding.\"},\n        ]\n    )\n    transport.providers[\"opencode-go\"] = {\"baseUrl\": standin.url}\n    try:\n        answer = stage2.run_reviewer(\n            contract_ctx(project),\n            \"contract-rung\",\n            \"Review the change demo as the appended instructions say.\",\n            SYNTHETIC_KEY,\n        )\n        assert \"No finding.\" in answer, \"the scripted stop never reached the runner\"\n        assert len(standin.requests) == 3, f\"expected the scripted three turns, saw {len(standin.requests)}\"\n        declared = tool_names(standin.requests[0])\n        assert declared == {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, (\n            f\"the model saw {sorted(declared)}, not the four reviewer tools\"\n        )\n        assert SENTINEL_IN in message_text(standin.requests[1]), \"the positive control read never executed\"\n        for exchange in standin.requests:\n            assert tool_names(exchange) <= {\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\"}, \"a foreign tool was declared\"\n        assert (project / \"sentinel.txt\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == SENTINEL_IN + \"\\n\", (\n            \"an undeclared tool changed the sentinel\"\n        )\n    finally:\n        standin.close()\n    # the launch was the runner's own construction, through the wrapper, under the guard\n    (call,) = transport.calls\n    assert call[\"argv\"][0] == str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"the reviewer did not start through the repository wrapper\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--tools\") + 1] == \"read,grep,find,ls\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--model\") + 1] == \"opencode-go/contract-rung\"\n    assert \"NODE_OPTIONS\" in call[\"env\"] and \"pi_network_guard\" in call[\"env\"][\"NODE_OPTIONS\"]\n    assert call[\"env\"][\"OPENCODE_API_KEY\"] == SYNTHETIC_KEY\n",

        {
          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::launch",
          "end_line": 1173,
          "excerpt": "def launch(\n    command: list[str],\n    root: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str],\n    secret: str | list[str] | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n    pass_fds: tuple[int, ...] = (),\n) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:\n    \"\"\"Start a foreign program: empty standard input, the worktree as its directory.\n\n    With a `timeout` the program leads a process group of its own, and a timeout kills the whole\n    group: a hung `make verify` leaves no shell, pytest or worker behind to write into the worktree\n    after the run stopped (O188-4 of the #188 review). The group is registered while it runs, so an\n    interrupted runner kills it too (`kill_live`), and the drain after a kill is bounded by\n    `KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS`: a descendant that left the group is abandoned, not waited for.\n    `pass_fds` hands descriptors — a verification admission's lock — to the child, so ownership\n    outlives this process for exactly as long as the child and its own children run.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        if timeout is None and deadline is None:\n            return subprocess.run(\n                command,\n                cwd=root,\n                env=env,\n                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                capture_output=True,\n                text=True,\n                errors=\"replace\",\n                check=False,\n                pass_fds=pass_fds,\n            )\n        process = None\n        try:\n            with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                    raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted; no program starts\")\n                with defer_launch_signals():\n                    # Admission and waiting for the launch lock use the same round budget.\n                    # Recheck at process creation so a late replacement is never consumed.\n                    if deadline is not None:\n                        left = remaining(deadline)\n                        timeout = left if timeout is None else min(timeout, left)\n                    process = subprocess.Popen(\n                        command,\n                        cwd=root,\n                        env=env,\n                        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,\n                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,\n                        text=True,\n                        errors=\"replace\",\n                        start_new_session=True,\n                        pass_fds=pass_fds,\n                    )\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.add(process.pid)\n            # Cancellation may have arrived while Popen was starting in a worker.\n            if _LAUNCH_STOPPED.is_set():\n                raise NotStarted(\"the runner was interrupted during launch\")\n            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)\n            # A grandchild that kept running after the command exited would outlive an admission\n            # released around this call; the group is ended before returning (review row F6-5).\n            verify_lock.end_lingering_group(process.pid)\n        except BaseException:\n            if process is None:\n                raise\n            # Kill before unregistering and before any Popen cleanup could wait for a live child.\n            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)\n            with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):\n                process.communicate(timeout=KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS)\n            raise\n        finally:\n            if process is not None:\n                for pipe in (process.stdout, process.stderr):\n                    if pipe is not None:\n                        pipe.close()\n                with _LIVE_LOCK:\n                    _LIVE_GROUPS.discard(process.pid)",

          "end_line": 2153,
          "excerpt": "def _valid_until(record: dict) -> tuple[dt.date | None, str]:\n    \"\"\"The record's parsed `valid_until`, or why it is not a usable end date.\n\n    Only a quoted ISO calendar date counts (spec, terms): a missing value, a\n    YAML-native date, a timestamp and a malformed or impossible calendar date\n    are all refused, never repaired or inferred (fail closed).\n    \"\"\"\n    value = record.get(\"valid_until\")\n    if value is None:\n        return None, \"valid_until is missing\"\n    if not isinstance(value, str) or not DATE_ONLY.fullmatch(value) or not _valid_date(value):\n        return None, \"valid_until is not a quoted ISO date YYYY-MM-DD\"\n    return dt.date.fromisoformat(value), \"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def declaration_problem(root: Path, endpoint: str, model: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why the declaration does not clear this endpoint and model for framework content, or None.\n\n    For the `opencode-go` endpoint a model is also refused while its data terms\n    are unread or its declaration records a dated skip (ADR 0021, decision 5):\n    no paid or interactive call runs on unread terms. For a subscription\n    endpoint (`SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS`, the Z.ai plan) a model is refused\n    without a dated, sourced record or after its `valid_until` day (bead\n    coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        data = yaml.safe_load((root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) or {}\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError):\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    found = next((e for e in data.get(\"endpunkte\") or [] if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get(\"name\") == endpoint), None)\n    if found is None:\n        return f\"model-endpoints.yaml declares no endpoint {endpoint}\"\n    excluded = excluded_problem(root, model)\n    if excluded:\n        return excluded\n    if model not in (found.get(\"modelle\") or []):\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} does not list the model {model}\"\n    if endpoint == OPENCODE:\n        problem = terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    elif endpoint in SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS:\n        problem = subscription_terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    allowed = found.get(\"darf_sehen\")\n    # A list, not a string: `\"framework\" in \"not-framework\"` would be true (phase 6 of stage2-session, F-4).\n    if not isinstance(allowed, list) or \"framework\" not in allowed:\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} may not see framework content\"\n    residency = found.get(\"residenz\")\n    if not isinstance(residency, str) or not residency.strip() or residency == \"nicht-erklaert\":\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} states no data residency\"\n    return None\n",

      "body": "Work package 4 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi.       "author_utc": "2026-10-13T15:44:32Z",
      "body": "`stage2.py repair` runs Codex gpt-6.1-sol (workspace-write, effort max), a\nfresh Codex attempt after a failed post-run check, then Sonnet 5.5; a failed or\nempty call and a moved HEAD stop the run; no GLM credential is read.     "3d7eb02b64085d2082b7963997a4ce98a7c6aa2c": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-27T16:24:07Z",
      "body": "The maintainer accepts ADR 0006 on 2026-09-27. The Omnigent M0 pilot is\ndropped; the adoption path starts at M1; parallel sessions run from then\non, every writing session beyond the first in a worktree of its own, at\nmost writing_sessions_per_repository of them (lakeswitch-ai D-59, D-60).\nThe first writing session writes the tracker; a worker session claims its\nown bead and adds its handover comment, nothing more, as D-60 has it. The\nworker claim waits until the maintainer rewrites AGENTS.md house rule 4.\nThe D-60 write guard takes the place of ADR 0005's Omnigent session\npolicy; it does not exist yet, so until it does, the bounds are stated,\nnot enforced.\n\nADR 0001 is superseded; ADR 0002 and ADR 0005 are superseded in part.\nEach records it in its header. The target document carries a notice at\nits top, in the D-3 and D-7 rows and in its tracker section; its other M0\npassages stay as the record of the earlier design.\n\nOwed item Coding Harness 3 of the lakeswitch-ai decision record.\n\nPrepared by a Claude Code session (the ADR, these notes, this message);\nthe maintainer asked for the acceptance to be prepared as a draft, and an\nagent review in a fresh context read it before signing. The explain-back\nand this commit are the maintainer's, signed with the Touch-ID key.\n\nExplain-back:\nhe owed decision record lands as one signed bundle per repository — coding-harness and lakeswitch-ai — putting the ratified decisions into the files they name.\nhe decisions are ratified and in force; only their promotion is owed, and bundling keeps it reviewable as single signed acts under gate M-30.\nThe bundle edits the very files the guard and gates read, so a wrong entry hits the enforcement layer itself — hence one Bead per item,\n\nPrepared-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "3d7eb02b64085d2082b7963997a4ce98a7c6aa2c",

    "821c248d484c4802053a5837203fecacc1252e4a": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-14T00:02:33Z",
      "body": "Orchestrator hand implementation after three rejected runner attempts (two\npost-run checks red, the third model call ended with exit 1), approved by\nthe maintainer on 2026-11-13. Second step on top of e2c8657d.\n\nCode:\n- stage2: a gate command without shell syntax starts as its own argument\n  vector (the world's `make verify`, the docs subset's `bash\n  scripts/verify_all.sh --job docs`); anything else runs through `bash -c`.\n  Each gate gets timeout=VERIFY_SECONDS cut to the shared deadline. A gate\n  program found only through a PATH entry inside the worktree is resolved\n  without it (O188-2, as `make verify` was); the cheap checks keep the\n  verify environment (state root, memory floor) outside the admission.\n- verify_run: `admission_command` names the check in the holder record\n  (Stage 2 passes `make verify` or the docs vector); the hard-coded cache\n  directory names are gone (decisions Q-5: no tool or path outside the one\n  gate list) — git's ignore rules leave the caches out.\n- kit manifest: the new scheduler's reason in English.\n- docs/WORKFLOW.md: an unmeasurable or changing tree refuses the run.\n- plan.md: criterion ledger entries no longer \"not yet written\".\n\nExisting tests changed because the spec changes the behaviour they pin\n(criteria 9 and 10: the scheduler frames every gate, Stage 2 takes no\nwhole-run admission, the docs subset is a seconds member of the verify job):\n- the repair-prompt frame tests: the gate that blocked is proved with three\n  gates the scheduler frames itself; the noisy run is bounded by the\n  per-gate window; the tail fallback is proved on verify_evidence_text; the\n  frame guard reads verify_run.py.\n- the call-sequence and review call-count tests count the docs gate the\n  full check now runs; the draft's document check carries no admission\n  marker; ruff's environment equals the gate's minus the scheduler's own\n  additions; the refused-docs case rebases its commit count after the\n  test's own commit.\n- the attempt's new budget/timeout tests: the queue-wait spy measures at\n  admission entry (the wait happens there), and the outside-timeout proof\n  holds the queue 2.5 s so a charged wait would still exceed the limit.\n- every new test names its planted fault in its docstring.\n\nChecked: ruff check/format clean; tests/test_stage2.py 1841 passed,\n1 skipped (335 s); the direct test files plus tests/test_ci.py 284 passed,\n2 skipped; kit probe --strict exit 0 (1391 of 1435 cases carry);\nci_gates --check-schema and --check-ci green;     "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",

      "touched_mapped_paths": [

    "d225f50d1ef4364395547863788297ef0959eaf3": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-09T13:12:52Z",
      "body": "Work package 3 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi. Pi asks\nfor no approval and has no sandbox, so the runner has to supply the policy: a\nplain ESM extension, scripts/stage2_session_policy.mjs, that the runner will\ncopy into the session's private directory and load explicitly.\n\nIt keeps read, grep, find, ls, edit and write inside the worktree as Pi\nresolves a path (a leading @, ~, file://, symlinks), keeps edit and write off\nits own file, .stage2-sessions/ and .pi/, asks before a dangerous bash command\nand blocks it when no UI can ask, blocks when its own handler fails, and\nregisters a flag that `pi --help` lists, which is how the runner will confirm\nthe load. 200 cases run it through a node driver without Pi and without a\nmodel; 25 planted faults, one rule removed each, all turn a test red. The\nfirst run caught `git -C . push` running unasked; the patterns now allow\nglobal git options before the verb.\n\nThe runner does not use the extension yet (package 4); nothing in\nscripts/stage2_session.py changes.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "d225f50d1ef4364395547863788297ef0959eaf3",
      "subject": "feat(stage2-session): add the policy extension of a Pi session and its tests",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/stage2_session_policy.mjs",
        "tests/test_stage2_session_policy.py"
      ]
    },

    "d83241f4cb6b45ad739910107a41c6ce303335f1": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-26T23:43:28Z",
      "body": "The maintainer dropped the Omnigent M0 pilot on 2026-09-23 and runs\nOmnigent as intended, with native configuration and no Omnigent sandbox.\nADR 0001 rests entirely on that pilot, and ADR 0005 has a layer (an\nOmnigent session policy) and a validation (\"in M0\") that will not exist.\nThis is owed item Coding Harness 3 of the lakeswitch-ai decision record.\n\nOn 2026-09-27 the maintainer chose parallel work from now, within bounds,\nover serial work until M3. ADR 0006 proposes: no pilot, the path starts at\nM1; every writing session beyond the first in a worktree of its own, at\nmost writing_sessions_per_repository of them (lakeswitch-ai D-59, D-60);\nADR 0005's claim rule kept as the one exception to a single tracker\nwriter; the D-60 write guard in place of the Omnigent policy. It states\nthat the guard does not exist yet, so until it is built the bounds are\nstated, not enforced.\n\nThe decision-continuity map now names ADR 0006 for D-3, D-7 and the\ncoordinator permission, so the gate checks that the new ADR speaks for\nthem.\n\nStatus stays \"proposed\"; the maintainer's signed commit accepts it and\nrecords the supersession in ADR 0001, ADR 0005 and the target document.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,

      "body": "Main (bead coding-harness-wb40) moved the research swarm's free selection\ninto the shared `stage2_free.select`, which keeps a drift notice only for an\neligible id. This branch requires every address-admissible candidate's notice\nto reach `address_notices` before any eligibility filter, each model once\n(spec criterion 3).\n\nResolution in `select_research_catalog`: main's shared selection stays the one\nrule (paid admission, declaration exclusion, destination refusal); the branch's\n`collect_notice` still runs for every free candidate before that selection, and\nthe selection's own notices are merged without repeats. `stage2_free.select` is\nunchanged: the review loop takes its notices from `activate_overlay`, which\nalready sees every row before selection, so the research swarm is the only\ncaller that needed the guarantee. Changing the shared module would have changed\nits documented contract for both callers without need.\n\nTests: the branch's two research-catalog calls pass main's new required\n`paid=()` and `exclusion=None`, as main did for the existing calls. A new test\ncovers the case only the merge creates: a `-free` row vetoed as paid-admitted\nby the shared selection keeps its notice, once (it fails without the\npre-filter collection). No test from either side was weakened or removed.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9FFLqLWsj1biQidvPo\n",

      "body": "The ADR prefix is now held, so each ADR needs a header. The owner is framework-architect, the provenance class human-decided\n(the map's only class for ADRs), and the review stays pending: an approval\nname written by an agent is what the signature rule exists against, and the\nbody's Review line remains the record of acceptance.\n\nHeader only: no line of any body changed (13 lines added per file, none\nremoved). The maintainer decided on 2026-09-29 that a header-only edit needs\nno signed commit (decisions.md, item 5, spec.md [DECISION] 1, option 2); it\ndoes not settle whether the signed-decision rule applies to ADR content.\n\nupdated: follows from the stamp in a later commit.\n\nBead coding-harness-qd7.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HRfJHTtj6rvcgudkYjJoP7\n",

          "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_codex(\n    ctx: Context, prompt: str, resume: str | None = None, writable: bool = False, *, verb: str\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"One Codex call, first or resumed, pinned the same way. Returns (answer, thread id).\n\n    A review reads in the CLI's `read-only` sandbox; a draft writes in\n    `workspace-write`, and the runner puts back what lands outside the change\n    folder. No call takes a bypass flag (spec, criterion 1). The reasoning\n    effort is the caller verb's entry of `CODEX_EFFORTS`, passed explicitly on\n    every argv, a resumed call included; that a resumed thread actually runs at\n    that effort inside Codex is not asserted (bead coding-harness-yzk, Q-6).\n    Only the verbs `CODEX_EFFORTS` names (draft, repair, review) may carry a\n    Codex route; any other verb stops with a `KeyError` before the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    _, model, _ = CODEX\n    effort = CODEX_EFFORTS[verb]\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        answer_file = Path(tmp) / \"answer.md\"\n        command = [\"codex\", \"exec\"]\n        if resume:\n            command += [\"resume\", resume]\n        command += [\n            \"--json\",\n            \"-m\",\n            model,\n            \"-c\",\n            f'model_reasoning_effort=\"{effort}\"',\n            \"-c\",\n            f'sandbox_mode=\"{\"workspace-write\" if writable else \"read-only\"}\"',\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"hooks\",\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"memories\",\n            \"-o\",\n            str(answer_file),\n            prompt,\n        ]\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, foreign_env({}))\n        thread = thread_id(done.stdout or \"\")\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\"), answer_file)\n        if thread is None:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, \"no thread.started event\"), answer_file)\n        try:\n            answer = answer_file.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n            raise fail(\"codex\", done, \"no answer file\") from error\n    return answer, thread\n",

          "excerpt": "def producer_for(endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The header's producer names the program: codex, claude-code, pi (spec, criterion 29).\n\n    The GLM endpoints run as Claude Code against Z.ai, so their producer is `claude-code`\n    too; `pi` stays the producer of an endpoint nothing here names.\n    \"\"\"\n    producers = {\"openai-codex\": \"codex\", \"claude-code-plan\": \"claude-code\", \"glm-coding-plan\": \"claude-code\"}\n    return producers.get(endpoint[0], \"pi\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def declaration_problem(root: Path, endpoint: str, model: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why the declaration does not clear this endpoint and model for framework content, or None.\n\n    For the `opencode-go` endpoint a model is also refused while its data terms\n    are unread or its declaration records a dated skip (ADR 0021, decision 5):\n    no paid or interactive call runs on unread terms. For a subscription\n    endpoint (`SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS`, the Z.ai plan) a model is refused\n    without a dated, sourced record or after its `valid_until` day (bead\n    coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        data = yaml.safe_load((root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) or {}\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError):\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    found = next((e for e in data.get(\"endpunkte\") or [] if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get(\"name\") == endpoint), None)\n    if found is None:\n        return f\"model-endpoints.yaml declares no endpoint {endpoint}\"\n    excluded = excluded_problem(root, model)\n    if excluded:\n        return excluded\n    if model not in (found.get(\"modelle\") or []):\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} does not list the model {model}\"\n    if endpoint == OPENCODE:\n        problem = terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    elif endpoint in SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS:\n        problem = subscription_terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    allowed = found.get(\"darf_sehen\")\n    # A list, not a string: `\"framework\" in \"not-framework\"` would be true (phase 6 of stage2-session, F-4).\n    if not isinstance(allowed, list) or \"framework\" not in allowed:\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} may not see framework content\"\n    residency = found.get(\"residenz\")\n    if not isinstance(residency, str) or not residency.strip() or residency == \"nicht-erklaert\":\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} states no data residency\"\n    return None\n",

A model the list does not hold is no id in\n    the code: adding or replacing one is a pull request that touches\n    `model-endpoints.yaml` and nothing else (spec, criterion 5).           "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). The same per-attempt snapshot serves\n    the early exits: a failed call and a retry recover whole snapshotted inputs, a moved HEAD keeps\n    its commit while the safe working-tree fields go back, a refused checkpoint puts the fields back\n    before the run stops, and every attempt's bookkeeping names what was restored or says the fields\n    stayed unchanged (status-fields-restore).           "excerpt": "export const PATH_TOOLS = [\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\", \"edit\", \"write\"];\nexport const WRITE_TOOLS = [\"edit\", \"write\"];\n// Relative to the worktree.
