The first three are the ones of Pi's shipped\n// example `permission-gate.ts` (Q-2); the rest are the maintainer's addition\n// (Q-8 and its 2026-10-09 extension): the git commands that discard unsaved\n// work. The patterns read the text of the command and do not parse the shell:\n// a word split by quotes (`s\"\"udo`) or built by expansion is not recognised. Network programs and\n// `git push` do not ask (Q-7, Q-8). The list is one array: change it here and\n// in its test, and record the decision in plans/changes/stage2-session/.\nexport const DANGEROUS = [\n  {\n    id: \"rm-recursive\",\n    pattern: new RegExp(String.raw`\\brm\\b${ARGS}\\s(-[a-zA-Z]*[rR][a-zA-Z]*|--recursive)\\b`),\n  },\n  { id: \"sudo\", pattern: /\\bsudo\\b/ },\n  { id: \"chmod-777\", pattern: /\\b(chmod|chown)\\b.*777/ },\n  { id: \"git-reset-hard\", pattern: new RegExp(`${GIT}reset\\\\b${ARGS}--hard\\\\b`) },\n  { id: \"git-clean\", pattern: new RegExp(`${GIT}clean\\\\b`) },\n  // Also discarding unsaved edits: `checkout -- <path>`, `checkout .`, `checkout -f`,\n  // `restore` (unless it only unstages).\n  { id: \"git-checkout-discard\", pattern: new RegExp(`${GIT}checkout\\\\b${ARGS}(\\\\s--(\\\\s|$)|\\\\s(-f|--force)\\\\b|\\\\s\\\\.(\\\\s|$))`) },\n  { id: \"git-restore\", pattern: new RegExp(`${GIT}restore\\\\b(?!${ARGS}(--staged|\\\\s-[a-zA-Z]*S)\\\\b)`) },\n  { id: \"git-restore-worktree\", pattern: new RegExp(`${GIT}restore\\\\b${ARGS}(--worktree|\\\\s-[a-zA-Z]*W)\\\\b`) },\n];\n\nconst UNICODE_SPACES = /[  -   　]/g;\nconst THIS_FILE = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);\n\n// A path the way Pi's `resolvePath` reads it (dist/utils/paths.js, Pi 1.1.0 —\n// the original measurement; the real-Pi contract test\n// `test_real_session_policy_blocks_foreign_reads` now holds this against the\n// pinned install too).\nexport function resolveToolPath(input, cwd, home) {\n  if (typeof input !== \"string\" || input.includes(\"\\0\")) {\n    throw new Error(\"the path is not a string, or holds a NUL byte\");\n  }\n  let path = input.replace(UNICODE_SPACES, \" \");\n  if (path.startsWith(\"@\")) path = path.slice(1);\n  if (path === \"~\") path = home;\n  else if (path.startsWith(\"~/\")) path = join(home, path.slice(2));\n  if (/^file:\\/\\//.test(path)) path = fileURLToPath(path);\n  return isAbsolute(path) ?           "excerpt": "def declaration_problem(root: Path, endpoint: str, model: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why the declaration does not clear this endpoint and model for framework content, or None.\n\n    For the `opencode-go` endpoint a model is also refused while its data terms\n    are unread or its declaration records a dated skip (ADR 0021, decision 5):\n    no paid or interactive call runs on unread terms. For a subscription\n    endpoint (`SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS`, the Z.ai plan) a model is refused\n    without a dated, sourced record or after its `valid_until` day (bead\n    coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        data = yaml.safe_load((root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) or {}\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError):\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    found = next((e for e in data.get(\"endpunkte\") or [] if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get(\"name\") == endpoint), None)\n    if found is None:\n        return f\"model-endpoints.yaml declares no endpoint {endpoint}\"\n    excluded = excluded_problem(root, model)\n    if excluded:\n        return excluded\n    if model not in (found.get(\"modelle\") or []):\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} does not list the model {model}\"\n    if endpoint == OPENCODE:\n        problem = terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    elif endpoint in SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS:\n        problem = subscription_terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    allowed = found.get(\"darf_sehen\")\n    # A list, not a string: `\"framework\" in \"not-framework\"` would be true (phase 6 of stage2-session, F-4).\n    if not isinstance(allowed, list) or \"framework\" not in allowed:\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} may not see framework content\"\n    residency = found.get(\"residenz\")\n    if not isinstance(residency, str) or not residency.strip() or residency == \"nicht-erklaert\":\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} states no data residency\"\n    return None\n",

          "excerpt": "def ladder(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The eligible paid models of the `opencode-go` entry, cheapest first: each is one later round.\n\n    The order is the runner's: `anfragen_5h` descending, ties by id, a model\n    without the value last (Q-13). A model the list does not hold is no id in\n    the code: adding or replacing one is a pull request that touches\n    `model-endpoints.yaml` and nothing else (spec, criterion 5). A model whose\n    data terms were not read is not eligible: it is skipped, and the skip is\n    named (ADR 0021, decision 5).\n    \"\"\"\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    models = [str(model) for model in entry.get(\"modelle\") or []]\n    eligible = [model for model in models if paid_problem(root, entry, model) is None]\n    return ordered_models(entry, eligible)\n",

          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\"",

          "end_line": 3269,
          "excerpt": "def run_codex(\n    ctx: Context, prompt: str, resume: str | None = None, writable: bool = False, *, verb: str\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"One Codex call, first or resumed, pinned the same way. Returns (answer, thread id).\n\n    A review reads in the CLI's `read-only` sandbox; a draft writes in\n    `workspace-write`, and the runner puts back what lands outside the change\n    folder. No call takes a bypass flag (spec, criterion 1). The reasoning\n    effort is the caller verb's entry of `CODEX_EFFORTS`, passed explicitly on\n    every argv, a resumed call included; that a resumed thread actually runs at\n    that effort inside Codex is not asserted (bead coding-harness-yzk, Q-6).\n    Only the verbs `CODEX_EFFORTS` names (draft, repair, review) may carry a\n    Codex route; any other verb stops with a `KeyError` before the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    _, model, _ = CODEX\n    effort = CODEX_EFFORTS[verb]\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        answer_file = Path(tmp) / \"answer.md\"\n        command = [\"codex\", \"exec\"]\n        if resume:\n            command += [\"resume\", resume]\n        command += [\n            \"--json\",\n            \"-m\",\n            model,\n            \"-c\",\n            f'model_reasoning_effort=\"{effort}\"',\n            \"-c\",\n            f'sandbox_mode=\"{\"workspace-write\" if writable else \"read-only\"}\"',\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"hooks\",\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"memories\",\n            \"-o\",\n            str(answer_file),\n            prompt,\n        ]\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, foreign_env({}))\n        thread = thread_id(done.stdout or \"\")\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\"), answer_file)\n        if thread is None:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, \"no thread.started event\"), answer_file)\n        try:\n            answer = answer_file.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n            raise fail(\"codex\", done, \"no answer file\") from error\n    return answer, thread\n",

          "end_line": 12991,
          "excerpt": "def repair_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    baseline: str,\n    taken: list[tuple[str, list[str]]],\n    diagnostics: list[str],\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None] = CODEX,\n    inputs: dict[Path, bytes] | None = None,\n    held_rows: list[tuple[str, list[str], list[str]]] | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The implement contract with the repair block: the format, the must-runs, the baseline, the rows.\"\"\"\n    rows = \"\\n\".join(f\"- {row[0]} [{row[1]}, {row[2]}] {row[4]}: {row[5]} — Status: {row[7]}\" for _, row in taken)\n    spec = prompt_input(ctx.folder / \"spec.md\", inputs)\n    plan = prompt_input(ctx.plan, inputs)\n    extra = [\n        REPAIR_FORMAT if endpoint == CODEX else REPAIR_FORMAT_FILE_TOOLS,\n        # A command-capable Codex runs the must-runs itself; the file-tools route delegates the same\n        # checks to the runner. The repair owes its findings' proofs and the written ledger entries;\n        # missing unwritten tests are named without being owed, and no missing id reaches its pytest\n        # list. The references come from the accepted plan's cached snapshot, so a retry rereads\n        # nothing the attempt may have edited (spec, criteria 13, 14 and 16).\n        \"## Must-run checks before handback\\n\\n\"\n        + (MUST_RUN_COMMANDS if endpoint == CODEX else MUST_RUN_DELEGATED_REPAIR)\n        + \"\\n\\nLedger tests:\\n\"\n        + repair_must_run_refs(ctx.root, plan.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        f\"Repair baseline: {baseline}\",\n        f\"## Taken rows\\n\\n{rows}\",\n        f\"## Accepted spec\\n\\n{spec}\",\n        f\"## Accepted plan\\n\\n{plan}\",\n    ]\n    if held_rows:\n        # The model is told the held rows are not its work (spec, criterion 18); the rows stay\n        # readable in the findings record it already receives.\n        ids = \", \".join(row[0] for _, row, _ in held_rows)\n     ",

          "excerpt": "def _check_paid_dispatch(world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Direct sends cannot rely on caller admission, even tool-free probes and research launches.\"\"\"\n    from types import SimpleNamespace\n\n    import stage2_research_run as research\n    from stage2_research_dispatch import Slot\n\n    model = TEST_LADDER[0]\n    set_terms(world, model, valid_until=\"2026-10-31\")\n    day = dt.date(2026, 10, 27)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"terms_today\", lambda: day)\n    sent = []\n\n    def send(*args, **kwargs):\n        sent.append((args, kwargs))\n        return SimpleNamespace(returncode=0, stdout=\"OK\", stderr=\"\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"launch\", send)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(research.subprocess, \"Popen\", send)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(availability, \"_checked_probe\", lambda *_args: None)\n    ctx = stage2.Context(world.root, \"demo\", world.research.parent, \"test-bead\")\n    ctx.models_store = go_store(model)\n    entry = {\"program\": \"pi\", \"model\": model, \"endpoint\": availability.GO, \"role\": \"repository\"}\n\n    def pi_command(_entry, _prompt, scratch):\n        agent = scratch / \"agent\"\n        agent.mkdir()\n        availability.install_measured_models(\n            stage2, agent, go_store(model), model=model, address=availability.go_policy(stage2, world.root)\n        )\n        return [\"synthetic-pi\"], world.root, {\"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": str(agent)}\n\n    run = SimpleNamespace(\n        runner=stage2,\n        root=world.root,\n        entries={\"saved\": entry},\n        scratch={},\n        line=lambda _text: None,\n        pi_command=pi_command,\n        ",

  "counter_evidence": [
    "Objection to rebuilding the write boundary in Python: a working, tested JavaScript confinement for exactly the tools read/grep/find/ls/edit/write already exists (scripts/stage2_session_policy.mjs::decide with its test tests/test_stage2_session_policy.py::test_a_path_outside_the_worktree_is_blocked); the Q-5 decision records 'plain Python with tests' but the packet contains no recorded reason why the JS extension could not be reused, and the JS module's own comment says its list is maintained together with its test.",
    "Counter to 'no writable Pi launch exists': the interactive session verb already runs a writable Pi session inside the worktree under the policy extension (scripts/stage2_session.py::cli_argv builds the writable argv with an extension, offline, no approvals), so the reuse gap is narrower than 'write-capable Pi is new'; what is genuinely new is a non-interactive, runner-checked, work-verb-shaped Pi call with our own tool module.",

          "excerpt": "def declaration_problem(root: Path, endpoint: str, model: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why the declaration does not clear this endpoint and model for framework content, or None.\n\n    For the `opencode-go` endpoint a model is also refused while its data terms\n    are unread or its declaration records a dated skip (ADR 0021, decision 5):\n    no paid or interactive call runs on unread terms. For a subscription\n    endpoint (`SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS`, the Z.ai plan) a model is refused\n    without a dated, sourced record or after its `valid_until` day (bead\n    coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        data = yaml.safe_load((root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) or {}\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError):\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    found = next((e for e in data.get(\"endpunkte\") or [] if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get(\"name\") == endpoint), None)\n    if found is None:\n        return f\"model-endpoints.yaml declares no endpoint {endpoint}\"\n    excluded = excluded_problem(root, model)\n    if excluded:\n        return excluded\n    if model not in (found.get(\"modelle\") or []):\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} does not list the model {model}\"\n    if endpoint == OPENCODE:\n        problem = terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    elif endpoint in SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS:\n        problem = subscription_terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    allowed = found.get(\"darf_sehen\")\n    # A list, not a string: `\"framework\" in \"not-framework\"` would be true (phase 6 of stage2-session, F-4).\n    if not isinstance(allowed, list) or \"framework\" not in allowed:\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} may not see framework content\"\n    residency = found.get(\"residenz\")\n    if not isinstance(residency, str) or not residency.strip() or residency == \"nicht-erklaert\":\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} states no data residency\"\n    return None\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2).           "end_line": 2391,
          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::run_reviewer",
          "end_line": 3442,
          "excerpt": "def run_reviewer(\n    ctx: Context,\n    model: str,\n    prompt: str,\n    key: str,\n    *,\n    free: bool = False,\n    timeout_seconds: int | None = None,\n    task: str | None = None,\n    deadline: float | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One reviewer call through Pi with this run's refreshed OpenCode Go definitions.\n\n    The launch is the measured set (spec, criterion 8), started through the\n    repository wrapper (ADR 0019): the rung's id under the `opencode-go`\n    provider, thinking `max` (Pi clamps it per model), the read-only tools,\n    every discovery switched off, no session, retries off. Each call gets its\n    own scratch directory: a `HOME`, an agent directory whose settings set retries and turn compaction off\n    and the run's refreshed provider definitions, and the prompt file.           "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def load_address_policy(root: Path) -> AddressPolicy:\n    \"\"\"The one address policy, read fresh from the held `model-endpoints.yaml` at call time.\n\n    The document is parsed with the duplicate-rejecting loader: a duplicate\n    key never reaches validation with one of its values silently lost. Any\n    unusable state — an unreadable file, duplicate keys, no or several\n    `opencode-go` entries, a malformed record — raises `RecordUnusable`;\n    no literal default or cached policy stands in for it.\n    \"\"\"\n    path = root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\"\n    try:\n        text = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):\n        raise RecordUnusable(f\"{path.name} cannot be read; the Go address record is unavailable\") from None\n    try:\n        data = yaml.load(text, Loader=_NoDuplicateLoader) or {}\n    except yaml.YAMLError as error:\n        # YAML exceptions include source excerpts and sometimes raw values in\n        # their problem text. Only structural type and numeric location are safe.\n        mark = getattr(error, \"problem_mark\", None)\n        location = f\" at line {mark.line + 1}, column {mark.column + 1}\" if mark is not None else \"\"\n        raise RecordUnusable(f\"{path.name} is not readable YAML: {type(error).__name__}{location}\") from None\n    entries = data.get(\"endpunkte\") if isinstance(data, dict) else None\n    if not isinstance(entries, list):\n        raise RecordUnusable(f\"{path.name} declares no endpoints list; the Go address record is unavailable\")\n    named = [entry for entry in entries if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get(\"name\") == PROVIDER]\n    if len(named) != 1:\n        raise RecordUnusable(\n            f\"{path.name} declares {len(named)} entries named {PROVIDER}; the address record must be unique\"\n        )\n    return _record_problem(named[0].get(\"adresse\"))\n",

          "excerpt": "def read_declaration(root: Path) -> dict | str:\n    \"\"\"The parsed `model-endpoints.yaml`, or the problem text when it cannot be read.\n\n    Every call reads the file's current bytes and decodes them, so an edit at an\n    unchanged size and modification time is still seen. A successful mapping\n    parse is reused for identical contents; every caller, including\n    the first, receives its own deep copy, so one caller's edits never reach\n    another read or thread.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = (root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    key = text\n    with _DECLARATION_CACHE_LOCK:\n        cached = _DECLARATION_CACHE.get(key)\n        if cached is not None:\n            _DECLARATION_CACHE.move_to_end(key)\n    if cached is not None:\n        return copy.deepcopy(cached)\n    try:\n        data = yaml.load(text, Loader=yaml.SafeLoader) or {}\n    except yaml.YAMLError:\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    with _DECLARATION_CACHE_LOCK:\n        _DECLARATION_CACHE[key] = data\n        while len(_DECLARATION_CACHE) > _DECLARATION_CACHE_SIZE:\n            _DECLARATION_CACHE.popitem(last=False)\n    return copy.deepcopy(data)\n",

The key reaches Pi as\n    `OPENCODE_API_KEY` only. Returns the scrubbed answer. A call that has not\n    ended after `REVIEWER_MINUTES` is stopped (criterion 15).\n\n    A free call (`free=True`, ADR 0021 decision 3) gets `--no-tools` instead of\n    the read tools and starts in its scratch directory, not the worktree: its\n    only input is the prompt it is given.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        scratch = Path(tmp)\n        agent = scratch / \"agent\"\n        agent.mkdir()\n        (agent / \"settings.json\").write_text(json.dumps(PI_AGENT_SETTINGS), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        # The launch resolves and assesses its model offline, against the one\n        # address record read fresh from the held declaration. Without the\n        # run's refreshed definitions there is no checked destination, and no\n        # unchecked launch stands in for one (criterion 2).\n        try:\n            policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(ctx.root)\n        except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n        store = getattr(ctx, \"models_store\", None)\n        if store is None:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"no refreshed provider definitions accompany the reviewer call for {model}; \"\n                \"its destination cannot be assessed and the call does not start.\"\n            )\n        (agent / \"models-store.json\").write_text(json.dumps(store), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        _dropped, notices = activate_overlay(agent, store, policy)\n        retain_address_notices(notices)\n        for notice in notices:\n            print(f\"Address notice: {notice}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        home = scratch / \"home\"\n        home.mkdir()\n        check_overlay(agent, home, model, policy=policy)\n        row = stage2_go.definition_of(store, stage2_go.PROVIDER, model)\n        if row is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"the refreshed definitions of {model} are missing or duplicated;           "excerpt": "def repair(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4b and 6: Codex repairs every taken finding in one call, checked and committed by the runner.\n\n    The attempts are Codex, one fresh Codex repair attempt with the first one's diagnostics, and one\n    Sonnet 5.5 stage-1 fallback after two failed post-run checks; a failed call or a leak-check BLOCK\n    stops without a fallback (ADR 0017). The orchestrator decides taken or rejected and re-checks with\n    the loop's next round and `review`, a fresh read-only Codex session; the verb writes no\n    `Broke a test` and starts no review. Every selected row's `Origin` is checked before any call\n    or write, an older block's selected row included (bead coding-harness-3h96). A taken Status that\n    already names a fix in the old hand-written form (`; fixed by`, `; fixed:`, `; repaired by`)\n    refuses before any call.\n\n    A selected row whose `Where` names a path the checkpoint cannot commit is handed to the\n    orchestrator before any model call: the runner reports it with the reason `runner-held path`,\n    appends the dated hand-step listing to findings.md once, and leaves the row's Status and\n    `Broke a test` cells unchanged (bead coding-harness-0zhf). Every row held, the existing\n    checkpoint commits that listing and the run exits 0 with no model call; a mixed batch dispatches\n    only the committable rows, names the held ones in the commit body, and ignores answer lines that\n    mention them.\n    \"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else CODEX\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    record = read_record(change, root)\n    current = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n    resolved = resolve_finding_rows(record, current)\n    taken, waiting = repair_targets(ctx, record, current, resolved=resolved)\n    if waiting:\n        raise Refused(f\"rows are waiting for a decision ({', '.join(waiting)}); decide them first.\")\n    # Both checks share the resolver's current rows. The target check covers older selected\n    # rows too; the shared check retains its scope without re-admitting superseded history.\n    target_refusal = target_origin_refusal(record, current, resolved=resolved)\n    if target_refusal:\n        raise Refused(target_refusal)\n    refusal = origin_refusal(record, current, resolved=resolved)\n    if refusal:\n        raise Refused(refusal)\n    if not taken:\n        raise Refused(\"no row is taken; nothing to repair.\")\n    legacy = [row[0] for _, row in taken if legacy_completed(row[7])]\n    if legacy:\n        # A legacy marker may name a completed fix or merely occur in an unrepaired reason.\n        # Refuse without rewriting and explain both corrections (spec, criterion 7).\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"rows carry a taken status that already names a fix ({', '.join(legacy)}); book the hand repair \"\n            \"by replacing the Status with `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or \"\n            \"`fixed — not a test — <reason>` and setting the loop row's `Broke a test` mark, then run \"\n            \"repair again; if the row is not repaired yet, reword its reason so it names no fix instead \"\n            \"of marking it fixed.\"\n        )\n    # The waiting, origin and legacy refusals above bind every selected row before any row is\n    # classified or handed off (spec, criterion 9).\n    hand = repair_hand_rows(root, change, taken)\n    hand_ids = [row[0] for _, row, _ in hand]\n    handed = set(hand_ids)\n    eligible = [(place, row) for place, row in taken if row[0] not in handed]\n    ids = [row[0] for _, row in eligible]  # the commit subject names only the repaired rows\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n\n    # A row already listed with the same held paths in an earlier block of this findings.md is\n    # reported again ",

          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",

Amends ADR 0021\n  decision 6; supersedes no ADR. Amends no D- or O-number.\n* Review: the maintainer decided on 2026-11-08, in the conversation, that\n  ADR 0021 decision 6 changes together with the runner change that makes a\n  repair pass on a targeted check (pull request #343, bead\n  coding-harness-gxwg), and that the amendment travels in a decision pull\n  request of its own (answer \"Fertig machen + ADR-PR\"), and answered its\n  interview the same day (`plans/changes/adr-repair-check/decisions.md`,\n  Q-1 to Q-5). Decider: maintainer ·\n  prepared by Claude Code. Acceptance is the merge commit; the review header\n  remains pending.\n* Date: 2026-11-08 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nADR 0021 decision 6 ends \"requiring `make verify` green after repair as\ntoday\".           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check\",\nbecause it implements the maintainer's model choice without weakening the\nrepair evidence contract.\n\n1. **Codex repairs all taken findings in one batch** through `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`: loop-record rows, released loop rows\n   and phase-6 findings. Each Codex attempt starts `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort\n   `max` in a fresh session, with the existing `workspace-write` configuration,\n   hooks and memories off, and no added directory, automatic approval or\n   bypass. Repair reads no GLM key and never routes to `glm-coding-plan`.\n2. **Only post-run failures advance the chain:** Codex; a fresh Codex attempt\n   with the first attempt's diagnostics; Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` on\n   Stage 1 with both diagnostics. A model call failure stops; with unchanged\n   HEAD, the existing restoration returns the worktree to baseline. When\n   Codex is unavailable, the orchestrator deliberately starts\n   `--stage2-off <reason>`, which uses Sonnet alone and records why. A\n   declaration refusal or leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.**\n   The orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>`, or\n   takes a finding no test can show as `taken — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Repair keeps those inputs, requests one fixed line per row and a measured\n   time entry, and starts no review. The runner checks each exact prompt,\n   prepares and formats the result, runs `make verify`, checks the time and\n   evidence, writes statuses and makes one clean descendant checkpoint.\n   A Codex call that moves HEAD stops before restoration or a runner commit.\n4. **The existing proof and statuses stand.** A code finding requires a\n   defined test the runner demonstrates red against baseline code; a finding\n   taken as `not a test` is proven by the separate re-check. Fixed rows read\n   `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Failed attempts retain their audit, quoted diagnostics and changed-file\n   evidence, while their model-written statuses are restored. Private loop\n   rows are marked only after the checkpoint; unreleased rows reach the\n   repair in the prompt rather than a worktree file.\n5. **The same model may repair phase-6 findings; a fresh session re-checks.**\n   A phase-6 verdict after an earlier `## Phase 6` block in `findings.md` — a\n   re-check — runs Codex read-only without resuming the repair, a prior\n   verdict or a historical phase-2a session; the first phase-6 review keeps\n   the resume rule of ADR 0016. Loop marks may\n   resume only that new verdict thread after its verdict. This replaces ADR\n   0015's blanket reviewer/repairer separation; it does not give review calls\n   write tools or move any review to another model.\n6. **The loop budget and run count stand.** A fixed row counts as taken;\n   round 3 requires a taken or fixed row in round 2, and the maximum stays\n   three rounds. The orchestrator writes `Broke a test` from the repair\n   evidence before the next round or release. Audit lines and historical GLM\n   counts retain their format. Initial implementation, Explore and draft's\n   GLM fallback retain their models.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it. Until that is built, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3 runs the two phases:\n   Haiku 4.5 explores and Sonnet 5.5 implements. This is an open item of the\n   change, not a claim that it works.\n6. **Endpoints are architecture; the models on them are declaration\n   (amended on 2026-10-30).** Which endpoints framework content may reach\n   stays this ADR's matter (decision 2) and its amendments'. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture. A newly admitted\n   model takes a place in the review loop's ladder only; any other role\n   (explore, implem",

          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Scope of the change\n\nasked: 2026-11-25\nanswer: \"All three parts: (1) fallback — when the normal implement/repair route fails, implement and repair run through Pi on OpenCode Go; (2) model choice — GLM 5.3 Flash or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as a declared parameter of the one route (house rule 9), not a second verb; (3) GLM off Claude Code — GLM 5.3 / 5.3 Flash for explore, implement and loop start through Pi instead of Claude Code.\"\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: what this change delivers.\n  Intention: implement and repair keep running when Claude Code or Z.ai is exhausted (both were on 2026-11-25).\n  Today: GLM 5.3 Flash starts only through Claude Code on Z.ai; DeepSeek through Pi only interactively (session verb).\n  Repository change: scripts/stage2.py routes, model-endpoints.yaml (opencode-go widened to work verbs), tests.\n  Architecture change: the work verbs gain a Pi route on OpenCode Go (new ADR, Q-4).\n\nIn the context of work verbs that stop when Claude Code or Z.ai is exhausted, facing a narrow or a full scope, we decided to build all three parts (fallback, model choice, GLM off Claude Code), to achieve one Pi route for every work verb, accepting a larger architectural change. — 2026-11-25\n\n",

The owner owes five interview answers of the maintainer,\n   whatever its class and its date.\n3. An ADR edit that no change of the work claims is a finding that names the\n   remedy. The gate reads the\n  day through `scripts/adoption.py`, which any other gate can call with its\n  own id (bead coding-harness-wpv); without the record the gate does not\n  measure (exit 3).\n* The gate script, its test, the reader and the reader's test travel as\n  mechanism (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`); the record stays as stock. An\n  instance such as LakeSwitch receives them with its next pinned Coding\n  Harness release (bead coding-harness-dj9).\n\n**What this record does not fix.** The field's name, the record's name and\nform, the reader and the gate's messages are the change's design: they change\nin an ordinary change as long as the five points hold.\n\nThis record amends no D- or O-number.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check\",\nbecause it implements the maintainer's model choice without weakening the\nrepair evidence contract.\n\n1. **Codex repairs all taken findings in one batch** through `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`: loop-record rows, released loop rows\n   and phase-6 findings. Each Codex attempt starts `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort\n   `max` in a fresh session, with the existing `workspace-write` configuration,\n   hooks and memories off, and no added directory, automatic approval or\n   bypass. Repair reads no GLM key and never routes to `glm-coding-plan`.\n2. **Only post-run failures advance the chain:** Codex; a fresh Codex attempt\n   with the first attempt's diagnostics; Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` on\n   Stage 1 with both diagnostics. A model call failure stops; with unchanged\n   HEAD, the existing restoration returns the worktree to baseline. When\n   Codex is unavailable, the orchestrator deliberately starts\n   `--stage2-off <reason>`, which uses Sonnet alone and records why. A\n   declaration refusal or leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.**\n   The orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>`, or\n   takes a finding no test can show as `taken — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Repair keeps those inputs, requests one fixed line per row and a measured\n   time entry, and starts no review. The runner checks each exact prompt,\n   prepares and formats the result, runs `make verify`, checks the time and\n   evidence, writes statuses and makes one clean descendant checkpoint.\n   A Codex call that moves HEAD stops before restoration or a runner commit.\n4. **The existing proof and statuses stand.** A code finding requires a\n   defined test the runner demonstrates red against baseline code; a finding\n   taken as `not a test` is proven by the separate re-check. Fixed rows read\n   `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Failed attempts retain their audit, quoted diagnostics and changed-file\n   evidence, while their model-written statuses are restored. Private loop\n   rows are marked only after the checkpoint; unreleased rows reach the\n   repair in the prompt rather than a worktree file.\n5. **The same model may repair phase-6 findings; a fresh session re-checks.**\n   A phase-6 verdict after an earlier `## Phase 6` block in `findings.md` — a\n   re-check — runs Codex read-only without resuming the repair, a prior\n   verdict or a historical phase-2a session; the first phase-6 review keeps\n   the resume rule of ADR 0016. Loop marks may\n   resume only that new verdict thread after its verdict. This replaces ADR\n   0015's blanket reviewer/repairer separation; it does not give review calls\n   write tools or move any review to another model.\n6. **The loop budget and run count stand.** A fixed row counts as taken;\n   round 3 requires a taken or fixed row in round 2, and the maximum stays\n   three rounds. The orchestrator writes `Broke a test` from the repair\n   evidence before the next round or release. Audit lines and historical GLM\n   counts retain their format. Initial implementation, Explore and draft's\n   GLM fallback retain their models.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **Framework content may also go to `opencode-go`** — at\n   `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, through Pi\n   (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, at the version the runner pins), with\n   the three ids below. Of the stage-2 phases, the review loop (4b) only,\n   with the runner's `probe` that measures its rungs. The\n   sentence of ADR 0007 decision 2 that closes with \"Nothing else goes, and\n   nowhere else\" now closes with Codex, Z.ai's GLM and OpenCode Go; nothing\n   else goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to none of the\n   three. The interactive `session` verb reaches a declared endpoint under\n   its own amendment (bead coding-harness-amp); this declaration is what that\n   verb waits for before it opens its OpenCode path to the three ids.\n2. **The loop's reviewer role moves.** The loop leaves GLM for the ladder;\n   the spec review and the review stay with Codex exactly as ADR 0007 set\n   them (the maintainer, 2026-10-08), and phase 6 keeps resuming the\n   phase-2a session. Codex and GLM remain declared endpoints for what still\n   routes to them — explore and implement stay on GLM 5.3 Flash.\n3. **The ladder is data, not code.** Round *n* of the loop calls\n   `modelle[n-1]` of the `opencode-go` entry (the order at this decision;\n   the yaml is the truth and no doctrine text repeats it): round 1\n   `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, round 2 `mimo-v2.6-flash`, round 3\n   `mimo-v2.6-pro`. Rounds 1 and 2 both run, each still held by an undecided\n   row; round 3 starts only when round 2 wrote at least one row whose status\n   begins `taken`. The loop runs at most three rounds. Reordering the list is\n   a one-line pull request that touches `model-endpoints.yaml` and nothing\n   else.\n4. **The unconfined reads accepted for ADR 0007's reviewers extend to the\n   rungs — measured, not assumed.** A round has `read`, `grep`, `find` and\n   `ls` and nothing that writes or runs a command; but `read` reaches files\n   outside the worktree, and Pi has no switch that confines it. A rung can\n   therefore read what the maintainer's user can read — the secrets file and\n   the customer instance's checkout included — and send it to OpenCode Go.\n   What bounds it is the prompt's request to read nothing outside the\n   worktree and the repository's git directory: a request, not a lock. The\n   leak check scans what this repository presents, not what a rung reads.\n   The maintainer accepted this residual risk for reviewers on 2026-09-30;\n   it reaches the three rungs by this record.\n5. **The key stays in the runner.** It is read from the secrets file at call\n   time, reaches the call only in its environment as `OPENCODE_API_KEY`,\n   never appears in an argument or in a file the runner writes, and an\n   OpenCode Go call carries no other endpoint's key.\n6. **Each round is isolated, and Pi is pinned.** Each call gets a fresh,\n   empty Pi configuration directory whose one file switches Pi's own retries\n   off, a scratch home directory, and the switches that keep extensions, MCP\n   servers, skills, context files, prompt templates, themes, project trust,\n   sessions and every network request but the model call off. The effort is Pi's `max`, which\n   Pi clamps to each model's ceiling — `max` for DeepSeek, `high` for both\n   MiMo rungs: a known limit, not a failure.\n7. **The address is measured before anything builds on it.** Three calls,\n   one per rung, run through the runner and Pi in phase 4 of the change that\n   carries this record — declaration and leak check in front of each, as one\n   special run whose commits are named in the pull request body. After the\n   probe, the change's own review loop runs on the ladder, at most three\n   rounds.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included.           "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::dispatch_go",
          "end_line": 2391,
          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "end_line": 88,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **Interactive foreign sessions start only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py\n   session <change> --model <id>`** in the canonical worktree. A declared\n   framework endpoint and a clean leak check over the exact initial prompt are\n   prerequisites, and the audit records date, model, endpoint, handover source\n   and scan counts. Terminal acceptance is success of the dispatch, not proof\n   that the program started, signed in or answered.\n2. **An `opencode-go/<model>` id selects Pi.** The id names the endpoint, not\n   the launcher; the OpenCode CLI is never called. Pi starts at the pinned\n   version only, with extensions, MCP servers, skills, prompt templates and\n   themes off, and one runner-supplied policy extension\n   (`scripts/stage2_session_policy.mjs`) loaded from a private copy.\n3. **The extension** keeps `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `edit` and `write`\n   inside the worktree as Pi resolves a path, keeps `edit` and `write` off its\n   own file, `.stage2-sessions/` and `.pi/`, asks before a recursive `rm`,\n   `sudo`, `chmod` or `chown` with 777, `git reset --hard`, `git clean`,\n   `git checkout` forms that discard (`--`, `.`, `-f`) and `git restore` (except\n   `--staged` alone), blocks those when no UI can ask, and blocks the call when its own handler fails. Every other `bash`\n   command runs unasked, network programs and `git push` included. `.git/`\n   stays writable.\n4. **The runner confirms the extension loaded** (its flag is listed by a\n   separate `pi --help` run under a scratch home, not by the session process\n   itself) and refuses otherwise. Whether its handlers hold inside a live\n   Pi is held by tests that run the extension without Pi, not read back.\n5. **The session signs in with the maintainer's own `~/.pi/agent`**; the runner\n   reads nothing from it and hands Pi no key.\n6. **Codex sessions** keep workspace-write with on-request approval and do not\n   claim worktree-only reads. This record claims no confinement beyond what\n   each harness provides itself; the runner does not verify Codex's sandbox,\n   and for Pi the extension confines the file tools only, not the shell.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "export const PATH_TOOLS = [\"read\", \"grep\", \"find\", \"ls\", \"edit\", \"write\"];\nexport const WRITE_TOOLS = [\"edit\", \"write\"];\n// Relative to the worktree. The runner's own launch files live under the first.\nexport const PROTECTED_DIRS = [\".stage2-sessions\", \".pi\"];\n// The sidecar beside this copy that carries the checked initial model.\nexport const MODEL_SIDECAR = \"checked-model.json\";\n\n// `git`, then any global options (`-C <dir>`, `-c k=v`, `--no-pager`), then a space: the verb follows.\n// An option value may be quoted and hold a space (`-C \"my dir\"`).\nconst VALUE = String.raw`(?:\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*'|[^-\\s\"']\\S*)`;\nconst GIT = String.raw`\\bgit(?:\\s+-\\S+(?:\\s+${VALUE})?)*\\s+`;\n// The rest of one simple command: a quoted string may hold `;`, `|` or `&`.\nconst ARGS = String.raw`(?:\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*'|[^\\n;|&\"'])*`;\n\n// Dangerous `bash` patterns. The first three are the ones of Pi's shipped\n// example `permission-gate.ts` (Q-2); the rest are the maintainer's addition\n// (Q-8 and its 2026-10-09 extension): the git commands that discard unsaved\n// work. The patterns read the text of the command and do not parse the shell:\n// a word split by quotes (`s\"\"udo`) or built by expansion is not recognised. Network programs and\n// `git push` do not ask (Q-7, Q-8). The list is one array: change it here and\n// in its test, and record the decision in plans/changes/stage2-session/.\nexport const DANGEROUS = [\n  {\n    id: \"rm-recursive\",\n    pattern: new RegExp(String.raw`\\brm\\b${ARGS}\\s(-[a-zA-Z]*[rR][a-zA-Z]*|--recursive)\\b`),\n  },\n  { id: \"sudo\", pattern: /\\bsudo\\b/ },\n  { id: \"chmod-777\", pattern: /\\b(chmod|chown)\\b.*777/ },\n  { id: \"git-reset-hard\", pattern: new RegExp(`${GIT}reset\\\\b${ARGS}--hard\\\\b`) },\n  { id: \"git-clean\", pattern: new RegExp(`${GIT}clean\\\\b`) },\n  // Also discarding unsaved edits: `checkout -- <path>`, `checkout .`, `checkout -f`,\n  // `",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration.           "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "end_line": 2391,
          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",
