          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check\",\nbecause it implements the maintainer's model choice without weakening the\nrepair evidence contract.\n\n1. **Codex repairs all taken findings in one batch** through `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`: loop-record rows, released loop rows\n   and phase-6 findings. Each Codex attempt starts `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort\n   `max` in a fresh session, with the existing `workspace-write` configuration,\n   hooks and memories off, and no added directory, automatic approval or\n   bypass. Repair reads no GLM key and never routes to `glm-coding-plan`.\n2. **Only post-run failures advance the chain:** Codex; a fresh Codex attempt\n   with the first attempt's diagnostics; Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` on\n   Stage 1 with both diagnostics. A model call failure stops; with unchanged\n   HEAD, the existing restoration returns the worktree to baseline. When\n   Codex is unavailable, the orchestrator deliberately starts\n   `--stage2-off <reason>`, which uses Sonnet alone and records why. A\n   declaration refusal or leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.**\n   The orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>`, or\n   takes a finding no test can show as `taken — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Repair keeps those inputs, requests one fixed line per row and a measured\n   time entry, and starts no review. The runner checks each exact prompt,\n   prepares and formats the result, runs `make verify`, checks the time and\n   evidence, writes statuses and makes one clean descendant checkpoint.\n   A Codex call that moves HEAD stops before restoration or a runner commit.\n4. **The existing proof and statuses stand.** A code finding requires a\n   defined test the runner demonstrates red against baseline code; a finding\n   taken as `not a test` is proven by the separate re-check. Fixed rows read\n   `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Failed attempts retain their audit, quoted diagnostics and changed-file\n   evidence, while their model-written statuses are restored. Private loop\n   rows are marked only after the checkpoint; unreleased rows reach the\n   repair in the prompt rather than a worktree file.\n5. **The same model may repair phase-6 findings; a fresh session re-checks.**\n   A phase-6 verdict after an earlier `## Phase 6` block in `findings.md` — a\n   re-check — runs Codex read-only without resuming the repair, a prior\n   verdict or a historical phase-2a session; the first phase-6 review keeps\n   the resume rule of ADR 0016. Loop marks may\n   resume only that new verdict thread after its verdict. This replaces ADR\n   0015's blanket reviewer/repairer separation; it does not give review calls\n   write tools or move any review to another model.\n6. **The loop budget and run count stand.** A fixed row counts as taken;\n   round 3 requires a taken or fixed row in round 2, and the maximum stays\n   three rounds. The orchestrator writes `Broke a test` from the repair\n   evidence before the next round or release. Audit lines and historical GLM\n   counts retain their format. Initial implementation, Explore and draft's\n   GLM fallback retain their models.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def declaration_problem(root: Path, endpoint: str, model: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why the declaration does not clear this endpoint and model for framework content, or None.\n\n    For the `opencode-go` endpoint a model is also refused while its data terms\n    are unread or its declaration records a dated skip (ADR 0021, decision 5):\n    no paid or interactive call runs on unread terms. For a subscription\n    endpoint (`SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS`, the Z.ai plan) a model is refused\n    without a dated, sourced record or after its `valid_until` day (bead\n    coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        data = yaml.safe_load((root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) or {}\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError):\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    found = next((e for e in data.get(\"endpunkte\") or [] if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get(\"name\") == endpoint), None)\n    if found is None:\n        return f\"model-endpoints.yaml declares no endpoint {endpoint}\"\n    excluded = excluded_problem(root, model)\n    if excluded:\n        return excluded\n    if model not in (found.get(\"modelle\") or []):\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} does not list the model {model}\"\n    if endpoint == OPENCODE:\n        problem = terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    elif endpoint in SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS:\n        problem = subscription_terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    allowed = found.get(\"darf_sehen\")\n    # A list, not a string: `\"framework\" in \"not-framework\"` would be true (phase 6 of stage2-session, F-4).\n    if not isinstance(allowed, list) or \"framework\" not in allowed:\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} may not see framework content\"\n    residency = found.get(\"residenz\")\n    if not isinstance(residency, str) or not residency.strip() or residency == \"nicht-erklaert\":\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} states no data residency\"\n    return None\n",

          "end_line": 330,
          "excerpt": "## Package 3 of the Pi plan: the policy extension (2026-10-09)\n\nBuilt and tested; the runner does not use it yet (package 4).\n\n**The [GAP] of the plan is settled by reading.** The extension is plain ESM\nJavaScript in `scripts/stage2_session_policy.mjs`: Pi loads direct TypeScript or\nJavaScript files (`docs/extensions.md` of the pinned Pi 1.1.0), and node ESM\nneeds no build step. It imports only `node:` modules, so the runner can copy it\ninto the session's private directory and the copy runs unchanged. The Python\ntests (`tests/test_stage2_session_policy.py`) run a copy through a node driver\n(`tests/stage2_session_policy_driver.mjs`) with made-up events, without Pi and\nwithout a model, and skip when `node` is not installed.\n\n**What it enforces**, with the Pi facts it rests on (all read, none run in a\nlive Pi): it resolves a tool path the way Pi does (`dist/utils/paths.js`: a\nleading `@` stripped, `~` expanded, `file://` read, relative to `ctx.cwd`),\nfollows symlinks to the deepest existing part so a new file beneath a link\ncannot leave the worktree, and blocks `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `edit`,\n`write` outside it; `grep`, `find` and `ls` without a path search the working\ndirectory. `edit` and `write` are also blocked on its own file,\n`.stage2-sessions/` and `.pi/`; `.git/` is not (Q-3). A `find` pattern or\n`grep` glob that is anchored elsewhere or climbs with `..` is blocked. A `bash`\ncall matching a dangerous pattern asks through `ctx.ui.select`, and is blocked\nwithout a UI (Q-2). Any failure of the handler blocks the call, as Pi's own\nfail-safe does. It registers the flag `--stage2-session-policy`, which\n`pi --help` lists when the file is loaded: that is what package 4's read-back\nlooks for (Q-1).\n\n**The test run caught one defect before any review.** The first pattern for\n`git push` did not know a global option with an argument, so `git -C . push` ran\nunasked. The patterns now allow `-C <dir>`, `-c k=v` and `--no-pager` before the\nverb.\n\n**Planted faults, 2026-10-09:** one rule at a time was removed in the source,\nthe suite run, the source restored. 26 faults: the outside check, the symlink\nresolution, the `@` prefix, `~/` and a bare `~`, the `file://` form, the NUL\ncheck, the own-file and protected-directory rules, case folding, the `find`\npattern and `grep` glob checks, a missing required path, the no-UI block, any\nanswer accepted, a failing handler letting the call through, a `bash` call\nwithout a command, the flag not registered, each of the five dangerous\npatterns, the git prefix that sees a verb behind `-C`, and, after the answers Q-7\nand Q-8, the network and `git push` patterns put back. The first run left two\nalive (a bare `~`, and the NUL check's own message); the tests were\nstrengthened and both then went red. At the end all 26 turn a test red; the\nsuite is 200 cases, green.\n\n**The shell patterns that ask** are the three of Pi's shipped\n`permission-gate.ts` (a recursive `rm`, `sudo`, `chmod`/`chown` with 777, Q-2)\nand, by the maintainer's answer Q-8, `git reset --hard` and `git clean`.\nNetwork programs and `git push` run without a question (Q-7, Q-8; both answers\ndiffer from the recommendation, and `decisions.md` names the cost). The list is\none array, `DANGEROUS`. An earlier draft of this package asked for network\nprograms and `git push` as well, which the maintainer declined in the interview\nof 2026-10-09.\n\n**Named limits.** A tool name the extension does not know (none is enabled with\ndiscovery off) passes. A word inside a command that matches a pattern, such as\n`rm -r` in a quoted argument, asks too: noise, not a hole. Nothing here was run\ninside a live Pi: whether the handler behaves there the way the tests say is\npackage 7, on the Mac.\n\n",

          "end_line": 51,
          "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **Reading:** one paid model's sourced retention/training record under\n  `modelle_terms` in the OpenCode Go endpoint declaration.\n- **Expiry:** `valid_until`, a quoted ISO calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD`, valid\n  through that UTC day; the following UTC day is expired.\n- **Warning window:** zero through seven calendar days before expiry,\n  inclusive; an expired reading is a skip, not an upcoming-expiry warning.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-06-terms-expiry/spec.md",
          "reference": "Terms",
          "start_line": 43,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "plans/changes/archive/2026-11-06-terms-expiry/spec.md::Acceptance criteria",
          "end_line": 104,
          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. If a paid model's reading has no usable `valid_until`, that reading grants\n   no admission.\n   *Refuted by:* a missing, empty, non-string, timestamp, malformed or\n   impossible calendar date admits the model, or the runtime invents a date.\n2. When a reading otherwise meets admission rules, its expiry admits the\n   model through the named UTC day and excludes it from the following day.\n   *Refuted by:* the model is excluded on its expiry day or eligible the\n   next UTC day, including when the local calendar date differs from UTC.\n3. If an effective base is not an unambiguous HTTPS URL on the admitted\n   host `opencode.ai`, with the default port and without credentials, query\n   or fragment, that destination is refused before a model request.\n   *Refuted by:* a foreign host, subdomain, host-suffix trick, userinfo,\n   plain HTTP, non-default port, query, fragment, malformed authority,\n   control character or backslash reaches a model request.\n   *Basis:* decisions.md#Q-2.\n3. When existing non-DeepSeek readings are migrated, every record receives\n   `valid_until` equal to its recorded `gelesen` plus 30 calendar days.\n   *Refuted by:* a record, including an explicitly skipped record, is left\n   undated, receives another deadline, or has its reading date advanced\n   without a new source reading.\n7.           "excerpt": "# Spec — repair-targeted-check\n\nRunner repairs pass targeted post-run checks, followed by full verification\nbefore phase 6 (bead `coding-harness-gxwg` — shorten runner repair cycles).\nResearch: `research.md`. Authority and scope: `decisions.md`, including its\nreasoned interview skip and three draft details.\nThis change is partly implemented: the targeted repair verification and the\nfull check before phase 6 are in the tree (baseline `9eae5d26`, 2026-10-31),\nand the held instructions and workflow text still follow after the accepted\nattempt. The earlier draft's failed check is not implementation evidence.\n\n## Problem\n\n- Every runner repair currently pays for full `make verify`, even for a\n  narrow edit: `run_attempts()` always calls the full `verify_attempt()`.\n  The exploration of 2026-10-31 cites a measured 12–13-minute full check on\n  2026-10-30 and the maintainer's targeted-check rule for hand repairs.\n- The interview extends that rule to runner repairs, while the workflow\n  still says runner repairs retain full verification. Existing cheap checks\n  select tests from edits and the criterion ledger, rather than all linked\n  test files. The touch map reads committed objects and misses new links in\n  uncommitted repairs (`research.md`, exploration and draft gap checks).\n- Phase 6 currently starts without independently enforcing full verification\n  on the current head. Replacing repair verification alone would leave that\n  final safety boundary unenforced (`research.md`, draft gap checks at\n  baseline `9eae5d26`, 2026-10-31).\n\n## Terms\n\n**Touched paths:** the repair's changes against its starting head, including\nindex-only changes, working-tree edits, untracked files and both names of a\nrename; retained edits from earlier attempts remain in scope.\n\n**Linked tests:** test files linked directly to touched paths by the touch\nmap's existing naming/import rules, using working-tree content and baseline\nlinks for removed paths. These are heuristic links, not complete dependency\nanalysis.\n\n**Targeted check:** touched and linked test files, existing accepted-ledger\nand retry test selections, lint and format checks of touched Python files,\nand the existing local gates applicable to the touched file kinds.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When a runner repair has determinable targeted coverage, its post-run\n   verification uses the targeted check instead of full `make verify`.\n   *Refuted by:* a narrow, covered Python repair invoking full verification.\n\n2. When a targeted repair is checked, every surviving touched test file and\n   every surviving linked test file is executed in full from current content.\n   *Refuted by:* an unchanged linked test's failing sibling being omitted,\n   an untracked or index-only touch being missed, a removed path losing its\n   baseline-linked tests, or a retry losing an earlier retained edit.\n\n3. When a repair touches surviving Python files, read-only ruff lint and\n   format checks cover those files after the runner's existing formatting.\n   *Refuted by:* accepting a touched file with a remaining lint or format\n   fault because it was outside the check's targets.\n\n4. When targeted verification runs, it measures the existing locally\n   runnable gates applicable to the touched file kinds with their declared\n   enforcement unchanged.\n   *Refuted by:* omitting the document gates after derived plan/index edits,\n   omitting a changed gate's own check, or treating an unmeasured blocking\n   gate as passing.\n\n5. If a repair touches `prompts/` or its targeted coverage cannot be\n   determined safely, full `make verify` is required for that attempt.\n   *Refuted by:* targeted acceptance of a prompt edit, an unclassified input,\n   an unreadable link inventory or production code with no linked test.\n\n6. When targeted post-run commands execute, they run outside the\n   machine-wide verify admission.\n   *Refuted by:* a targeted command acquiring or claiming inherited ownership\n   of that admission; full fallback and phase-6 checks s",

          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When `python3 scripts/stage2.py session <change> --model <id>` runs in the\n   change's dedicated worktree, it accepts the declared supported model.\n   *Refuted by:* no session parser, or dispatch from the main checkout,\n   detached HEAD or a different root than the validated change.\n2. If the endpoint/model declaration is absent, ambiguous, unreadable or\n   disallows framework content, the command refuses before terminal dispatch.\n   *Refuted by:* an unknown model, unapproved transport, missing residency\n   or malformed declaration reaching the terminal stand-in.\n3. When the handover is supplied, its actual text becomes the first prompt;\n   otherwise the change-local `handover.md` is used.\n   *Refuted by:* an empty/missing/unreadable/nonregular file being accepted,\n   only a pathname being sent, or an unrelated handover silently selected.\n   Prompts over 32 KiB UTF-8 or containing NUL refuse before dispatch; the\n   complete dispatch command is bounded to 64 KiB to fit the launch transport.\n4. If a handover path resolves outside the validated worktree, it is refused.\n   *Refuted by:* traversal or a symlink sending outside-file text to a model.\n5. When dispatch is attempted, the runner checks the change, visible tree,\n   index, history and the exact outgoing prompt with the existing leak check\n   in the same invocation before any terminal or model starts.\n   *Refuted by:* a planted forbidden value in the handover or index reaching\n   the stand-in, or a stale preflight result being reused.\n6. If the leak check cannot measure or finds a match, nothing is dispatched.\n   *Refuted by:* missing denylist or failed scan producing a terminal call\n   or an audit claiming a clean check.\n7. When dispatch succeeds, a findings audit names date, requested model,\n   endpoint, handover source and the measured file/commit/rule counts.\n   *Refuted by:* missing or invented counts, wrong model, lost prior findings\n   or an audit indistinguishable from a completed review verdict.\n8. If dispatch fails after clean preflight, the command returns failure and\n   records a failed dispatch rather than claiming an interactive model ran.\n   *Refuted by:* denied automation or terminal dispatch failure\n   returning success or leaving a success-only audit.\n   A missing CLI/terminal executable is a prerequisite refusal (exit 2).\n   Successful Terminal acceptance is exit 0, not a CLI-start acknowledgment;\n   a subsequent CLI/login/model failure is reported in the new window.\n9. When a supported model is launched, the terminal runs the official CLI\n   interactively with that model and the checked worktree as its directory.\n   *Refuted by:* a non-interactive Pi mode (`--print`, `--mode`),\n   `codex exec`, any `opencode` call, wrong cwd, automatic fallback, or a\n   runner waiting for the interactive session to terminate.\n10. When a terminal command includes paths or handover text, those values\n    remain data rather than executable shell or AppleScript instructions.\n    *Refuted by:* quotes, shell substitutions or newlines in a temporary\n    path/prompt executing an extra command in a launch stand-in test.\n11. When Pi is dispatched, it runs with discovery off (`--no-extensions`,\n    no project-local files) and one runner-supplied policy extension loaded\n    explicitly, with `--offline` and `--no-approve`. The extension (a) blocks\n    `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `edit` and `write` on a path outside the\n    worktree, (b) blocks writes to its own file, to `.stage2-sessions/` and\n    to `.pi/` (Q-3; `.git/` is not blocked), (c) asks before a `bash` call\n    that matches a dangerous pattern and blocks that call when no UI exists\n    (Q-2), and (d) blocks the call when its own handler fails. The runner\n    confirms that the extension *loaded* (Q-1); the handlers' behaviour is\n    held by tests that run without Pi and without a model.\n    *Refuted by:* a path outside the worktree, or a write to a protected\n    path, passing the handler; a listed",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it. Until that is built, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3 runs the two phases:\n   Haiku 4.5 explores and Sonnet 5.5 implements. This is an open item of the\n   change, not a claim that it works.\n6. **Endpoints are architecture; the models on them are declaration\n   (amended on 2026-10-30).** Which endpoints framework content may reach\n   stays this ADR's matter (decision 2) and its amendments'. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30.           "end_line": 36,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Scope of the change\n\nasked: 2026-11-25\nanswer: \"All three parts: (1) fallback — when the normal implement/repair route fails, implement and repair run through Pi on OpenCode Go; (2) model choice — GLM 5.3 Flash or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as a declared parameter of the one route (house rule 9), not a second verb; (3) GLM off Claude Code — GLM 5.3 / 5.3 Flash for explore, implement and loop start through Pi instead of Claude Code.\"\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: what this change delivers.\n  Intention: implement and repair keep running when Claude Code or Z.ai is exhausted (both were on 2026-11-25).\n  Today: GLM 5.3 Flash starts only through Claude Code on Z.ai; DeepSeek through Pi only interactively (session verb).\n  Repository change: scripts/stage2.py routes, model-endpoints.yaml (opencode-go widened to work verbs), tests.\n  Architecture change: the work verbs gain a Pi route on OpenCode Go (new ADR, Q-4).\n\nIn the context of work verbs that stop when Claude Code or Z.ai is exhausted, facing a narrow or a full scope, we decided to build all three parts (fallback, model choice, GLM off Claude Code), to achieve one Pi route for every work verb, accepting a larger architectural change. — 2026-11-25\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Scope of the change\n\nasked: 2026-11-25\nanswer: \"All three parts: (1) fallback — when the normal implement/repair route fails, implement and repair run through Pi on OpenCode Go; (2) model choice — GLM 5.3 Flash or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as a declared parameter of the one route (house rule 9), not a second verb; (3) GLM off Claude Code — GLM 5.3 / 5.3 Flash for explore, implement and loop start through Pi instead of Claude Code.\"\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: what this change delivers.\n  Intention: implement and repair keep running when Claude Code or Z.ai is exhausted (both were on 2026-11-25).\n  Today: GLM 5.3 Flash starts only through Claude Code on Z.ai; DeepSeek through Pi only interactively (session verb).\n  Repository change: scripts/stage2.py routes, model-endpoints.yaml (opencode-go widened to work verbs), tests.\n  Architecture change: the work verbs gain a Pi route on OpenCode Go (new ADR, Q-4).\n\nIn the context of work verbs that stop when Claude Code or Z.ai is exhausted, facing a narrow or a full scope, we decided to build all three parts (fallback, model choice, GLM off Claude Code), to achieve one Pi route for every work verb, accepting a larger architectural change. — 2026-11-25\n\n",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0015-glm-5-3-repairs-taken-findings.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 136,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"GLM 5.3 through a runner verb `repair`\", because it takes the\nrepairs off Claude's budget behind the guards every other GLM call passes,\nwhile the reviewers stay read-only.\n\n1. **The repair of taken findings runs on GLM 5.3** — `glm-5.3` on\n   `glm-coding-plan`, through Claude Code, started only by `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`. One call takes every loop row and every\n   phase-6 finding whose Status begins `taken`. The attempts are GLM 5.3, one\n   GLM 5.3 repair attempt that carries the first one's diagnostics, and one\n   Sonnet 5.5 stage-1 fallback; `--stage2-off [REASON]` runs Sonnet 5.5 alone\n   and records why; a leak-check BLOCK stops without a fallback. The guards of\n   `implement` hold: the declaration and the leak check before each attempt,\n   file tools without a command tool, the credential clean-up, `make verify`\n   run by the runner, a measured line in the time log, one checkpoint commit.\n   This amends ADR 0011's decision 2, whose last sentence names what still\n   routes to GLM: the repair joins explore and implement there, on GLM 5.3.\n2. **A reviewer never repairs its own findings.** The rungs and Codex keep\n   their read-only tools; the repair is a separate call by a model no review\n   phase routes to. A change that routes a review phase to `glm-coding-plan`\n   again has to say who repairs that phase's findings.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.** The\n   orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>` into a\n   phase-6 finding as into a loop row, and `taken — not a test — <reason>` for\n   a finding no test can show. The verb repairs only the taken rows and ends\n   with its checkpoint commit; the orchestrator then re-checks with the loop's\n   next round and with `review`.\n4. **A repaired row reads `fixed`.** Its Status becomes `fixed —\n   tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`, the forms of\n   ADR 0013's criterion ledger. A finding on code is fixed only with a test\n   that the runner ran against the baseline's code and saw fail; a finding on\n   text is proven by the re-check.\n5. **A fixed row counts as a taken one.** Round 3 starts when round 2 wrote a\n   row whose Status begins `taken` or `fixed`, which amends ADR 0011's\n   decision 3; the stage-2 run count counts a fixed loop row as take",

          "excerpt": "def test_the_repository_seat_launch_loads_only_the_path_lock(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run.pi_command keeps --no-extensions and adds the one explicit -e of the lock, copied to a scratch path.\"\"\"\n    import sys\n    from types import SimpleNamespace\n\n    sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent / \"scripts\"))\n    import json\n\n    import stage2\n    from stage2_research_run import Run\n\n    # The launch reads the one Go address record of its root (go-access-point); JSON is YAML.\n    record = {\n        \"host\": \"opencode.ai\",\n        \"apis\": {\n            \"openai-completions\": {\n                \"basis\": \"https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1\",\n                \"quelle\": \"a synthetic test record\",\n                \"gelesen\": \"2026-10-31\",\n            }\n        },\n    }\n    (tmp_path / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").write_text(\n        json.dumps({\"endpunkte\": [{\"name\": \"opencode-go\", \"adresse\": record}]}), encoding=\"utf-8\"\n    )\n    run = Run.__new__(Run)\n    run.root, run.change, run.key = tmp_path, \"some-change\", \"k\"\n    run.selection = {}\n    run.runner = SimpleNamespace(\n        PI_WRAPPER=Path(\"/pinned/pi\"),\n        PI_TOOLS=stage2.PI_TOOLS,\n        PI_AGENT_SETTINGS=stage2.PI_AGENT_SETTINGS,\n        foreign_env=stage2.foreign_env,\n    )\n    scratch = tmp_path / \"seat\"\n    scratch.mkdir()\n    command, cwd, _env = run.pi_command({\"model\": \"qwen3.8-flash\", \"tools\": \"repository\"}, \"prompt\", scratch)\n    assert cwd == tmp_path\n    assert command.count(\"-e\") == 1 and command.count(\"--no-extensions\") == 1\n    assert command.index(\"--no-extensions\") < command.index(\"-e\")\n    loaded = Path(command[command.index(\"-e\") + 1])\n    assert loaded.parent == scratch and loaded.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == EXTENSION.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert command[command.index(\"--tools\") + 1] == \"read,grep,find,ls\"\n",

the launch was the runner's own construction, through the wrapper, under the guard\n    (call,) = transport.calls\n    assert call[\"argv\"][0] == str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"the reviewer did not start through the repository wrapper\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--tools\") + 1] == \"read,grep,find,ls\"\n    assert call[\"argv\"][call[\"argv\"].index(\"--model\") + 1] == \"opencode-go/contract-rung\"\n    assert \"NODE_OPTIONS\" in call[\"env\"] and \"pi_network_guard\" in call[\"env\"][\"NODE_OPTIONS\"]\n    assert call[\"env\"][\"OPENCODE_API_KEY\"] == SYNTHETIC_KEY\n",

The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 95,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike.           "excerpt": "def declaration_problem(root: Path, endpoint: str, model: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Why the declaration does not clear this endpoint and model for framework content, or None.\n\n    For the `opencode-go` endpoint a model is also refused while its data terms\n    are unread or its declaration records a dated skip (ADR 0021, decision 5):\n    no paid or interactive call runs on unread terms. For a subscription\n    endpoint (`SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS`, the Z.ai plan) a model is refused\n    without a dated, sourced record or after its `valid_until` day (bead\n    coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        data = yaml.safe_load((root / \"model-endpoints.yaml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) or {}\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError):\n        return \"model-endpoints.yaml cannot be read\"\n    found = next((e for e in data.get(\"endpunkte\") or [] if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get(\"name\") == endpoint), None)\n    if found is None:\n        return f\"model-endpoints.yaml declares no endpoint {endpoint}\"\n    excluded = excluded_problem(root, model)\n    if excluded:\n        return excluded\n    if model not in (found.get(\"modelle\") or []):\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} does not list the model {model}\"\n    if endpoint == OPENCODE:\n        problem = terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    elif endpoint in SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_ENDPOINTS:\n        problem = subscription_terms_problem(found, model)\n        if problem:\n            return problem\n    allowed = found.get(\"darf_sehen\")\n    # A list, not a string: `\"framework\" in \"not-framework\"` would be true (phase 6 of stage2-session, F-4).\n    if not isinstance(allowed, list) or \"framework\" not in allowed:\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} may not see framework content\"\n    residency = found.get(\"residenz\")\n    if not isinstance(residency, str) or not residency.strip() or residency == \"nicht-erklaert\":\n        return f\"the endpoint {endpoint} states no data residency\"\n    return None\n",

          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition.           "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::dispatch_go",
          "end_line": 2391,
          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "excerpt": "export function resolveToolPath(input, cwd, home) {\n  if (typeof input !== \"string\" || input.includes(\"\\0\")) {\n    throw new Error(\"the path is not a string, or holds a NUL byte\");\n  }\n  let path = input.replace(UNICODE_SPACES, \" \");\n  if (path.startsWith(\"@\")) path = path.slice(1);\n  if (path === \"~\") path = home;\n  else if (path.startsWith(\"~/\")) path = join(home, path.slice(2));\n  if (/^file:\\/\\//.test(path)) path = fileURLToPath(path);\n  return isAbsolute(path) ? resolve(path) : resolve(cwd, path);\n}\n\n// The real path of the deepest part that exists, with the rest appended, so a\n// symlink inside the worktree cannot lead a new file out of it. Any other\n// failure (a loop, no permission) throws, and a throw blocks the call.\nexport function canonical(path) {\n  const tail = [];\n  let head = path;\n  for (;;) {\n    try {\n      const real = realpathSync.native(head);\n      return tail.length ? join(real, ...tail.reverse()) : real;\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error.code !== \"ENOENT\" && error.code !== \"ENOTDIR\") throw error;\n      const parent = dirname(head);\n      if (parent === head) throw error;\n      tail.push(basename(head));\n      head = parent;\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nfunction fold(path, caseInsensitive) {\n  return caseInsensitive ? path.toLowerCase() : path;\n}\n\nexport function caseInsensitiveOn(platform) {\n  return platform === \"darwin\" || platform === \"win32\";\n}\n\nexport function isInside(root, target, caseInsensitive) {\n  const rel = relative(fold(root, caseInsensitive), fold(target, caseInsensitive));\n  return rel === \"\" || (rel !== \"..\" && !rel.startsWith(`..${sep}`) && !isAbsolute(rel));\n}\n\n// A find pattern or grep glob that is anchored elsewhere or climbs out.\nfunction reachesOut(glob) {\n  if (typeof glob !== \"string\") return false;\n  const text = glob.replace(UNICODE_SPACES, \" \");\n  return /^[/~@]/.test(text) || /^file:/.test(text) || text.split(/[\\\\/]/).includes(\"..\");\n}\n\nfunction block(reason) {\n  return { action: \"block\", reason: `stage2 session policy: ${reason}` };\n}\n\n// The decision for one tool call. Pure apart from reading the file system:\n// `env` is { cwd, home, ownFile, caseInsensitive }. Returns\n// { action: \"allow\" } | { action: \"block\", reason } | { action: \"ask\", title }.\nexport function decide(event, env) {\n  const tool = event.toolName;\n  const input = event.input;\n  if (tool === \"bash\") {\n    const command = input && input.command;\n    if (typeof command !== \"string\") return block(\"a bash call without a command\");\n    // A backslash-newline joins the lines the way the shell reads them.\n    const joined = command.replace(/\\\\\\r?\\n/g, \" \");\n    const hit = DANGEROUS.find((entry) => entry.pattern.test(joined));\n    return hit\n      ? { action: \"ask\", title: `Dangerous command (${hit.id}):\\n\\n  ${command}\\n\\nAllow?` }\n      : { action: \"allow\" };\n  }\n  if (!PATH_TOOLS.includes(tool)) return { action: \"allow\" };\n\n  const root = canonical(resolve(env.cwd));\n  const given = input.path;\n  const required = tool === \"read\" || tool === \"edit\" || tool === \"write\";\n  if (given === undefined && !required) {\n    // grep, find and ls search the working directory when no path is given.\n  } else {\n    const target = canonical(resolveToolPath(given, env.cwd, env.home));\n    if (!isInside(root, target, env.caseInsensitive)) {\n      return block(`${tool} on a path outside the worktree`);\n    }\n    if (WRITE_TOOLS.includes(tool)) {\n      const own = canonical(env.ownFile);\n      const guarded = PROTECTED_DIRS.map((name) => canonical(join(root, name)));\n      if (fold(target, env.caseInsensitive) === fold(own, env.caseInsensitive)) {\n        return block(`${tool} on the policy's own file`);\n      }\n      if (guarded.some((dir) => isInside(dir, target, env.caseInsensitive))) {\n        return block(`${tool} on a protected directory`);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (tool === \"find\" && reachesOut(input.pattern)) return block(\"a find pattern that reaches outside the worktree\");\n  if (tool === \"grep\" && reachesOut(input.glob)) return block(",

          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses.           "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

      "The Python write tools must reproduce or replace the JavaScript policy's path rules on three platforms: symlinks resolved through the deepest existing parent, case folding on darwin and win32, and protected directories (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/1/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C4, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/8/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C3, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6).",

Otherwise a new Go work family escapes the terms and address proofs (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/7/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/7/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C4, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/8/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C4).",
      "If OpenCode Go is a provider Pi already includes, Pi's own guidance favours the /login and /model flow over custom configuration (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C5)."
    ],
    "architecture_comparison": "The documented architecture and the code agree on today's routes. House rule 9 requires one entry point with variants as declared parameters, and the runner is the only way a foreign model starts (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C6, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2). The change fits the existing single choke points for admission and sending, dispatch_go and declaration_problem in preflight (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C7, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5). It crosses several documented boundaries. ADR 0007 decisions 2 and 6 and ADR 0011 decision 1 limit opencode-go to the review loop and require a decision for any other role, and ADR 0017 decision 6 keeps implement and explore on their models (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/3/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5). The opencode-go remark names no work verb (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4). The only confinement for a writable Pi run is the JavaScript session extension, which allows a shell (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1). The attempt loop branches on endpoint == CODEX in more than one place; how many is contested (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2 against 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/1/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C2). Work calls run untimed (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3). Responsibility is split: WORKFLOW travels to instances as kit mechanism, scripts/ stays in this repository, and the target architecture points toward a per-instance routing file (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7). The supersession bookkeeping lists ADR 0015, already superseded, but not ADR 0017, 0020 or 0016 (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C6).",
    "assumptions": [
      "Q-3 assumes GLM 5.3 Flash has no end date on OpenCode Go. The recorded reading expires 2026-12-14, so a fallback without a gap rests on renewing a second dated reading (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/1/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C5, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3).",
      "Whether an automatic switch from DeepSeek to GLM is compatible with terms-expiry is a matter of interpretation. One reading sets it against that change's provider-substitution non-goal and its per-call refusal. The other treats it as a routing parameter that never extends a terms reading (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C5, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C3, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/8/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C3).",
      "That a Pi work call can be modelled on run_reviewer, with only the tool set and the store provisioning changed, is a design reading, not a measured result (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/1/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C3, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5).",
      "Part of what seats say about declaration_problem, dispatch_go, endpoint_entry and ladder rests on finder descriptions, not on full reads of the function bodies (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/1/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C6, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/4/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C7).",
      "That gateways document routing as a reliability and failover feature rather than a cost-optimisation one is a judgement drawn from page titles alone (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:mimo-v2.6-flash/C3, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/10/opencode-go:mimo-v2.6-flash/C4).",
      "That CVE-2025-53773 sits at the execution and tool layer is inferred from its title alone (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/11/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3).",
      "The script-only NVD and cve.org responses are taken to be client-side rendering, not evidence that the records are missing (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/11/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C4, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/11/opencode-go:mimo-v2.6-flash/C6).",
      "That red-first tests for the Python path checks can be written against a module that does not yet exist is a judgement; no such test was run (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/7/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C7)."
    ],

    "neighbour_comparison": "Five neighbour specs were given: go-access-point, terms-expiry, repair-targeted-check, finder-partial-report and stage2-session. go-access-point (done) binds every Go launch to one address record, but its definition of a Go launch does not name a work-verb Pi run (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C2, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C1). terms-expiry (done) requires a dated valid_until on every paid reading, the reading date plus 30 days when the provider names none, and a refusal at each call. That conflicts with Q-3's premise that GLM has no end date (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3). Seats differ on whether the automatic fallback also clashes with terms-expiry's provider-substitution non-goal (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C5 against 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C3). repair-targeted-check (done) fixes the verification scope of repairs and shares held instruction files with this change (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C6). stage2-session (draft, partly implemented) holds the JavaScript policy extension, whose boundary permits a shell where Q-5 decides Python tools and no shell; one seat labels the relation a contradiction, two call it related (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C6, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C7). finder-partial-report covers finder locator validation only and not the timed-out topics this change's research rests on (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/5/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C2). The neighbours' design, plan and research files were mostly not read.",
    "practice_comparison": "Evidence on outside practice is thin. Every online seat's search timed out, so sources were reached by guessed URLs and mostly only titles or metadata were readable. OpenRouter ('Model Fallbacks - Automatic Failover Between Models', 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1) and LiteLLM ('Routing & Reliability', 'Fallbacks (Provider Failover)', 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/10/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4) present multi-model fallback as a reliability feature; that reading rests on titles only (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4). No retrieved page states fallback-order semantics, trigger conditions or cost-based selection (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5). Pi's own documentation recommends providers it already includes, through /login and /model, and custom configuration only when a provider is missing (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C1, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C2). That fits OpenCode Go but says nothing about fallback or write confinement. On confinement, only OWASP's 'Excessive Agency' risk entry and an OpenAI agent approvals and security page were reached, and neither page's body was readable (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/9/opencode-go:mimo-v2.6-flash/C2). The repository's choice in Q-5 (runner-owned path-checked tools, no shell) therefore cannot be compared to a documented external practice from this packet. The one incident record found is a Copilot and Visual Studio remote code execution CVE, which points to failure at the execution layer of coding assistants (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/11/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/11/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3); no advisory on fallback order was found.",
    "supported_facts": [
      "Implement today starts GLM_FLASH (glm-coding-plan, glm-5.3-flash) through Claude Code, then one Flash repair, then Sonnet 5.5.       "Repair today starts Codex (gpt-6.1-terra), then one fresh Codex attempt, then Sonnet 5.5.       "Route orders are literal tuple lists inside each verb.       "run_attempts dispatches by endpoint identity.       "repair_prompt chooses REPAIR_FORMAT or REPAIR_FORMAT_FILE_TOOLS, and the must-run block, by endpoint == CODEX. Any non-Codex repair therefore receives the file-tools, no-command contract.       "run_codex reads its effort from CODEX_EFFORTS, whose only keys are draft, repair and review.       "run_reviewer is the existing pattern for a Pi call on OpenCode Go: scratch HOME and agent directory, refreshed store, overlay check, assess, dispatch_go, --no-extensions, read-only PI_TOOLS or --no-tools, and every secret of the secrets file scrubbed. It refuses without ctx.models_store, which implement, repair and explore never set (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/1/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C3, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/2/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5, 43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/8/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C5).",
      "Every Go send ends in dispatch_go.       "Admission is checked for the first route only, and the credential is read per verb.       "Work-model calls are launched with no timeout, so they lack the process-group kill that reviewer and probe calls get (43fdfb08b4ae42db3dc9b8f89069d7d0/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3).",
